issues.title: Proposal to add support for structured sizes and measurements
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
In Release 9.0 a new [/size](https://schema.org/size) property was published (see issue #2587) to model product sizes as free-form text.

As a follow-up to address the still open items from issue #2587 and in collaboration with @danbri and @mfhepp we are now proposing to also allow a more structured way of specifying product sizes. 

For example, apparel sizes are often expressed as a combination of one or more of the following attributes:
- a size **system**, typically a country, region, or standard identifier (e.g., "eu", "iso 8559").
- a size **group** (e.g., "big and tall", "petite"), typically used together with age group and gender information to identify a fashion department.
- A size **code** (per the size system and size group), for example "3XL" or "32Wx34L".
- one or more manufacturer-defined **measurements** of the product (e.g. for pants: "waist" with a measurement of 32 inches and "inseam" with a measurement of 34 inches).
- one or more (ranges of) **measurement**(s) for the intended consumer (e.g. "waist" between 30 and 32 inches and "inseam" between 33 and 35 inches). 

We propose to add a few new types and properties to model these size-related attributes, building on prior art such as the GS1 Web Vocabulary ([SizeDetails](https://www.gs1.org/voc/SizeDetails)) and the CPI Ontology ([example](http://www.ebusiness-unibw.org/ontologies/cpi/evaluation/jeans.n3), [reference](http://www.ebusiness-unibw.org/ontologies/cpi/ns)). 

We also propose to generalize the concept of a "measurement" since it applies to many types of products (i.e., not just wearables). For example a bicycle has wheel and frame measurements, and a screw has gauge and thread-distance measurements. 

Given the size of the proposal, an external Google Docs [document](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1MbYXG8wRallckDFbqY2NYc8Y83gUGA4ABDHdMclxzQA) is created for review and inline comments.

Adding @mgh128 and @jvandriel based on the discussion in #2587.

We are interested in semantic modelling of digital receipts and logically a receipt is an invoice in which the https://schema.org/paymentStatus is https://schema.org/PaymentComplete (unless the card transaction failed etc., e.g. https://schema.org/PaymentDeclined)

We're currently looking into existing specifications for machine-readable receipts and may be able to contribute a proposal for enhancing schema:Invoice to support itemised receipts.

issues.title: Improve discovery of datacatalogs by registering well-known suffix 'datacatalog'
issues.author: coret
issues.body:
[RFC 5785](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5785) defines a mechanism for reserving 'well-known' URIs on any Web server. By registering the 'datacatalog' suffix and promoting its use, the discovery of datacatalogs can be improved. 

Although this proposal is not **schema.org/DataCatalog** specific (eg. DCAT would also benefit), [we](https://github.com/netwerk-digitaal-erfgoed/) do seek support of the schema.org community for this proposal (as well as the DCAT community, therefor a similar issue has been posted at https://github.com/w3c/dxwg/issues/1290).

We have drafted a text which could be included in a specification document (this is highly inspired by https://www.w3.org/TR/void/#well-known):

> **Discovery with well-known URI**
>
> The [RFC 5785](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5785) defines a mechanism for reserving 'well-known' URIs on any Web server. 
>  
> The URI /.well-known/datacatalog on any Web server is registered by this specification for a datacatalog with dataset descriptions of datasets hosted on that server.  For example, on the host www.example.com, this URI would be http://www.example.com/.well-known/datacatalog.
>  
> This URI may be an HTTP redirect to the location of the actual datacatalog file. The most appropriate HTTP redirect code is 302. Clients accessing this well-known URI MUST handle HTTP redirects.
>  
> The datacatalog file accessible via the well-known URI should contain descriptions of all datasets hosted on the server. This includes any datasets that have resolvable URIs, a SPARQL endpoint, a data dump, or any other access mechanism whose URI is on the server's hostname. Datacatalogs can be described using [http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Catalog](http://www.w3.org/ns/dcat#Catalog) or [https://schema.org/DataCatalog](https://schema.org/DataCatalog).

Broad support for this proposal will help in getting the 'datacatalog' suffix registered. The registration procedure and template from Section 5.1 of [RFC 5785](https://tools.ietf.org/html/rfc5785) requires a change controller and specification document. Can this community assist in this process?

issues.title: Add a structure for "pros" and "conts" to be associated with a review (most typically of a reviewed product)
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
For a Review where the itemReviewed is most typically a Product, it is common for sites to use organized lists of "pros" and "cons" to show summaries the positive and negative aspects. 

This is a proposal from Google to add a structure that makes this kind of data explicit. If adopted by schema.org and publishers we consider it likely that we could improve search experience by making use of such markup.

# Proposal

* add a pair of properties, /positiveNotes and /negativeNotes, applicable on /Review, with /ListItem and /Text values.
* typical usage would be an order-preserving list of short sentences. Let's start with an ItemList of strings. 
* Potentially could be more structured (add a WebContent node, so variants of each pro/con could be represented with different properties. 
* Complex comparisons of characteristics of products could be modeled with a /PropertyValue structure, but that would be more challenging.
* Let's acknowledge that ItemList is not a work of beauty, but it is our current main structure for representing order within the graph.


# Example usage (simplified, showing "PROs" only):

This example skips any description of Product, and any example of /negativeNotes.

```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Review",
  "name": "Megaphone 11 review",
  "description": "blah blah",
  "positiveNotes": 
  {
    "@type": "ItemList",
    "itemListElement": [
    {
      "@type": "ListItem",
      "position": 1,
      "item": "Tougher and water resistant design."
    },
    {
      "@type": "ListItem",
      "position": 2,
      "item": "Cheery bright colours and solid feel."
    },
    {
      "@type": "ListItem",
      "position": 3,
      "item": "Excellent amplification."    
    }
  ]
 }
}
```

issues.title: How to find current version of schema.org programmatically?
issues.author: stain
issues.body:
https://schema.org/docs/developers.html tells developers to download schema.org definition using URLs like 
https://schema.org/version/latest/schemaorg-current-http.jsonld - note `latest`

We saw in #2805 how named versions, replacing `latest` with `11.0` for instance, have temporarily disappeared with 404. 

While I'm sure this will be corrected, the use of `latest` above still raises the question of how software can detect/record which version of schema.org they have used or been built with (or if they should be updated).

Previously we have used the fact that the `.jsonld` file included:
```json
"@id": "http://schema.org/#10.0"
```

<http://schema.org/#10.0> works, but of course that page has no `#10.0` but we were able to string-replace from that to find the version.

Now since 11.0 this `@id` has disappeared from the JSON-LD download, presumably to avoid the definitions being in a named graph? (I'm did look to hard yet to find the corresponding issue)

At the moment https://schema.org/version/latest/schemaorg-current-http.nq still includes such a named graph identifier, however slightly different:

```
<http://schema.org/exifData> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#type> <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#Property> <http://schema.org/11.01> .
```

It should be obvious that it is useful to have a versioned identifier for Schema.org.

Now http://schema.org/11.01 gives 404 (and I think always did), so perhaps, considering #2837 this is not an ideal `schemaVersion` candidate either?

Is it possible to include such a `@id` self-declaring version in the other downloads, or is there a risk this version identifier also disappear from the `.nt` download later?

issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
This is part of #2450 but just for the codelist piece.

From Duke (Nov 2020):

MediaReview Fields and Labels (as of November 2020)
Media Type: VIDEO 

RATINGS
Original: No evidence the footage has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may contain false or misleading claims.
Missing Context: Presenting unaltered video in an inaccurate manner that misrepresents the footage. For example, using incorrect dates or locations, altering the transcript or sharing brief clips from a longer video to mislead viewers. (A video rated “original” can also be missing context.)
Edited: The video has been edited or rearranged. This category applies to time edits, including editing multiple videos together to alter the story being told or editing out large portions from a video.
Transformed: Part or all of the video has been manipulated to transform the footage itself. This category includes using tools like the Adobe Suite to change the speed of the video, add or remove visual elements or dub audio. Deepfakes are also a subset of transformation.
Staged: A video that has been created using actors or similarly contrived.
Satire/Parody: A video that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

OTHER FIELDS
Video URL: Link to the page containing the video, such as an article or social media post
Original Media URL: Link to the original, non-manipulated version of the video (if available)
Original Media Context: A short sentence explaining the original context if media is used out of context
Timestamp of video edit (in HH:MM:SS format)
Ending timestamp of video edit, if applicable (in HH:MM:SS format)
[Fact-checker] Article URL

Media Type: IMAGE

RATINGS
Original: No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.
Missing Context: Presenting unaltered images in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An image rated “original” can also be missing context.)
Cropped: Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.
Transformed: Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.
Staged: An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.
Satire/Parody: An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

OTHER FIELDS
Image URL: Link to the page containing the image, such as an article or social media post
Original Media URL: Link to the original, non-manipulated version of the image (if available)
Original Media Context: A short sentence explaining the original context if media is used out of context
[Fact-checker] Article URL


Media Type: IMAGE WITH OVERLAID/EMBEDDED TEXT 

RATINGS
Original: No evidence the image has been misleadingly altered or manipulated, though it may still contain false or misleading claims.
Missing Context: An unaltered image presented in an inaccurate manner to misrepresent the image and mislead the viewer. For example, a common tactic is using an unaltered image but saying it came from a different time or place. (An “original” image with inaccurate text would generally fall in this category.)
Cropped: Presenting a part of an image from a larger whole to mislead the viewer.
Transformed: Adding or deleting visual elements to give the image a different meaning with the intention to mislead.
Staged: An image that was created using actors or similarly contrived, such as a screenshot of a fake tweet.
Satire/Parody: An image that was created as political or humorous commentary and is presented in that context. (Reshares of satire/parody content that do not include relevant context are more likely to fall under the “missing context” rating.)

issues.title: `URL` should not be subclass of `Text`
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
IMHO this should be removed:
```ttl
schema:URL rdfs:subClassOf schema:Text
```

OWL has a dichotomy between ObjectProperties and DatatypeProperties. 
Schema doesn't have such dichotomy, but in a sense the Schema JSONLD context does:
it declares 71 props to be URLs (`@id`), so they can't carry literal values.

I checked in the ontology, and none of them allow datatype values (#1747): This doesn't find any amongst those 71 props, if no reasoning is employed:
```sparql
  ?p schema:rangeIncludes/rdf:type schema:DataType
```

Many of these props have range `URL`. So if RDFS reasoning is employed, the above subclass declaration will imply that they allow datatype values.

Many OWL ontologies use xsd:AnyURI literal for "free-floating URLs" vs a resource (owl:Thing) for URLs that carry some statements. But there's no such distinction in Schema.

In short: if you even consider `URL` to be a literal, it's a very special kind of literal, so please don't declare it subclass of `Text`.

issues.title: is having ontology URLs in `http` and `https` variants a good idea?
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
- https://schema.org/docs/developers.html "For those preferring to use https based definitions of Schema.org terms, these equivalent definitions are available in the schemaorg-current-https and schemaorg-all-https files. For more information on using http or https based terms see the FAQ for details."
- https://schema.org/docs/faq.html#19 "This is a lengthy way of saying that both 'https://schema.org' and 'http://schema.org' are fine."

I'd like to raise an objection to this practice, although I'm sure it has been discussed at length.

It makes it harder for consumers to process the data. 
If I crawl (or get from WebDataCommons) 50B schema triples and half use http the other half https ontology URLs, I have to either:
- declare equivalentProperties and equivalentClasses, and enable expensive reasoning to handle that
- employ an expensive URL rewrite process before ingesting the data

The schema website redirects eg http://schema.org/Person to https://schema.org/Person. 
Does this extra step cause significant insecurity, inconvenience or inefficiency?

issues.title: Authoritative document issuers
issues.author: davux
issues.body:
## Introduction

It's sometimes useful to describe the fact that a person or an organization has some authority as an issuer for specific kinds of documents. Or course, "authority" is to be understood in general terms of other people's trust, not necessarily in legal or institutional terms. (Recognition of institutions is just one particular trust policy.)

For instance:
- University X is described as a trusted authority for issuing doctor diplomas.
- John Doe is described by his friends as a good authority for claiming that someone knowsAbout art.
- Tech Organization X is seen by some as an authority for issuing Cloud certifications.
- Country/State X is seen by some other countries/states as an authority for delivering valid driving licenses.

## Proposed approach

I'd like to propose something like:
- A new `IssuerScope` class, describing the scope of authority of an entity.
  - That class has a main attribute called `issuerFor` (or similar, like `issuesAbout`, `authoritativeFor`...), of type Thing (be it some CreativeWork, a schema attribute, or even a descriptive text).
  - More attributes can appear to further define a scope, such as a delegation depth (see below).
- Extending Person and Organization with a new `hasIssuingAuthority` attribute (or similar name) of type `IssuerScope`.

## Examples

**Example 1a.** To express an entity's authority to make an affirmation about someone's birth date.
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
    "@type": "IssuerScope",
    "issuerFor": {
      "@id": "http://schema.org/birthDate",
      "@type": "Property"
  }
}
```

**Example 1b.** Same thing, shorter (without `@type` and taking into account `@context`).
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "issuerFor": "birthDate"
}
```

**Example 2.** To express an entity's authority to issue a specific type of VerifiableCredential, namely a UniversityDegreeCredential.
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "issuerFor": {
    "@id": "https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/examples/v1/UniversityDegreeCredential",
    "@type": "Class" // or should it be "https://www.w3.org/2018/credentials/v1/VerifiableCredential"?
  }
}
```

**Example 3.** To express an entity's authority to claim that someone knows about art. I'm not sure how to restrict acceptable values (or whether we want to).
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "issuerFor": {
    "@id": "knowsAbout",
    "@type": "Property",
    acceptableValue: ["Art"] // Not sure how to express this
}
```

**Example 4.** To express an entity's authority to issue Microsoft Azure certifications.
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "issuerFor": "Azure Architect Level 4 Certification" // Text
}
```

**Example 5.** To express that an entity is able to issue invoices.
```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "issuerFor": {
    "@id": "http://schema.org/Invoice",
    "@type": "Class"
  }
}
```

## Delegation

On top of that (and optionally), it should be possible to express delegation of such authority. I'm thinking of a `delegationDepth` attribute in the `IssuerScope` class, representing a number of hops (defaulting to 0, meaning no delegation).

Anyone inheriting a capability by delegation can claim the same `IssuerScope` about another entity, but with a `delegationDepth` that is strictly lower than their own.

**Example 6.** To express an entity's authority to either directly issue Azure Certifications or name authorities to do so (i.e. 1 hop).

```js
"hasIssuingAuthority": {
  "@type": "IssuerScope",
  "issuerFor": "Azure Architect Level 4 Certification"
  "delegationDepth": 1
}
```

## Possible uses

One example of useful applications of such a schema, including the delegation part, is in a Verifiable Credential, as it enables the description of chains of trust – similar to X.509's CA chains but with richer semantics. We're trying it out in the KayTrust project as described in [this WIP document](https://developer.kaytrust.id/Specs/Trusted-Credentials/) along with a proof-of-concept VC implementation, but we don't want to go too far without involving the schemaorg community on the schema level first (regardless from whether it's applied on VCs or anywhere else).

What do you think?

issues.title: Ranges of addressLocality and addressRegion
issues.author: tmciver
issues.body:
The range for both [addressLocality](https://schema.org/addressLocality) and [addressRegion](https://schema.org/addressRegion) is Text.  I wonder if the range should instead be "Text or URL" so that localities and regions can be referenced by their URI's too.

Another thought along these lines is having more specific sub-types of `PostalAddress` like `USPostalAddress`, `UKPostalAddress`, etc.  Then `USPostalAddress` could have `addressCity` and `addressState` whose ranges could be "Text or [City](https://schema.org/City)" and "Text or [State](https://schema.org/State)", respectively.  `UKPostalAddress` could then have appropriate members which should solve the problem described in [this comment](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/75#issuecomment-50509817) of issue #75.

issues.title: Action-based interactionStatistics are implicitly counting only the '/object' entity of an Action; can we count '/agent' too?
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
This is feedback on InteractionStatistic from Google Search, based on our experience actively consuming the current markup from sites (e.g. see [video-related docs](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/data-types/video) ). Google has been investigating ways to make more use of this and encountered this issue.

For example, if this markup was attached to a VideoObject,
 
```"interactionStatistic": {
        "@type": "InteractionCounter",
        "interactionType": { "@type": "http://schema.org/WatchAction" },
        "userInteractionCount": 5647018,
  },
```

... we are counting the number of Watch Actions in which the entity it it attached to (the video) is the '/object' of the Action.

Can we find a model to make this more explicit (in docs and data), and extend it to allow '/agent' statistics to be published this way too? For example AskAction, FollowAction, ReplyAction, ... potentially both numbers are interesting. 

For example if we added these ...:

```
        "userInteractionObjectCount": 5647018,
        "userInteractionAgentCount": 2234
```

where userInteractionObjectCount is an alias, or subproperty, or eventual replacement for, userInteractionCount; and userInteractionAgentCount means the same but counting agents instead of objects. Potentially this could also be extended for other properties of the Agent.

issues.title: For entry level jobs `monthsOfExperience` cannot be explicitly set to 0 according to GSC
issues.author: rogierslag
issues.body:
The documentation on https://schema.org/monthsOfExperience is unclear about the allowed values for the `monthsOfExperience` property. Based on real-life situations, any negative value would not make sense and probably should return an error. However a value of 0 might be valid.

Google Search Console seems to consider it a warning though
![Screenshot 2021-03-29 at 09 37 32](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/2778689/112802394-6af45100-9072-11eb-8881-25bbd58be67b.png)

Schema.org does not explicitly define the value as either _non-negative_ nor _positive_.

I believe that being able to set the value to `0` for entry-level position which do not require any experience does make sense though. It conveys that the value is both known, and set. Omitting the field altogether could cause confusion about the intent for that specific job: it could be entry-level, or the value would be unknown by the publisher.

I'd like to suggest to make the field non-negative, and request Google to update their current implementation. Curious to see what others within the community seem to think!

issues.title: Potential problem with @Dataset/property
issues.author: jaygray0919
issues.body:
`@Dataset/property` has expected type `@DataDownload`

`@DataDownload` is a subClass of `@MediaObject` and has one property: `measurementTechnique`

In order to annotate `@DataDownload` with properties such as `contentUrl` and `encodingFormat`, we must use properties from `@MediaObject`

so we have these triples:
`@Dataset distribution @Datadownload`
`@DataDownload encoding @MediaObject`

However, when we define a *specific, reusable* @MediaObject with target properties (contentUrl and encodingFormat), GSDTT does not accept the @MediaObject properties.

Instead, GSDTT requests that target properties (contentUrl and encodingFormat) be linked directly on `@DataDownload`.

Does schema.org disallow a superClass (e.g. `@MediaObject`) to link with its subClass (`@DataDownload`)?

We don't see any other pattern to define @MediaObject once and then reuse it for an `@Dataset` using the property `distribution`.

issues.title: Write down that Event.endDate is the non-inclusive end
issues.author: dilyanpalauzov
issues.body:
https://ips-bas.org/2021/01/21/покана-за-участие-в-международна-науч/ describes an event “Refugees – Fears, Understanding, Empathy”, which happens on 17th March 2021.  This event is mapped to an iCalendar file: https://aaa.bapha.be/c/4/bfc7c227-834c-4fc1-b23f-1b961ff173f7.ics .  The file contains:
```
BEGIN:VEVENT
SUMMARY:Refugees – Fears\, Understanding\, Empathy
DTSTART;VALUE=DATE:20210517
DTEND;VALUE=DATE:20210518
END:VEVENT
```

Per RFC 5545 DTSTART is the inclusive start and DTEND is the non-inclusive end.  The above event file reflects that the event is on 17th May and not 18h May 2021.

From the iCalendar file another file is generated https://aaa.bapha.be/s/4/bfc7c227-834c-4fc1-b23f-1b961ff173f7.ics_en.html which contains structured data:

```iCalendar
"startDate":"2021-05-17T00:00:00+0300",
"endDate":"2021-05-18T00:00:00+0300",
```

I am currently in Timezone UTC+3.  When I search in Google for the event, G. shows:
![ref-google](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/4992947/116807294-0fb6f200-ab3b-11eb-9672-08752e3f8d24.png)


so it prints as dates 17 and 18th May.

https://schema.org/Event defines the fields:

* endDate - type: Date or DateTime - The end date and time of the item (in ISO 8601 date format).
* startDate - type: Date or DateTIme - The start date and time of the item (in ISO 8601 date format).

Please extend the definition of endDate and startDate, by stating that endDate is the non-inclusive end and and startDate is the inclusive start.

I could in theory map the iCalendar file to "startDate":"2021-05-17", "endDate": "2021-05-18", but this will not help further: it is still unclear, whether "endDate": "2021-05-18",  is the inclusive or non-inclusive end.

issues.title: Proposal to expand support for product return policies
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body: **Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org /[MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy) markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand eCommerce return policies. ### **Introduction** Schema.Org currently supports a limited subset of product return policies through type /[MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy). Certain return policies that are common in the industry are not supported through this type, for example product returns to a different country than the shipping country, restocking fees, and different fees based on item condition (unopened or used). We therefore propose to add a few additional types and properties for a more comprehensive coverage of common return policies in the eCommerce industry. ### **Proposal** We propose to expand schema.org with a few enumeration types and new properties: * Support for more return methods, through a new enumeration /_ReturnMethodEnumeration_, with values such as /_ReturnByMail_, /_ReturnInStore_, and /_ReturnAtKiosk_. * Support for different types of return labels through a new enumeration /_ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration_, with values such as /_ReturnLabelDownloadAndPrint_, /_ReturnLabelInBox,_ /_ReturnLabelCustomerResponsibility_ * Add additional types of return fees to existing enumeration /_ReturnFeesEnumeration_, with common values such as /_ReturnFeesCustomerResponsibility_ and /_FreeReturn_. We will use these new enumerations and values to add a few new properties related to return methods, fees, and labels for use on existing type /[MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy): **Return methods** * /_returnMethod_ of (new) type /_ReturnMethodEnumeration_. This improves on the existing more limited Boolean /[inStoreReturnsOffered](https://schema.org/inStoreReturnsOffered). * /_returnPolicyCountry_ of (existing) type /[Country](https://schema.org/Country) to allow the specification of a country where the return has to be sent to. **Return fees** * /_itemDefectReturnFee_ of type /_ReturnFeeEnumeration_ to specify return fees for defect products. * With corresponding property _/itemDefectReturnShippingFeeAmount_ of type /[MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount), to be provided when /_itemDefectReturnFee_ has value /_ReturnShippingFee_ * /_customerRemorseReturnFee_ of type /_ReturnFeeEnumeration_, to specify return fees for products returned due to customer remorse. * With corresponding property /_customerRemorseReturnShippingFeeAmount_ of type /[MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount), to be provided when _/customerRemorseReturnFee_ has value /_ReturnShippingFee_ * /_restockingFee_ of type /[MonetaryValue](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) to represent a fixed restocking fee, or of type /[Number](https://schema.org/Number) to represent a percentage of the paid product price. * [/itemCondition](https://schema.org/itemCondition) of type [/OfferItemCondition](https://schema.org/OfferItemCondition) to specify the condition of the item accepted for returns, for example /[NewCondition](https://schema.org/NewCondition), [DamagedCondition](https://schema.org/DamagedCondition), or /[UsedCondition](https://schema.org/UsedCondition). **Return labels** * /_itemDefectReturnLabelSource_ of type /_ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration_ to specify how the customer can get a return label for defect items. * /_customerRemorseReturnLabelSource_ of type /_ReturnLabelSourceEnumeration_ to specify how the customer can get a return label for products returned due to customer remorse. ### **Other additions** In addition to the just proposed new properties and types related to return methods, fees, and labels, we have also seen that it is common in the industry to have different return policies during holiday periods. We therefore also propose to allow merchants to specify such seasonal overrides through a new property /_returnPolicySeasonalOverride_ of new type /_MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride_ on type /[MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy) with the following existing properties: * [/returnPolicyCategory](https://schema.org/returnPolicyCategory) * [/merchantReturnDays](https://schema.org/merchantReturnDays), for use when [returnPolicyCategory](https://schema.org/returnPolicyCategory) equals [MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnFiniteReturnWindow). * we propose to add [Date](https://schema.org/Date) and [DateTime](https://schema.org/DateTime) to the range of [/merchantReturnDays](https://schema.org/merchantReturnDays) to allow for fixed latest return dates. * For the existing range of [Integer](https://schema.org/Integer) we propose to change the definition to the number of days from the delivery date (instead of from the purchase date). * [/startDate](https://schema.org/startDate) * [/endDate](https://schema.org/endDate) Finally, to increase flexibility related to return policies we also propose to add property [/additionalProperty](https://schema.org/additionalProperty) to [/MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy) to allow for generic or custom return-policy related fields.

issues.title: Clarify http/https vocabulary differences with JSON-LD
issues.author: stain
issues.body:
https://schema.org/docs/developers.html seems to indicate that developers should prefer `https` version of the vocabulary definitions.

However the [JSON-LD context](https://schema.org/docs/jsonldcontext.json) (even with `@context: https://schema.org/`) maps to the `http` namespace which has been consistent since the beginning of schema.org (I do not suggest changing this!) - try for instance in https://json-ld.org/playground/ 

I think it's good the JSON-LD is consistent for both `@context` examples.

However RDFa examples like https://schema.org/CreativeWork use `vocab="https://schema.org/"` as namespace declaration.

I think `developers.html` should acknowledge this difference so that developers are aware of both variants, and highlight that the JSON-LD context will map to `http`. It depends on where the data comes from which variant developers will want.

Something like:

> For consistency with structured data already deployed with JSON-LD, the `@context` [resolved](https://schema.org/docs/jsonldcontext.json) for both `http://schema.org/` and `https://schema.org/`  will continue to be mapped to terms in the `http` namespace.

BTW: `developers.html` page could also benefit with a link to the JSON-LD context <https://schema.org/docs/jsonldcontext.json> as I struggled to find it!

issues.title: Add typValue and nomValue properties on QuantitativeValue type
issues.author: jaw111
issues.body:
I'm looking at how to represent product descriptions using Schema.org where the products are described using terms from [IEC 61360-4](https://cdd.iec.ch/) - Common Data Dictionary (CDD). IEC CDD uses the data model defined in ISO 13584-42, which is also used by [ECLASS](https://www.eclass.eu/en/).

Properties in IEC CDD can be described as level type, which is equivalent to the [QuantitativeValue](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue) type, where the minimum/typical/nominal/maximum values can be specified. The minimum and maximum values can be represented using the [minValue](https://schema.org/minValue) and [maxValue](https://schema.org/maxValue) properties. Whilst the typical and nominal values could be represented using the [value](https://schema.org/value), there is a semantic difference between a nominal and typical value that may need to be explicitly communicated. Where typical values are generally based on some characterization of devices (i.e. actual measurements done in the lab), whilst nominal values represent some given or assigned value.

In the GoodRelations ontology (from which some terms in Schema.org are derived), the [gr:hasValue](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#hasValue) property is defined to be a rdfs:subPropertyOf [gr:hasMaxValue](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#hasMaxValue) and [gr:hasMinValue](http://purl.org/goodrelations/v1#hasMinValue), whilst there are no explicit statements relating the Schema.org properties to GoodRelations properties, we would definitely want to avoid that any typical or nominal value is inferred to be a minimum and maximum value.

Therefore I would propose to add new properties typValue and nomValue with the same domain and range as the existing minValue and maxValue properties.

issues.title: indicate on a JobPosting whether direct application on the same site is possible
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
Context: This is a proposal from Google, feedback based on experience with building user-facing job search based on schema.org/JobPosting data (see https://developers.google.com/search/docs/data-types/job-posting for current documentation). If adopted by schema.org and publishers, Google expects to explore improvements the job search experience using this additional information.

The proposal is to add a property for JobPosting to help clarify the nature of the posting: /directApply.

Rationale: It is common to encounter JobPosting descriptions in which is it is impossible to tell from the metadata supplied whether there is a straightforward way for applicants to apply on the site where the posting is described (and marked up using schema.org/JobPosting).

Draft definition for /directApply:

 * Applies on JobPosting, values are Boolean.
 * Definition: "Indicates whether an /url that is associated with with /JobPosting enables direct application for the job, via the posting website. A job posting is considered to have directApply of 'True' if an application process for the specified job can be directly initiated via the url(s) given (noting that multiple internet domains might nevertheless be involved at an implementation level). A value of 'False' is appropriate if there is no clear path to applying directly online for the specified job, navigating directly from the JobPosting url(s) supplied."

Editorial comment from Dan Brickley (in schema.org capacity, and noting my Google affiliation):

> I will proceed to add this to schema.org Pending area, where we should take care to solicit review from folk who may not be monitoring Github or other schema discussions. I am satisfied that something like this would be a positive improvement to schema.org's expressivity, but anticipate there may be feedback on the clearest and most appropriate way to express the distinction. As always, Schema.org will review implementation situation (publishers, consumers, definitions) as part of the process for terms progressing beyond Pending status, see [how we work](https://schema.org/docs/howwework.html#pending) for details.

issues.title: Support ISO/IEC 6523 as identifier for /Organization
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
The /Organization type has several identification properties, for example, /duns, /leiCode, /globalLocationNumber, /vatID and /taxID.

Many of these existing identifiers can be expressed using the [ISO/IEC 6523](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523) standard. ISO 6523 codes are composed from an International Code Designator (ICD) value, which identifies the type of the code (e.g., 0060 for DUNS, 0199 for leiCode, or 9910+9920-9957 for European /vatID), and an Organization Identifier (OI) which identifies the organization within that frame of reference.

We therefore propose to add a new property /iso6523 with values of type /Text for use on type /Organization. Alternatively we could introduce a structured type with the 2 fields ICD and OI for values of /iso6523, but since /leiCode allows values of type /Text we propose to do the same for /iso6523 for consistency.

issues.title: Normalize CreativeWork Play
issues.author: WeaverStever
issues.body:
Condensing the discussion on "Persons engaged in TheaterEvents #503'" as a proposal for the next release. 

**Problem**
The pending type (https://schema.org/Play) has no independent properties that you would expect to find for a play: director, actor, productionCompany, musicBy, trailer, beginDate, endDate.

**The following types have similar specific properties that are missing from Play:**
Clip
CreativeWorkSeason
Episode
MovieSeries
RadioSeries
TVSeries

The additional properties are needed so that the person offering the metadata can describe a collection of **past** events (aka a production), for inclusion in a contributing artist's resume or CV without having to supply irrelevant (or unavailable) data associated with a pending Event.

Google Rich Snippets and Wikidata appear to understand the Event (type) to be pending at some future time -- in the context of an opportunity to attend still exists.  In WikiData, a past event would be more accurately described as an occurrence.

**Proposed solution:**

Thing > CreativeWork > Play should be similar to "Thing > CreativeWork > Movie", available as a top-level type and not be required to have TheaterEvent or BroadcastEvent as a parent type (just to be able to include the actor property). 

Additionally, because the singular and the plural for "play" is often the same word, Play should be listed as a "more specific type" of CreativeWorkSeries.  

Inclusion in CreativeWorkSeries for disambiguation between a performance in a production and a collection of performances within a production.  (It is not uncommon for a production of a play to also be described as production(s) when performed or engaged in different locations. I.e. the Boston production of _CATS_)

Specific types for CreativeWorkSeries are currently:

BookSeries
MovieSeries
Periodical
PodcastSeries
RadioSeries
TVSeries
VideoGameSeries

Similar to Periodical, a separate instance of "PlaySeries" would not be required if startDate and endDate are included as specific properties within Play -- so the type covers both the singular and plural understanding of the word.

Related discussion:
**Persons engaged in TheaterEvents #503**

A very similar problem addressed and closed last month  (by adding specific properties to the type).
**Expect existing 'actor' property on existing PodcastSeries #2896**

issues.title: Using schema.org OWL ontology in a medical project - a general question
issues.author: kubajal
issues.body:
Hi,
I'd like to use https://schema.org/docs/schemaorg.owl as an ontology in a medical research study. The study is concerned with _patients_, _diseases_, _drugs_, _symptoms_ and relations between them.
More specifically, I'd like to:
1) map [ICD-10 diseases](https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/ICD10CM) to instances of https://schema.org/MedicalCondition
2) map [ATC codes](https://bioportal.bioontology.org/ontologies/ATC) to instances of https://schema.org/Drug
3) map all data gathered about patients to instances of https://schema.org/Patient
4) serialize the data gathered in the research study using [Turtle RDF syntax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Turtle_(syntax)) and to load it into RDF tools like Apache Jena.

My goal isn't to annotate an HTML webpage with schema.org but rather to use schema.org as an intermediate representation of medical data which will be further processed in tools like Apache Jena.

My questions would be: 
 - is schema.org being practically used in such a way that I described - as an exchange format before loading the data into RDF processing tools?
 - are there better approaches to express information about patients, drugs, diseases etc. using other biomedical ontologies? Ideally, I'm looking for a _single_ ontology, not a hand-made combination of different ontologies to minimize complexity of the solution.

issues.title: Support contributor roles for CreativeWork
issues.author: gjvnq
issues.body:
A simple way to do this would be to have a ```Contributor```  class (to be used in attributes like ```author```, ```contributor``` and ```creator```) with the following properties:

  * ```who```: a ```Person``` or ```Organization```.
  * ```roles```: an array of URIs for the role. Usually one of the following:
    * An UUID for the [Contributor Roles Taxonomy](http://credit.niso.org), e.g.: ```urn:uuid:0c8ca7d4-06ad-4527-9cea-a8801fcb8746``` for supervisor.
    * A [Library of Congress relator](https://id.loc.gov/vocabulary/relators.html), e.g.: ```http://id.loc.gov/vocabulary/relators/tyg``` for typographer
  * ```details```: text description explaining what the contributor did.

A more sphisticated way to handle this is to create a ```Contribution``` class that contains the following attributes:

  * ```who```: a ```Person``` or ```Organization```.
  * ```role```: same as ```role``` of ```Contributor``` but a single value instead of an array.
  * ```part```: URI or text specifying what part of the larger work this contribution applies to (e.g. a specific chapter).
  * ```details```: text description explaining what this contribution is about did.

Crucially, if a person does more than one thing, they have multiple ```Contribution``` instances instead of a single ```Contributor``` one.

issues.title: Microdata and HTML5 semantic markup failures
issues.author: AndySky21
issues.body:
Tested on a [page sample](https://validator.schema.org/#url=http%3A%2F%2Fandysky21.altervista.org%2Fmicrodata.xhtml).
Microdata spec vs. Schema.org Markup Validator interpretation:

- _If the element is a `<time>` element: The value is the element's `datetime` value._
Confirmed
-  _If the element is a `<data>` element: The value is the value of the element's `value` attribute, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise._
Failed: Validator only considers element's text content.
- _If the element is a `<meter>` element: The value is the value of the element's `value` attribute, if it has one, or the empty string otherwise._
Totally failed: `value` attribute is completely ignored and `<meter>` element itself is not recognized as an empty element (validator interprets it as a container even in XHTML serialization and passes its sibling elements' text content as property value).

Microdata spec has been around since 2017 and it is now a standard as part of HTML. It is high time it's implemented in its entirety.

issues.title: Microdata examples incorrect markup
issues.author: AndySky21
issues.body:
https://schema.org/price is just an example.

_Note that both RDFa and Microdata syntax allow the use of a "content=" attribute_

On what planet? Microdata just expects the use of `content` on the only element which natively supports it: the `<meta>` element.
The use of `<span>` element in the Microdata example is totally incorrect. HTML has a completely different way to markup data with a machine-equivalent content: the `<data>` element in conjunction with the `value` attribute. This is the model supported (and suggested) by Microdata spec.
Speaking of new elements, why embedding non-textual numeric content (namely in ratings) with `<meta>` element? There is <meter> for that purpose, it supports articulated value semantics, it's used for Microdata and it's also visually rendered in page.

This scenario deserves updating.

issues.title: DefinedRegion should have a clearer relationship to regional aspects in Offer descriptions, esp. areaServed and eligibleRegion.
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
This is largely housekeeping / integration, following up on the [introduction of DefinedRegion in schema.org v8](https://schema.org/docs/releases.html#g2506) last year. I suggest addressing #2730 at the same time. 

Background:

 * DefinedRegion was added as part of a push for better handling of shipping information.
 * the construct allows a set of postcodes to be grouped together as a named region
 * Offer has 4 properties whose values are places:
    * eligibleRegion and ineligibleRegion
    * areaServed
    * availableAtOrFrom

I suggest adding in DefinedRegion as a possible value type for each of these.

It would also be good to document useful patterns for sites declaring such regions, e.g. how to define several on one page, identify them with URI/URL, so that other pieces of schema markup could make use of them.

Adoption: since DefinedRegion was added to Schema.org, Google have declared support for it in the context of Shipping markup, see https://developers.google.com/search/docs/advanced/structured-data/product

/cc @alex-jansen

issues.title: schema:title, schema:name and schema:jobTitle
issues.author: marco-brandizi
issues.body:
[schema:title](https://schema.org/title) is defined as: "The title of the job", however, 'title' in the URI is a much more generic term and usually, it refers to whatever title an entity might have (book title, film title, `dcterms:title`).  

Moreover, [schema:jobTitle](https://schema.org/title) exists too and [schema:name](https://schema.org/name) seems to be intended as one of name, label (it's defined as subproperty of `rdfs:label`) or title (it's defined as equivalent to `dct:title`). This isn't very good, since often a name is a short name for an entity and not necessarily the same as a title or an ID, eg, the [protein with name: TP53](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P53) might also have the title: 'tumor protein p53' and the ID/accession: ENSG00000141510.  

I would propose to redefine `schema:title` adopting a generic definition, and to separate `schema:name` from dct:title (possibly, from rdfs:label as well).

issues.title: Problems schema:additionalType as subproperty of rdf:type
issues.author: marco-brandizi
issues.body:
I'm copy-pasting the following from a discussion we had in BioSchemas (#BioSchemas/specifications/issues/538):

In my opinion, the fact that `additionalType` extends `rdf:type` can be problematic. In particular,
I have strings that I convert into "sample properties" and then enrich with ontology terms using 
text mining tools (eg, ZOOMA, Bioportal Annotator). The result is something like:

```turtle
ex:prop1234 rdf:type schema:PropertyValue;
  schema:propertyID "Sample Characteristic";
  schema:value "seed size"; # The string it was created from
  schema:additionalType ex:seed, ex:size # computed by text mining, not much under manual control
```

with `additionalType` as subproperty of `rdf:type`, the case above implies a couple of formally wrong statements: one, the property value is an information artifact entity, and not a seed. Two, seed and size are disjoint classes (and declared as such in many actual ontologies).  

This might not be very important if you don't expect to use a formal (OWL) reasoner with your data, yet I don't like to introduce such potential inconsistencies in my data.  

So, my proposal would be to remove this rdf:type inheritance and to have something that is less formally committing in its place (first candidate I can think of is `dc:type`).

issues.title: (adult-oriented product offers and ...) Proposal to expand support for audience restrictions
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
## Context

This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org Product markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would allow site owners to add structured data that specifies potential audience restrictions for eCommerce products, for example based on law or commonly accepted norms in specific countries or cultures.


## Proposal

Schema.org currently allows specifying a [suggested gender](https://schema.org/suggestedGender) or [suggested](https://schema.org/suggestedAge) (or [required](https://schema.org/requiredMinAge)) age-range on the /[PeopleAudience](https://schema.org/PeopleAudience) class. However, depending on the country or region, a specific product might or might not be legally allowed or might have different age restrictions (for example: marijuana is legal in some US states and not in others). We therefore propose to add a new **/applicableRegion** property with range [/DefinedRegion](https://schema.org/DefinedRegion) to the [/PeopleAudience](https://schema.org/PeopleAudience) class to specify the region(s) for which the specific PeopleAudience instance applies.

User (audience) restrictions might not always be age-related (for example, some products require special training before use), so we also propose to add a new property **/audienceRestriction** to the [/PeopleAudience](https://schema.org/PeopleAudience) class that allows site owners to specify **why** a product could be audience-restricted, e.g., because it is dangerous and requires certain training, because it is considered harmful for children, because it is designed to inflict bodily harm, etc.

The range of the proposed **/audienceRestriction** property would be a new enumeration **/AudienceRestrictionEnumeration** with the following suggested enumeration values based on common reasons why a product could be audience-restricted:



*   **Alcohol** - The product contains alcohol, for example wine, beer, or spirits.
*   **Violence** - The product shows or promotes violence.
*   **Healthcare**, for example prescription and OTC drugs, sexual enhancement treatments, restricted medical devices.
*   **Narcotic**, as defined by the 1961 UN convention (subdivided in 4 classes or schedules, ranging from least to most restrictive). For example marijuna or heroin.
*   **Tobacco**, for example cigars, cigarettes, chewing tobacco, e-cigarettes, hookahs.
*   **AdultContent** - The product contains adult content such as nudity, sexually suggestive or explicit material, or is intended to enhance sexual activity. Examples: Erotic videos,  sex toys.
*   **Weapon** - The product is intended to induce bodily harm, for example guns, mace, combat knives, brass knuckles, nail or other bombs, and spears.
*   **DangerousGood** - The product is dangerous and requires careful handling and/or special training of the user. See also [UN Model Regulations](https://www.delta-net.com/compliance/customs-controls/faqs/what-are-the-nine-classes-of-dangerous-goods) defining the 9 classes of dangerous goods.  

Additionally we could add [/Text](https://schema.org/Text) to the range of **/audienceRestriction** to allow a free-form explanation of why a product is audience-restricted.


## Possible extensions

To further classify narcotics we could consider introducing a new property **/narcoticSchedule** (with range Number and values 1-4 per the schedules defined by the UN).

To further classify dangerous goods we could introduce a new enumeration type /**_DangerousGoodTypeEnumeration_** and property **/dangerousGoodType** with possible values:



*   DangerousGoodExplosives
*   DangerousGoodGases
*   DangerousGoodFlammableLiquids
*   DangerousGoodFlammableSolid
*   DangerousGoodOxidisingAgentOrOrganicPeroxide
*   DangerousGoodToxinsAndInfectiousSubstances
*   DangerousGoodRadioactiveMaterials
*   DangerousGoodMiscellaneous

We could consider adding existing rating schemes for certain types of content, e.g, the EU and US rating schemes for movies.


## Considerations



*   Our goal is not to define a new rating scheme. The act of defining a rating scheme is full of pitfalls (well-documented in [ICRA fail](https://philarcher.org/icra/ICRAfail.pdf)). Different countries and cultures have very different rating systems and interpretations for example of what is nudity and what is violence ([example](https://qz.com/1335380/eighth-grade-shows-the-difference-between-how-the-us-and-europe-think-about-teens-and-sex/)) and what ages are allowed to be exposed to such content. Therefore this proposal restricts itself to simply allowing merchants and manufacturers to tag their products with specific characteristics ("this is a weapon", "this is a recreational drug", "this is an adult product") which could be a potential reason the product is audience-restricted in certain countries. The actual **interpretation** (e.g., deciding whether or not to block the content) of the tag is left to the consuming system.
*   We considered building on the existing [/isFamilyFriendly](https://schema.org/isFamilyFriendly) property in Schema.org but decided against since this a culture or country-specific interpretation. Although it is obvious that most or all of the here defined restrictions would make a product not family-friendly.
*   The proposal overlaps with the domain of product classification. Another option would be adding an enumeration under the existing [/category](https://schema.org/category) property. However, the domain of audience-restriction is narrow and specific, so we think it deserves its own definition.
*   Outside scope though somewhat related is defining other reasons why products should be restricted, e.g., because they have been recalled, because they contain certain chemicals, could be a choking hazard, etc.

issues.title: Rebase code for failing PRs
issues.author: RichardWallis
issues.body:
Following the fix of #2946, caused by the upgrading of some dependant python libraries such as rdflib, PRs that were failing (such as #2958) now pass CI tests.

For the failing PRs to pass the CI tests the code behind the PR had to be rebased against the current state of the main branch.  This was simple for PRs based on branches in this repository.

However several PRs (#2941, #2953, #2965, #2985 and possibly #2738) are hosted in branches in other forked repositories.  In these cases the code in those repositories, should be rebased against the main branch in this repository.

This issue is to capture to actions to achieve that

issues.title: scribe, pagination, provenance
issues.author: siglun
issues.body:
I added a comment somewhere else, now I realize that what I should have added an issue. I copy the comment here.

* [Manuscripts](https://schema.org/Manuscript)  require [numberOfPages](https://schema.org/numberOfPages) (or perhaps even number of folios. Manuscripts are more often than not foliated not paginated),
* they are written by a `scribe` who may or may not be identical to the `author` (usually not identical for medieval manuscripts) 
* and  may have a  `provenance` (which is basically a list  of changes of `owner` [Events](https://schema.org/Event)). 

It is a problem that "manuscripts" are as wide a genre as "printed matter" or "web page".
https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/1448#issuecomment-979107885

issues.title: Add country where a MerchantReturnPolicy applies to
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
[MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy) allows the definition of the country ([returnPolicyCountry](https://schema.org/returnPolicyCountry)) where a product must be sent to for returns. 

Merchant return policies often also differ depending on the country where the product is sold (returned from), so we propose to add an additional property /applicableCountry to allow the definition of countries where a particular return policy applies.

issues.author: tobiasschweizer
issues.body:
We are using JSON-LD to represent our metadata. We are using <https://validator.schema.org> to make sure that our metadata is valid.

In some cases, we use type annotations in JSON-LD to express that a value is an `xsd:date` or `xsd:float` etc.

However, these annotations do not pass validation:
![Screenshot 2021-12-06 at 12 00 29](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/6000023/144835043-cc6cff54-02d7-49bf-9af1-6f69938a0c0d.png)

We are using https://datashapes.org/schema.ttl as a reference implementation for our SHACL shapes that are applied in our own validation process. By convention, we encode an `schema:Date` as an `xsd:date`. For numerical values, we use `xsd:integer` or `xsd:float`, depending on the required precision.

Do the errors indicate that our data is actually wrong or is this rather a limitation of the validator (JSON-LD/RDF support)?

issues.title: Avatars and MetaAgents
issues.author: csarven
issues.body:
(Potentially a duplicate issue or can already be addressed by existing terms. The idea here was inspired by the advances in technology like Unreal Engine's MetaHuman Creator: https://docs.metahuman.unrealengine.com/ but the idea of avatars is far from new.)

A property to refer to specific kinds of avatars that can be used in digital systems. foaf:depiction/schema:image are related concepts (so can be a subproperty) but the emphasis here is on online avatars / "metahuman" (or perhaps more generally "metaagent"). The intention is an object that can be referred from (social?) agent profiles, along the lines of:

```turtle
<https://csarven.ca/#i>
  a schema:Person ;
  schema:avatar <https://example.org/sarven-avatar.ext> .
<https://example.org/sarven-avatar.ext>
  a schema:MetaAgent .
```

(What the exact property and/or the class is named in the example above is besides the point.)

One could grant access to applications and agents to use their avatar (that's on their personal storage) for specific purpose; anything that could incorporate the presentation of the self on the Web.

issues.title: Text type definition is unclear
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
The definition for the text data-type (https://schema.org/Text) is not well defined. The assumption seems to be that it contains Unicode text, but this is not stated explicitly and leaves many ambiguities: * What characters are allowed? Are C0 and C1 control characters allowed? * How are white-space characters handled? The current validator just echoes back text fields, but this this collapses all white-spaces to a single space (0x20). De facto this implies that carriage returns and paragraph cannot exist in text-fields. * Is the content expected to be raw text? Are some tagged formats allowed (HTML, markdown), or extensions (ANSI escape sequences). What is value of `description` of the following snippets: ``` ``` ``` ``` If the following snippet is allowed: ``` ``` Is it equivalent to the following? ```
Line 1
Line 2
```

issues.title: SMV does not seem to load external context definitions
issues.author: kulla
issues.body:
### Current behavior

The external context definition https://w3id.org/kim/lrmi-profile/draft/context.jsonld is basically schema.org since it includes the following definition:

```js
{
    "@context": {
        "id": "@id",
        "type": "@type",
        "@vocab": "http://schema.org/",
        ...
    }
}
```

Thus the following JSON-LD should be valid schema.org metadata:

```json
{
  "@context": [
    "https://w3id.org/kim/lrmi-profile/draft/context.jsonld",
    {
      "@language": "de"
    }
  ],
  "id": "https://serlo.org/1495",
  "type": [
    "LearningResource",
    "Article"
  ],
  "dateCreated": "2014-03-01T20:36:44+00:00",
  "dateModified": "2021-03-08T20:51:17+00:00"
}
```

However in [Schema Markup Validator](https://validator.schema.org/) an error is shown that the type couldn't be determined:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1327215/146656835-34654879-b904-496e-a51c-48fa8c8a4565.png)

### Expected behavior

I would expect that SMV can determine that the type of the above JSON-LD is http://schema.org/LearningResource and http://schema.org/Article

### Workaround

By copy and pasting the definition of https://w3id.org/kim/lrmi-profile/draft/context.jsonld into the above JSON-LD:

```json
{
  "@context": [
    "https://w3id.org/kim/lrmi-profile/draft/context.jsonld",
    {
      "@language": "de",
      "@vocab": "http://schema.org/",
      "type": "@type",
      "id": "@id"
    }
  ],
  "id": "https://serlo.org/1495",
  "type": [
    "LearningResource",
    "Article"
  ],
  "dateCreated": "2014-03-01T20:36:44+00:00",
  "dateModified": "2021-03-08T20:51:17+00:00"
}
```

the error disappears:

![](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/1327215/146656859-05a02134-781a-4244-8901-7a258adb342f.png)

Thus I suspect that https://w3id.org/kim/lrmi-profile/draft/context.jsonld was not loaded / interpreted properly by SMV.

Currently:

> Keywords or tags used to describe this content. Multiple entries in a keywords list are typically delimited by commas.

> Keywords or tags used to describe this item. Multiple entries in a keywords list are typically delimited by commas. The keywords property can also be repeated to avoid confusion if multi-word phrases are used and contain commas.

In https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/1150 @betehess proposes ActionPlatform as a class, to accompany the existing https://schema.org/actionPlatform

However we also have a similar construct on VideoGame and VideoGameSeries, i.e. https://schema.org/gamePlatform - this property is currently super open-ended (Text/URL/Thing).

There are also some unofficial terms in widespread use dating from the days before we had the "Pending" mechanism for proposals: http://schema.org/DesktopWebPlatform http://schema.org/MobileWebPlatform http://schema.org/AndroidPlatform http://schema.org/IOSPlatform. To these I would suggest we add a general /WebPlatform, since much content now tries to target both mobile and desktop; not to mention the other environments the Web is available from (e.g. WebXR browsers).

I suggest we start with an enumeration that can be used by both actionPlatform and gamePlatform, and be open to adding new codes to it as they're suggested here.

issues.title: /shortName proposal
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
A proposal from my colleagues suggesting the addition of a property shortName to schema.org.

> This is a change proposal from Google based on experience building products and services using Schema.org, in particular its existing naming properties. It also reflects experience with non-structured data approaches. If the property were adopted and used well we anticipate it could become a very useful contribution to the ecosystem.

Proposed changes:

 * /shortName  "Indicates a shortened version of the name of an item. It is often useful to know a short version of something's name - for example, to suggest compact abbreviated titles for Web pages. The [[alternateName]] property does not require names to be short, or even shorter than the main [[name]]. No specific character length is defined since these vary between natural languages and application contexts, but it would be unexpected for a shortName to be longer than the [[name]] of the same item."
 * Applies on types: Thing
   * Noting that this is unusually general, but there is wide applicability and a strong precedent with /name and /alternateName."
Value type: Text
 * Other changes: update [[alternateName]] to say "See also [[shortName]]."

issues.title: Proposal for Permit generalization
issues.author: Deele
issues.body:
During attempt to describe a real world situation where a certain organization has a certain permit to provide certain services, I found out that there is really no way in Schema to do that out of box. To challenge myself, I found closest relative https://schema.org/AuthorizeAction, as it had properties I had a necessity for. - agent - an Organization, gov institution that game that permission - location - a Place, address where services are being served - instrument - a DigitalDocument, that is that said permit document, that describes in details what this permission is about - actionStatus - CanceledActionStatus for permit that is no longer valid, ActiveActionStatus for permit that is still valid - recipient - an Organization, that this permit is for - object[0] - Service, that this permit is allowing - object[1] - another Service, that this permit is allowing - object[n] - more Services Then, inside DigitalDocument, I am using - temporalCoverage - to store time period this permit is valid from/to - creativeWorkStatus - Obsolete for permit that is no longer valid, Published for permit that is still valid (this needs to be updated for both entities) - expires - date for permits that are no longer valid - sourceOrganization - an Organization, that this permit is for - contentReferenceTime - a date when permit is valid from (because temporalCoverage is a complex field that I can't search by easily) - alternateName - stores a document identifier used in document management system - text - copy of contents of permit document (if possible) in HTML format ```json { "@context": "https://schema.org", "@type": "AuthorizeAction", "agent": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Gov entity X" }, "location": "Example street 1, City 2, Country 3, PO-4", "instrument": { "@type": "DigitalDocument", "name": "Permit ABC-321 to Company Y", "identifier": "ABC-321", "temporalCoverage": "2020-02-01/2020-12-31", "creativeWorkStatus": "Obsolete", "expires": "2020-02-10", "sourceOrganization": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Company Y", "identifier": "C-Y" }, "contentReferenceTime": "2020-01-20", "alternateName": "ABC-2020-321", "text": "

This is permit to allow Company Y do services A, B and C within store located in \"Example street 1, City 2, Country 3, PO-4\" by following conditions: D, E and F. Lorem ipsum.

" }, "actionStatus": "ActiveActionStatus", "object": [ { "@type": "Service", "name": "Service A", "identifier": "S-A" }, { "@type": "Service", "name": "Service B", "identifier": "S-B" }, { "@type": "Service", "name": "Service C", "identifier": "S-C" }, ], "recipient": { "@type": "Organization", "name": "Company Y", "identifier": "C-Y" } } ``` Now that I have begun explaining, I have a feeling, that upgrading Permit would be much better. A way to store related DigitalDocument, maybe, call the property "proof" or "issuedVia" (in spirit of "issuedThrough") or "instrument" (in spirit of AuthorizeAction property for same purpose) A way to store target organization or person, maybe, call the property "issuedTo", or, maybe, expand Audience type to allow specifying target organization or person A way to clearly determine status of this permit, maybe, a new type "permitStatus"? A way to keep the "validUntil" and store date when permit was canceled (early), because it might be that permit was for a year, but it was canceled after 6 months A way to store "The geographic area where a permit or similar thing is valid.", because "validIn" allows only "AdministrativeArea", but I would like to have "Place" there, or any other, location-kind. What about bringing in [https://schema.org/location](https://t.co/NXMoZnuy4q) property and, maybe, add "AdministrativeArea" as a possible option to it?

issues.title: FEATURE REQUEST: `status` property on `Role` type
issues.author: JLKM
issues.body:
At first glance schema seems to offer a set of metadata with a snapshot of the present status. Luckily we have the (a little overlooked?) type `Role`, that can be inserted anywhere and store more information about the relations between types.

Of the extra properties offered by `Role`, `startDate` and `endDate` are useful, if you want to expand metadata into historical relations.

An obvious use case in this regard is Person => worksFor => several Roles at different Organizations including start- and endtimes.

Often, however, you just know, that the relationsship (job, membership, athlete etc.) has ended - not when it ended.

This would be solved nice and easy by adding a `status`-property to the `Role`-type. Just like in:

1. Property `eventStatus` on type `Event`
2. Property `nonprofitStatus` on type `Organization`
3. Property `status` (plain and simple) on type `MedicalStudy`

A property like that will IMO make it a lot easier to add historical (and still accurate) metadata to records on the web. And eventually pave the way for a even more semantic web thanks to schema.org.

issues.body:
This is a proposal from Google, based on experience building products that use Schema.org Event descriptions. 

Currently it is hard to determine if an Event is considered "all day".  Heuristics like start date and end dates being the same day are complicated if an event continues for more than one day, but each day is "all day". It would be good to have a more explicit handling of this concept.

Suggestion: 

> :allDay a rdf:Property ;
    rdfs:label "allDay" ;
    schema:domainIncludes schema:Event ;
    schema:rangeIncludes schema:Boolean ;
    rdfs:comment "Whether this is an 'all day' type of event that doesn't specify hour/minutes granularity for start time or duration." .

Apparently this has been [discussed](https://github.com/icalendar/icalendar/issues/71) over in the icalendar standard:

A [proposal](https://github.com/icalendar/icalendar/issues/71#issuecomment-48607091) there from 2014:

 >I came up with this too after looking into the RFC and diffing the output of a thunderbird-lightning export. Though I would consider it a work around. Even though the RFC does not seem to include an explicit "allday" boolean most calendar clients soft of emulate it by giving you a checkbox that says "all day".
Would you perhaps consider something like this checkbox by adding something like this?
>
> event.allday = true

Apparently this was added to the icalendar Wiki, which I haven't yet found. 

Looking at https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/rfc5545/ I don't see a treatment of "all day".

issues.title: Barcode object should have a embeddedData attribute
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
Barcodes typically contain some data, if the content is plain-text, then the `text` field inherited from CreativeWork can be used, but what if it is a gtin (probably the most common case), or some structured information, like for instance a data-matrix.

It would make sense to add a `embeddedData` field to `Barcode` which would contain:

* GTIN (typical linear barcodes)
* StructedData (data-matrix).
* Text

issues.title: "sender", an "Action" property, is incompatible with "Message"
issues.author: Seirdy
issues.body:
This is a specific instance of [issue 53](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/53)

## Problem

The schema.org [`Message` type](https://schema.org/Message) allows a [`sender` property](https://schema.org/sender).

`sender` is a sub-property of [`participant`](https://schema.org/participant). `participant` can only be used on `Action` types; `sender` can be used on `ReceiveAction` and `Message` types. `Message` is not an `Action` type; therefore, giving a `Message` a `sender` will (correctly) trigger an error in the Structured Data Linter.

## Reproduction

Live example: [this Article/BlogPosting](https://seirdy.one/2020/11/23/website-best-practices.html) contains microdata. One part of it describes a `Quotation` from an `EmailMessage` whose `sender` is a `Person`. It validates perfectly according to the schema.org validator, but triggers the following message on the Structured Data Linter:

```
property schemas:participant: Subject _:g1337520(schemas:EmailMessage,schemas:Thing,schemas:CreativeWork,schemas:Message,rdfs:Resource) not compatible with domainIncludes (schemas:Action)
```

## Possible solutions

I see three ways to fix this, ranked by my personal preference (descending):

1. amend `participant` to allow use on the type `Message`
2. reform `sender` to no longer be a sub-property of `participant`
3. reform `Message` to be an `Action`
