issues.title: Proposal to add a few properties to express shipping dimensions of a Product
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand shipping dimensions (and associated delivery fees) for products sold online. 

**Proposal** - Schema.org supports the specification of product dimensions through properties [depth](https://schema.org/depth), [width](https://schema.org/width), [height](https://schema.org/height), and [weight](https://schema.org/weight). However, delivery dimensions of a product can be substantially different from the product's dimensions itself, for example flat-pack furniture that needs to be assembled after delivery, or fragile items that require heavy protective materials for transport. Such shipping dimensions can also vary depending on the merchant, so are typically related to an Offer and not a Product. We therefore propose to add 4 new properties _shippingWidth, shippingHeight, shippingLength_, and _shippingWeight_. All 4 properties will be of type [QuantitativeValue](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue) and will be for use on class [Offer](http://schema.org/Offer).

**Alternatives**

*   Instead of adding 4 new properties we could add the existing [depth](https://schema.org/depth), [width](https://schema.org/width), [height](https://schema.org/height), and [weight](https://schema.org/weight) properties for use on [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) (currently these are only available on Product). However, this might be ambiguous and cause confusion. 
*   A more flexible alternative would be adding the 4 existing properties [depth](https://schema.org/depth), [width](https://schema.org/width), [height](https://schema.org/height), and [weight](https://schema.org/weight) for use on [OfferShippingDetails](https://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails), which allows for multiple packaging options for the same product. However, this might be unnecessary since packaging is typically the same independent from the shipping destination. 
*   Yet another alternative would be adding a new _ShippingDimension_ structured type (to be used on [Offer](https://schema.og/Offer) using a new property), and adding the 4 existing dimension properties for use on this new type.
*   Instead of the "shipping" prefix we could decided to use a "package" or "shippingPackage" prefix for the property names.

issues.title: Bump rack from 2.2.3 to 2.2.3.1 in /software/scripts
issues.author: dependabot[bot]
issues.body:
Bumps [rack](https://github.com/rack/rack) from 2.2.3 to 2.2.3.1.
Changelog

Sourced from rack's changelog.

Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. For info on how to format all future additions to this file please reference Keep A Changelog.

[3.0.0] - Unreleased

Security

  • Do not use semicolon as GET parameter separator. (#1733, [@​jeremyevans])

SPEC Changes

  • Response status must now be an integer greater than or equal to 100.
  • Response headers must now be an unfrozen hash.
  • Response header keys can no longer include uppercase characters.
  • Response header values can be an Array to handle multiple values (and no longer supports \n encoded headers).
  • Response body can now respond to #call (streaming body) instead of #each (enumerable body), for the equivalent of response hijacking in previous versions.
  • Middleware must no longer call #each on the body, but they can call #to_ary on the body if it responds to #to_ary.
  • rack.input is no longer required to be rewindable.
  • rack.multithread/rack.multiprocess/rack.run_once are no longer required environment keys.
  • SERVER_PROTOCOL is now a required key, matching the HTTP protocol used in the request.

Removed

  • Remove rack.multithread/rack.multiprocess/rack.run_once. These variables generally come too late to be useful. (#1720, [@​ioquatix], [@​jeremyevans]))
  • Remove deprecated Rack::Request::SCHEME_WHITELIST. ([@​jeremyevans])
  • Remove internal cookie deletion using pattern matching, there are very few practical cases where it would be useful and browsers handle it correctly without us doing anything special. (#1844, [@​ioquatix])

Added

  • Rack::Headers added to support lower-case header keys. ([@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::Utils#set_cookie_header now supports escape_key: false to avoid key escaping. ([@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::RewindableInput supports size. (@​ahorek)
  • Rack::RewindableInput::Middleware added for making rack.input rewindable. ([@​jeremyevans])
  • The RFC 7239 Forwarded header is now supported and considered by default when looking for information on forwarding, falling back to the X-Forwarded-* headers. Rack::Request.forwarded_priority accessor has been added for configuring the priority of which header to check. (#1423, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Allow response headers to contain array of values. (#1598, [@​ioquatix])

Changed

  • BREAKING CHANGE: Require status to be an Integer. (#1662, @​olleolleolle)
  • BREAKING CHANGE: Query parsing now treats parameters without = as having the empty string value instead of nil value, to conform to the URL spec. (#1696, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Relax validations around Rack::Request#host and Rack::Request#hostname. (#1606, @​pvande)
  • Removed antiquated handlers: FCGI, LSWS, SCGI, Thin. (#1658, [@​ioquatix])
  • Removed options from Rack::Builder.parse_file and Rack::Builder.load_file. (#1663, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::HTTP_VERSION has been removed and the HTTP_VERSION env setting is no longer set in the CGI and Webrick handlers. (#970, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::Request#[] and #[]= now warn even in non-verbose mode. (#1277, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Decrease default allowed parameter recursion level from 100 to 32. (#1640, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Attempting to parse a multipart response with an empty body now raises Rack::Multipart::EmptyContentError. (#1603, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Rack::Utils.secure_compare uses OpenSSL's faster implementation if available. (#1711, @​bdewater)
  • Rack::Request#POST now caches an empty hash if input content type is not parseable. (#749, [@​jeremyevans])

issues.title: Proposal to add support for shipping origin
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand delivery routes for products sold online.

**Proposal** - Schema.org supports the specification of shipping **destinations** (through the [shippingDestination](https://schema.org/shippingDestination) property) where an online merchant delivers ordered products to. However, Schema.org currently does not support shipping **origins**, where merchants ship the product from. Often a product's shipping source is relevant information for consumers, so propose to add a new _shippingOrigin_ property of type [DefinedRegion](http://schema.org/DefinedRegion) for use on type [OfferShippingDetails](https://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails).

**Alternatives** - Instead of adding the shipping origin under [OfferShippingDetails](https://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails) we could consider adding it under [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) directly to avoid having to repeat the origin for every separate [OfferShippingDetails](https://schema.org/OfferShippingDetails) instance. However, the flexibility of having different origins depending on the destination is useful, especially for retailers with multiple fulfillment centers and warehouses.

issues.title: Proposal to add support for Amazon's ASIN product identifier
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org [Product ](https://schema.org/Product)markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to identify products sold online.

**Proposal** - Schema.org supports a variety of industry-standard product identifiers, for example [gtin](https://schema.org/gtin), [mpn](http://schema.org/mpn), and [nsn](https://schema.org/nsn). We propose to add a new property _asin_ of type [Text](https://schema.org/Text) for use on [Product](https://schema.org/Product), representing the Amazon Standard Identification Number. Given its common and broad use in the industry it would be beneficial to allow products to be identified with their corresponding ASIN code in structured data.

**Alternatives** - An alternative option would be supporting ASIN through the existing [productID](https://schema.org/productID) property. However, given the broad usage of ASIN, support as a first-class property seems more appropriate.

issues.title: Proposal for a new "Job" type
issues.author: jdevalk
issues.body:
Schema.org already has [quite a few job related properties](https://www.google.com/search?q=site:https://schema.org/+job):

* [`JobPosting`](https://schema.org/JobPosting)
* [`jobBenefits`](https://schema.org/jobBenefits)
* [`jobTitle`](https://schema.org/jobTitle)
* [`jobLocation`](https://schema.org/jobLocation) & [`jobLocationType`](https://schema.org/jobLocationType)

and lots of ways to describe salaries etc for job openings. 

We also have [`worksFor`](https://schema.org/worksFor), for describing which `Organization` one works for, and [`Occupation` ](https://schema.org/Occupation) / [`hasOccupation`](https://schema.org/hasOccupation) to describe specific occupations. What's really hard though, is tying all of these together for a `Person`. You can't describe that a person has a job with a specific title. It's even harder to describe one's employment history in Schema. So I'm proposing to introduce a `Job` type and a `jobHistory` attribute.

Note: I know that `Role` was [originally supposed to fix this](http://blog.schema.org/2014/06/introducing-role.html). That doesn't seem to have really worked well, and since we already have so many "Job" related attributes and properties I think having the global Job type makes a ton of sense.
 
## Example schema

```json
{
	"@context": "https://schema.org/",
	"@type": "Person",
	"name": "Joost de Valk",
	"worksFor": {
		"@type": "Job",
		"jobTitle": "Partner",
		"organization": {
			"@type": "Organization",
			"name": "Altha"
		},
		"startDate": "2010-05-28"
	},
	"jobHistory": {
		"@type": "Job",
		"jobTitle": "CEO",
		"organization": {
			"@type": "Organization",
			"name": "Yoast"
		},
		"startDate": "2010-05-28",
		"endDate": "2019-08-01"
	}
}
```

issues.title: Proposal to add new property /mobileUrl as sub-property of /url
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to differentiate mobile optimized URLs from standard (desktop) URLs.

**Proposal** - Schema.org supports a [/url](https://schema.org/url) property for use on [/Thing](https://schema.org/Thing), used to specify the URL of an item. Online publishers often create separate mobile-optimized landing pages, and we therefore propose to add a new **/mobileUrl** property as a sub-property of [/url](https://schema.org/url) for use on [/Thing](https://schema.org/Thing) to allow consuming systems to better understand mobile vs non-mobile versions of web pages representing the same entity.

issues.title: Proposal to add new property /checkoutUrl on /Offer
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** 

This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand URLs used by online merchants to send consumers to checkout pages for products sold online.

**Proposal** 

Schema.org currently provides a [/urlTemplate](https://schema.org/urlTemplate) property with values of type [/Text](https://schema.org/Text), used to specify a templated URL following [RFC6570](https://schema.org/urlTemplate). In the world of eCommerce, such templated URLs are important in the case of checkout URLs, where a consumer clicks on a product for a one-click purchase, sending the user directly to a checkout page, passing in parameters such as for example a logged-in consumer id, product identifier, quantity, discount code, and more.

We therefore propose to add a new **/checkoutUrl** property for use on the [/Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) type to allow merchants to specify a checkout page URL to allow online checkout of the offered product. The property would be a templated URL to allow passing-in of aforementioned parameters to the checkout page. We can decide to allow values of type [/Text](https://schema.org/Text) for **/checkoutUrl** or we could introduce new types, for example, **/UrlTemplate** as a subtype of [/Text ](https://schema.org/Text)or [URL](https://schema.org/URL).

issues.title: add an ML Model type to schema.org, likely under /Dataset, ... and potentially other major types (SingleTabularDataset, MultipleTabularDataset?)
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
[Dataset](https://schema.org/Dataset) is pretty vague, it can cover anything from .zip files of .wavs of social science interviews, application-specific on-disk file formats, etc etc. In theory we could have subtypes for all of these, but it would be a neverending task, so we have tended to address such needs through indirect mechanisms like https://schema.org/fileFormat

The practice of publishing and consuming ML models is different, and worth exploring a special subtype, to allow consuming services to differentiate machine learning models from other unrelated things. This is partially to do with the massive attention associated with "ML", "AI" etc., but also relates to the relatively inscrutable nature of trained ML models. You get something that can map inputs to outputs or act as a controller of an agent of some kind, ... but how it works internally is relatively unclear. This is in stark contrast to the most stereotypical kinds of Datasetty Dataset, i..e. where you have the rows and columns of descriptive tables, and some reasonable clarity on how the parts of the dataset relate to the whole. 

In many ways machine learning models are more like software artifacts than they are like (for example) "open data" CSV files. Historically Schema.org hasn't included https://schema.org/SoftwareSourceCode or https://schema.org/SoftwareApplication as subtypes of /Dataset, ... although a case could be made to do so. Similarly Docker (etc.) packaging, or Debian/CPAN/NPM etc packages are somewhat related.

This issue comes out of discussions (with colleagues and in wider world) about the scope of "Dataset", and the concern that it will just be super confusing to try to persuade ML folk to markup up models as datasets, whereas in their preferred technology, models are built from datasets.

So - 

How about we add (as an exploratory, "Pending" term) a type: MLModel

* Description: A schema.org MLModel represents a machine learning model. These will typically but not necessarily consist of some data describing the general setup and architecture of the model, and a larger set of parameters. The specific format of the model can be indicated via fileFormat, and might be proprietary, toolkit specific, or adhere to some published standard.

Adding an MLModel type would allow publishers to distinguish models from other datasets more clearly, and in a way that could be used by consuming applications. Recently there has been an increasing recognition of the risks around bias and inappropriate re-use of pre-trained machine learning models, as well as a concern that the high cost of training certain kinds of model makes it important for such models to be shareable, lowering barriers to entry of the ML/AI field. In this climate, it is ideal when data publishers provide not only the information describing a pre-trained machine learning model they're offering, but also the dataset(s) upon which the model was trained. Calling both of these published artifacts "Dataset" may be confusing, ...despite ML models fitting under Schema.org's pretty broad notion of Dataset. My proposal here partially resolves this by adding a convenience type. For those who care to dig they might find out that MLModel is considered a special kind of Dataset, but most won't even encounter this information.

There's more to say on this but I've written too much already, and wanted to start some discussion. Opinions welcomed!

issues.title: Property or mechanism for Plus Codes for Places and Businesses (and more)
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
[**Plus Codes**](https://maps.google.com/pluscodes/) are a neat and precise way of identifying a geographical place or area.

I think it would be useful to support Plus Codes in schema.org, at least for

- indicating places, e.g. in local business and organization markup
and
- indicating service areas, 

but there are likely many additional applications.

Someone on the Web ([hugoscott.com](https://hugoscott.com/en/how-to-implement-googles-plus-codes-in-schema-org-markup/)) suggested the use of [`AdditionalProperty`](https://schema.org/AdditionalProperty), but even as the original proposer of this pattern, I do not think it fits here.

Since Plus Codes can indicate both **"points"** (yes, I know, they do not exist in reality ;-) - think of a particular store, [`GeoCoordinates`](https://schema.org/GeoCoordinates)) and **areas** ([`GeoShape`](https://schema.org/GeoShape)), I think the most straightforward way would be to expand the range of [`geo`](https://schema.org/geo) to include [`Text`](https://schema.org/Text) and indicate it should be a `PlusCode`.

A bit cleaner will be 

a) a subproperty of `schema:geo` named `geoPlusCode` with a range of `Text` 
or
b) a new type `schema:PlusCode` as a subtype of `Text` and expanding the range of `geo` to include this new type.

I think that option b) will be best, and easy to implement.

issues.title: NewsArticle -- paywall, subscription and thirdparty properties
issues.author: WeaverStever
issues.body:
I've been reading more news content from my phone (Android) recently. Basically, I want the news, I am not going to subscribe or submit my email address to read content from my phone (with my over-sized fingers, I avoid the keypad like the plague). If the publisher wants more than what the ad-revenue generates, I will go elsewhere.

I'm thinking that it might be useful for future generations to be able to tag news articles, similar to what [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Reliable_sources/Cost) has done for references. Wikipedia's [Template:Subscription required](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Template:Subscription_required) shows a padlock image (locked) next to the reference.
 
 **Paywall** -- the article, or portions thereof are behind a paywall. 
 **Subscription** -- requires a subscription, I.e., email address or other identity information.
 **ThirdParty** -- the complete article, is on another website, the content creator's website.
 
I have noticed over the years, that some websites will have a mixture, for instance, the Wall Street Journal will sometimes place articles outside of their paywall.  (Some publishers, who are predominantly behind a paywall, might want to notify the reader that a specific article is free.)

Anyway, it would be nice if the search engines could eventually flag these articles so we don't waste our time and bandwidth on them.

issues.title: Proposal to add support for product highlights
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org Product markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would allow merchants to add product highlights to their product structured data, and allow us and others to better understand products sold online.

## Description

Products advertised or sold online are often displayed not only with a title and description, but also with more detailed information, such as a list of product highlights, which are easy to consume and quick to scan ordered bullet points emphasizing the relevant attributes of a product. For example:



*   _Capture quality 24mp photos and UHD video in an easy to use point and shoot camera with a 2.8" preview screen_
*   _Excellent for underwater photography, submersible up to 16 feet_
*   _Protective plastic cover to protect from scratches_
*   _A great first DSLR camera with enough features for novice photographers of any age_
*   _Uses 2 AAA Batteries (included) and saves videos to a mini SD card (not included)_

To support ordered highlight lists we propose to introduce a new property **/highlights** of type [/ItemList](https://schema.org/ItemList) (for use on [/Product](https://schema.org/Product)). The example given above could then be represented as follows:

```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Product",
  "sku": "camera-12345",
  "image": "https://www.example.com/camera.jpg",
  "name": "Nice camera",
  "description": "Compact DSLR camera with pancake lens",
  "gtin": "12345678901234",
  "brand": {
    "@type": "Brand",
    "name": "CameraBrand"
  },
  "color": "black",
  "offers": {
    "@type": "Offer",
    "url": "http://www.example.com/camera_offer",
    "itemCondition": "https://schema.org/NewCondition",
    "availability": "https://schema.org/Backorder",
    "price": "539.99",
    "priceCurrency": "EUR"
  },
  "highlights": {
    "@type": "ItemList",
    "itemListElement": [
      {
        "@type": "ListItem",
        "position": 1,
        "item": "Capture quality 24mp photos and UHD video in an easy to use point and shoot camera with a 2.8\" preview screen"
      },
      {
        "@type": "ListItem",
        "position": 2,
        "item": "Excellent for underwater photography, submersible up to 16 feet"
      },
      {
        "@type": "ListItem",
        "position": 3,
        "item": "Protective plastic cover to protect from scratches"
      },
      {
        "@type": "ListItem",
        "position": 4,
        "item": "A great first DSLR camera with enough features for novice photographers of any age"
      },
      {
        "@type": "ListItem",
        "position": 5,
        "item": "Uses 2 AAA Batteries (included) and saves videos to a mini SD card (not included)"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

It is important to note that the present proposal suffers from the same disadvantage as for example [#2832](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2832), i.e., it requires verbose markup to support explicit ordering of list elements. Eventually (but outside scope of this proposal) it would be beneficial to support ordered elements with syntactic sugar or even an extension of RDFS since ordered elements are a very common need and would benefit from a more concise notation.

issues.title: Constructs to represent corrections - and their use in factchecking
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
This came up via the Trust Project contributions (c.f. #1950) to Schema.org a few years back, and is touched on in the [blog post](http://blog.schema.org/2021/12/enriching-claim-reviews-sharing.html) from Andy Dudfield and Leigh Dodds.

From that blog post:

> Corrections and actions. The [second wave of fact checking](https://fullfact.org/blog/2019/jun/how-fact-checking-works/) is about more than just writing fact checks, it involves taking action to tackle disinformation. How might we surface data about requests for corrections to published content, and record when those corrections have been made? Schema.org currently includes some vocabulary to help describe corrections and comments which we've explored. But further work is needed to define a useful way of recording and sharing the other activities undertaken by fact checkers.


Currently we have:

 * [https://schema.org/correction](https://schema.org/correction) 
   * "Indicates a correction to a [CreativeWork](https://schema.org/CreativeWork), either via a [CorrectionComment](https://schema.org/CorrectionComment), textually or in another document."
 * [https://schema.org/correctionsPolicy](https://schema.org/correctionsPolicy)
   * "For an [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) (e.g. [NewsMediaOrganization](https://schema.org/NewsMediaOrganization)), a statement describing (in news media, the newsroom’s) disclosure and correction policy for errors."
 * The [https://schema.org/version](https://schema.org/version) is also relevant.

These are a good foundation, but seem to have been under-utilized so far.

In the context of a ClaimReview, it would be good to know - in the case of problematic claims - if the claimant has made a correction somewhere. This could be written/spoken, informal or formal, or perhaps also journalistic coverage of those. This case I suspect is likely to be largely political factchecking, but there are also other high profile public figures who sometimes retract or correct their claims.

However, we should also cover cases beyond fact checking - books, articles (scholarly or otherwise), media content - these are all areas where mistakes are made and corrected.

I am opening this issue to encourage evaluation of the existing correction vocabulary, especially in the context of factchecking and ClaimReview. Are there important usecases we don't cover, or examples we should add to the site?

issues.title: Pending review of /sha256 - consider subresource integrity format instead
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
See https://www.w3.org/TR/SRI/#the-integrity-attribute

> 3.1 Integrity metadata
To verify the integrity of a response, a user agent requires integrity metadata as part of the [request](https://fetch.spec.whatwg.org/#concept-request-integrity-metadata). This metadata consists of the following pieces of information:

> cryptographic hash function (“alg”)
[digest](https://www.w3.org/TR/SRI/#dfn-digest) (“val”)
options (“opt”)
The hash function and digest must be provided in order to validate a response’s integrity.

> NOTE
At the moment, no options are defined. However, future versions of the spec may define options, such as MIME types [[MIMETYPE](https://www.w3.org/TR/SRI/#bib-MIMETYPE)].

>This metadata must be encoded in the same format as the hash-source (without the single quotes) in [section 4.2 of the Content Security Policy Level 2 specification](http://www.w3.org/TR/CSP2/#source-list-syntax).

>For example, given a script resource containing only the string alert(\'Hello, world.\');, an author might choose [SHA-384](https://www.w3.org/TR/SRI/#dfn-sha-2) as a hash function. H8BRh8j48O9oYatfu5AZzq6A9RINhZO5H16dQZngK7T62em8MUt1FLm52t+eX6xO is the base64-encoded digest that results. This can be encoded as follows:

>EXAMPLE 4
sha384-H8BRh8j48O9oYatfu5AZzq6A9RINhZO5H16dQZngK7T62em8MUt1FLm52t+eX6xO

issues.title: Validator cannot recognise mixture of tagged and untagged strings in JSON-LD
issues.author: RichardWallis
issues.body:
A combination of language tagged and untagged strings assigned to a single property causes the tagged strings to be reported as errors.  

Cut down example:
```
{
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "schema:Person",
    "name": "Lee, Kuan Yew",
    "alternateName": [
        "Li Guangyao",
        "LKY",
        {
            "@language": "zh",
            "@value": "李光耀"
        },
        {
            "@language": "ta",
            "@value": "லீ, குவான் யூ"
        },
        "Harry Lee Kuan Yew"
    ],
    "birthDate": "1923-09-16"
}
```
Results in : 
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13315406/185806724-1d4ff7b7-d5a8-4653-ab8c-47a2e0c41765.png)
 
Remove the non-tagged strings from the array assigned to the alternateName property and the tagged strings are captured correctly:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/13315406/185806882-b1f5f4a9-1ab7-4c18-8c16-d1458106365f.png)

Remove the tagged strings and the non-tagged strings are captured correctly.

Separate the tagged and non-tagged arrays into separate statements, results in a _Duplicate key found_ error.

Outcome is that you cannot represent a name, alternateName or similar properties with multiple values if they are a mixture of tagged and untagged strings.  A common occurrence in countries where English is not the, or only, primary language.

Note: Other tools such as the JSON-LD Playground correctly process the example.

issues.title: "cost of goods sold"?
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
Schema.org can now express the vast majority of the things that Google defined in its Shopping Feeds specification (also used by Facebook, Bing and others). 

One thing that hasn't been proposed by my Google colleagues (/cc @alex-jansen) is something to match their "cost of goods sold" field. This makes more sense in non-public use than for being included in a web page. Publishers likely do not want to broadcast to competitors and customers the exact price they paid for things being sold - it's usefulness is for analytics and reporting.

Although we have a draft "[feeds](https://schema.org/docs/feeds.html)" spec for Schema.org which would support non-public feeds, and the precedent of non-public vocabulary for use in email messages, I'd welcome wider input.

My inclination is to add it, but to expect it to stay in Pending status a while, until some evidence of utility emerges.

I am looking at the MapCategoryType Enumeration values. https://schema.org/MapCategoryType

I notice that this vocabulary is deeply rooted in the functional use of the visual display rather than the type of content or the method of content displayed. In-line with this observation I would like to suggest three additional values to be added. These values represent broad categories, rather than discrete cartographic or plot types.

issues.title: Proposal to add support for customs declaration code
issues.author: Radiergummi
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from [Matchory](https://matchory.com); we build a comprehensive database of manufacturing companies, their customers, and shipments between them. Currently, we have a database of around 10 million companies and about 800 million individual shipments, all structured as an extended schema.org vocabulary, stored as JSON-LD.  
While designing the data structure, we had to come up with several additional properties; some of them are too specific to B2B shipping for schema.org (we plan to publish our own vocabulary in the future), but others would make good candidates for inclusion. This is one of them.

**Proposal** - Schema.org already provides a lot of properties for shipments and trading (#3122 being highly anticipated); we would like to propose adding a property for the customs declaration code from the internationally used [Harmonized System](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Harmonized_System). More than 200 countries are members in the issuing organisation and use those codes for imported and exported goods. Every merchant buying and every supplier selling goods knows, and searches for, those codes. Every participating country requires these codes to be declared for goods leaving and entering customs.  

An HS code is a hierarchical, numeric string, consisting of three two-digit groups of wares, from less to more specific. This makes them ideal for broadly categorising products. As HS is an internationally used and maintained standard, it fosters interoperability across vendors and platforms.

Therefore, we'd like to propose to add a new `hsCode` property to the [Demand](https://schema.org/Demand) and [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) classes. This would fit in well with the existing [gtin](https://schema.org/gtin) property, but provide a way to express offers or demand for a category of products, not just a single instance.

**Alternatives** - Currently, we use the [category](https://schema.org/category) property to store the HS code, but that is only available on Offer, not Demand, and it doesn't feel particularly correct to store the customs classification code in a general product category.

It's our -- my -- first time contributing to schema.org, so apologies for any missteps. I'm more than happy to carry this forward, though.

issues.title: Add support for sales tax
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body: Products sold in the US and Canada are typically advertised with a price that does not include sales tax. It would be beneficial for consumers to understand the total price they have to pay. However, Schema.org currently does not allow the specification of said sales taxes. The only currently available nearby property is [/valueAddedTaxIncluded](https://schema.org/valueAddedTaxIncluded), for use on [/PriceSpecification](https://schema.org/PriceSpecification). We propose to consider adding first-class support for sales taxes, possible extended with related properties such as customs duties, additional regulatory fees (e.g., related to recycling), and  even explicit support for VAT/GST rates.

issues.title: Add /additionalProperty for use on /Offer

issues.title: Icons (or favicons) sensitive to color scheme
issues.author: tomayac
issues.body:
According to https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6408, (fav)icon markup that is respective of the user's preferred color scheme as below is valid (code sample taken straight from https://github.com/whatwg/html/issues/6408#issue-813641454):

```html
<link
      rel="icon"
      href="https://fakeimg.pl/128x128/000000/"
      media="(prefers-color-scheme: dark)"
      type="image/png"
/>

<link
      rel="icon"
      href="https://fakeimg.pl/128x128/ffffff/"
      media="(prefers-color-scheme: light)"
      type="image/png"
/>
```

Now schema.org currently doesn't allow [WebContent](https://schema.org/WebContent), [WebPage](https://schema.org/WebPage), [WebPageElement](https://schema.org/WebPageElement), [WebSite](https://schema.org/WebSite), or [WebApplication](https://schema.org/WebApplication) to have an icon or favicon (related: https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/1303, https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/939), but if it did, these icons should probably be sensitive to the user's preferred color scheme.

In the context of _potentially_ using structured markup (apart from the HTML) for the purpose of presenting favicons alongside Web search results, having this feature would improve the user experience:

- Search engine results page (itself respecting the user's preferred color scheme, that is, dark) suggests the site has a red favicon:

   ![Screenshot 2022-11-02 at 10 53 14](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/145676/199459318-65b8bb6c-f583-42ea-96c0-b75d44cc7573.png)
- Upon navigating to the site, the favicon actually is black:

   ![Screenshot 2022-11-02 at 10 53 35](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/145676/199459328-43fed62e-8348-4a0b-8700-cf6f6748ebf9.png)

issues.title: Proposal: RestrictedDiet Subtypes: LowSucrose, LowMaltose & LowStarch
issues.author: GinMorgWireless
issues.body:
Hi Community Team, 

I would like to request the addition of three restricteddiet subtypes to the
schema (https://schema.org/RestrictedDiet#subtypes).

* LowSucroseDiet
* LowMaltoseDiet
* LowStarchDiet

Lactose, Sucrose and Maltose are three disaccharides that can be problematic to
digest for people who lack the enzymes to do so. Sucrase-Isomaltase deficiency
(SID) with/without lactase deficiency are serious medical conditions that
require a specific diet, and/or replacement enzymes such as Lactase or
invertase. Those with SID can also be sensitive to starches, as the digestive
process breaks starches into Sucrose and/or Maltose which may then subsequently
cause health issues. 

Further it is challenging for people without extensive nutrition knowledge to
identify low sucrose/low maltose and low starch foods individually and within
meals so they can eat without adverse effects. Being able to tag recipes for
search will offer an immediate opportunity for people to locate appropriate
recipes that will contribute to their greater health, wellness and welfare.

The precedent for adding these already exists as the disaccharide lactose is
already represented by the LowLactose restrictedDiet subtype. 

Thank you for your consideration on this request.

issues.title: datamodel clarification - interpreting strings as things
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
This issue addresses the situation in which Schema.org somewhat encourages the use of strings, on properties that are defined in a way that only expects one or more non-literal types. It proposes some additional documentation that can be used by applications that parse and consume Schema.org documentation.

We can do better than saying that consumers will often "do the best we can".

## Background

From the start, schema.org has said in our [datamodel](https://schema.org/docs/datamodel.html) docs:

> We [...] expect that often, where we expect a property value of type Person, Place, Organization or some other subClassOf Thing, we will get a text string, even if our schemas don't formally document that expectation. In the spirit of "some data is better than none", search engines will often accept this markup and do the best we can.

We have said this for 10+ years now, and it is based on Schema.org's initial creation as a very Search-centric effort. Years later we are seeing other usecases alongside Search, in particular Schema.org's various connections to the world of Knowledge Graphs, where this kind of vague data and underspecified parsing rules risks holding back innovative uses of the data.

It is time to tidy up the "strings as things" piece of Schema.org, while respecting the fact that millions of pages still use this convention, particularly in our original primary syntax, HTML5 Microdata.

## Proposal

We should improve our general documentation by sketching a minimal transformation on parsed Schema.org graphs which converts string-valued properties into entity-valued properties, where the referenced entity is described using at least one Schema.org type, while the original string property value (in absence of other information) then becomes the value of a property of the new entity.

### Design Sketch

Rough idea, for some entity X with a property P whose value V is unexpectedly of a Text type, we can optionally create a replacement graph that expands and makes explicit that V can be seen as the value of a property on a previously implicit entity. 

For this to be implementable, we sketch some options for assigning types and properties in this new structure.

 -  basic-de-stringify-transform:
     - any graph edge which points to a string literal, i.e. Text) value ("V") is re-written to reference a non-Text entity which will have a Schema.org type.
     - This new entity, in turn, will have a property whose value is  the original value, V.
     - In the absence of any additional information, the type will be `/Thing`, and the property `/name`.
   - basic de-stringify can be augmented through any heuristics and background knowledge (of application, site, dataset, etc.) available. Schema.org probably won't enumerate these, preferring to encourage explicit markup instead.
   - basic de-stringify could also be augmented by using explicit annotations recorded within our schema definitions, which give a "best guess" type for some or all properties.
      - For example,  we might annotate the `/publisher` property to say its best guess de-stringifying type is `/Organization`, whereas for '/author' it might be `/Person`. In the absence of this information, our most boring type, `/Thing`, could be used.
      - To facilitate this, Schema.org would need to create and document a property that can be used in Schema definitions to map from some property to the "best guess" type for de-stringified values. Possible names: `/destringifyTypeHint`, `/bestGuessType`, ...
     
## Examples

Some initial examples, and suggestions for more complex examples and problems.

# Example 1: The /publisher of an /Article

source-data:

```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Article",
  "publisher": "QWERTYUIOPASDFGHJKLZXCVBNM"
}
```

schema-defs:

> /publisher /bestGuessType /Organization.

output: 

```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Article",
  "publisher": 
     { 
       "@type": "Organization",
       "name": "QWERTYUIOPASDFGHJKLZXCVBNM"
    }
}
```

(...since publishers tend towards being organizations, although they can be people).

# Example 2: The /author of an /Article

source-data:

```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Article",
  "author": "QWERTYUIOPASDFGHJKLZXCVBNM"
}
```

schema-defs:

> /author /bestGuessType /Person.

(...since authors tend towards being people, although they can be organizations).

output:
```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Article",
  "author": 
     { 
       "@type": "Person",
       "name": "QWERTYUIOPASDFGHJKLZXCVBNM"
    }
}
```

## Notes and further work

Some notes on things to address.

### annotation-less algorithms 

Note that in the absence of the "/bestGuessType" hint from the schema definitions, it is possible to do something similar with generic techniques. Either by just using `/Thing` everywhere, or trying to walk up the (potentially multiple) supertype paths to find the nearest common super-type that covers the set of types which are declared as  `/rangeIncludes` for the property.

### Identifiers / entity resolution

Note that the default de-stringify transformation here does not attempt to assign a URI identifier or URL to the entity being introduced. In practice, certain applications might do so, e.g. in a Knowledge Graph context, a KG-specific identifier might be used.

In this case we might call this transformation something like a 
local-heuristics-destringify-transform. But it quickly grows in scope and should probably be treated as a separate issue. 

source-data:

```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Movie",
     "name": "The Black Hole",
     "brand": "The Walt Disney Company"
}
```

schema-defs:

> /brand /bestGuessType /Brand

output:
```json
{ 
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Movie",
     "name": "The Black Hole",
     "brand": 
       {
         "@id": "https://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q7414",
         "@type": "Corporation",
         "name": "The Walt Disney Company"
}
```

Note that here a sophisticated transform goes substantially above the basic approach sketched. It does a few things that exploit additional out-of-band knowledge:

 -  It figures out that the value of `/brand` here is a particular organization, and gets the ID from a KG (in this example, Wikidata).
 - Figures out the item can also be matched to a KG ID.
 - Ignores the /bestGuessType hint, which suggests the `/Brand` type, because it has matched something that is a Corporation, i.e. a particular kind of Organization.
 - It emits a more specific type, i.e. Corporation.

## Next Steps

This is a slightly strange issue compared to our usual work here. It is partly a cleanup of the underlying datamodel, but also something that ought to be implementable in software. As such I suggest we try to characterise it with unit tests that parser-extractors could be measured against.

There are also other normalizations we could imagine documenting and testing in a similar manner, such as to always use https:// or http:// schema.org URIs within some data repository. Or to normalize when we have several ways of saying the same thing (e.g. opening hours). These are out of scope for this issue, but worth bearing in mind.

For a "basic stringify" algorithm and a set of candidate `/bestGuessType` hints, it would help to understand a bit more what's out there. Which properties should be prioritized for annotation in this manner, and how can we decide which type is the best default to apply when applying the transformation?

issues.title: Add an object to represent product recalls
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
Authorities and manufacturers regularly mark products as recalled. Example of recall authorities include Rapex (EU), CPSC (USA), FDA (USA), OECD (World), Rappel Conso (France), etc. There are fundamentally two types of recalls, mandated ones (typically by some authority or government) and voluntary ones (manufacturers doing the recall preemptively). 

At the core, a recall would have three properties:

* A product being recalled
* A organization ordering the recall (either some authority or the owning brand/manufacturer).
* A recall type (voluntary or mandatory)

One way to do this would be extend creative work and use `publisher` for the entity ordering the recall, maybe use the `about` property for the product?

issues.title: Add a mechanism to support product certifications
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
Many objects can bear some form of certification, Organizations can be ISO certified, Food products can be Organic or Vegan, a person can be a certified professional. There are certifications for many domains: regulatory, organizational, recycling, food, efficiency, educational, ecological, etc. 

Certifications can be first party (the certification authority makes the claim), second-party (an authorized party makes the claim), or self-certification (recipient of the certification makes the claim). Some certifications have a unique identifier, for instance the FSC (Forest Stewardship Council). 

Some schema.org objects have support for some specific certifications, for instance `Product` has `hasEnergyConsumptionDetails`, `Person` and `Organization` have `hasCredential`, but these are very specific. Adding specific attributes for all possible certification is not feasible. 

A certification would be an object with the following properties:

* A certification unique identifier
* A certification authority
* A certifying organization (for second party)
* A certification measurement (energy efficiency, CO² emissions). 
* The object of the certification (could be `about`). 

Certification could descend from `CreativeWork`

issues.title: EventStatusType
issues.author: pbuttigieg
issues.body:
Hi all, 

In some of our implementation work for Ocean InfoHub  / ODIS, we'd like to express Events that are yet to happen (use case: planned expeditions https://github.com/iodepo/odis-arch/issues/151 and planned samplings https://github.com/iodepo/odis-arch/issues/156 (lots to clean up in those, but the idea is there). 

To express that the Event is planned, but hasn't / isn't happened / happening, would it be sensible to extend the enumeration of https://schema.org/EventStatusType to include "Planned" or similar? 

EventScheduled may be fine, however, the wording in the def is a little ambiguous: 
> The event is taking place or has taken place on the startDate as scheduled.

the "is" could be read as applying to the future as well as the present, but could also be read as applying only to the present - but we're not sure.  We're defaulting to this value for now. 

If this value applies to both planned and ongoing events, we propose a wording change to:
>The event is expected to take place, is taking place, or has taken place on the startDate as scheduled.

issues.title: Common base class for EducationalOccupationalProgam and Course
issues.author: knoan
issues.body:
I'm leveraging [EducationalOccupationalProgam](https://schema.org/EducationalOccupationalProgram) and [Course](https://schema.org/Course) to model the aggregate educational offer of a European University Alliance.

In the process I noticed that the two classes share a number of properties that could be conveniently factored to a common base class (something like `EducationalOffer` or `EducationalActivity`), e.g.

- [provider](https://schema.org/provider)
- [numberOfCredits](https://schema.org/numberOfCredits)
- [educationalCredentialAwarded](https://schema.org/educationalCredentialAwarded)
- [occupationalCredentialAwarded](https://schema.org/occupationalCredentialAwarded)

Other pairs of properties share a similar semantics and could be also merged/factored, e.g.:

| **EducationalOccupationalProgram**                           | **Course**                                                   |
| ------------------------------------------------------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| [timeToComplete](https://schema.org/timeToComplete)          | [timeRequired](https://schema.org/timeRequired)              |
| [programPrerequisites](https://schema.org/programPrerequisites) | [coursePrerequisites](https://schema.org/coursePrerequisites) |

Other properties currently specified only for `Course` could be considered for factoring, e.g.:

- [educationalLevel](https://schema.org/educationalLevel)
- [inLanguage](https://schema.org/inLanguage)

The availability of a common base class would improve semantics and reduce documentation/coding efforts.

issues.title: Adding DefinedTerm as range for properties expecting also a URL or PropertyValue or Text (if it corresponds to a standard)
issues.author: ljgarcia
issues.body:
In [Bioschemas](https://bioschemas.org/), it has become a common practice to use DefinedTerm whenever possible (e.g., to avoid ambiguity, increase interoperability). However, DefinedTerm is not always an option as it is not listed within the expected types for the range of a given property. 

A specific case is [measurementTechnique](https://schema.org/measurementTechnique). Some of the examples used for that property could be found in well-known ontologies, i.e., DefinedTerm would be ideal in those cases. How can we get DefinedTerm added as a range for [measurementTechnique](https://schema.org/measurementTechnique)?

More in general, properties with ranges such as URL, PropertyValue and Text (when its use suggests a standard or enumeration) could benefit from the addition of DefinedTerm to the range. How to get there?

The `Recipe` schema has:
`cookTime`

And the `HowTo` schema has:
`prepTime`

But when following a recipe, there is also `inactiveTime` where the user is not actively doing anything.  This is important to distinguish when looking at recipes.  

Examples:

- Air fried potato french fries have to soak in water for 45 minutes.
- Amish Friendship Bread has to sit for 10 days.
- Beans have to soak for 11 hours before making bean soup.
- Bourbon slush has to freeze for 4 hours before serving.

This request is to add `inactiveTime` as a property to the `Recipe` schema.

issues.title: Using the HTTPS context applies HTTP properties and classes
issues.author: wouterbeek
issues.body:
### Observation

In line with [the HTTPS/HTTP FAQ](https://schema.org/docs/faq.html#19) Triply prefers the HTTPS variant of the Schema.org vocabulary over the HTTP variant (although both are fine and supported).

However, if we reference the Schema.org remote context we can only use the HTTP variant, and not the HTTPS variant.  Specifically:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@id": "https://triplydb.com/DBpedia-association/dbpedia",
  "@type": "Dataset"
}
```

results in:

```turtle
<https://triplydb.com/DBpedia-association/dbpedia> a <http://schema.org/Dataset>.
```

^ Notice that the HTTP variant of the class is applied, not the HTTPS variant.

[Live run in the JSON-LD Playground](https://tinyurl.com/2s3def43)

### Expected

Specifying the HTTPS remote context to result in applying the HTTPS variants of the properties and classes.

issues.title: Course related proposals
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
Context: Passing this along from Google colleagues who have been working with web data that uses current Course schema. The suggestions are based on a desire to be able to do more with this kind of data.

# Proposal

1. Course-related properties: 

Property name in Schema.org | Description | Appears on Type | Expected Type
-- | -- | -- | --
syllabusSections | Syllabus that lays out what each section of the course will cover. | Course | Syllabus [new]
courseLength | Represents the length and pace of the course. | CourseInstance | Schedule
skills | Skills the course can help users obtain. | Course,Occupation,JobPosting | Text,DefinedTerm
totalHistoricalEnrollment | The total number of students that have enrolled in the history of the course. | Course | Integer
financialAidEligible | Any scholarships, special payment plans, or other financial aid opportunities for users looking to take the course. | Course,EducationalOccupationalProgram | Text,DefinedTerm
availableLanguage | Subtitles, closed captions, or other languages the course is offered in. | Course | Text

2. A Syllabus type

Definition: “ A syllabus that describes the material covered in a course”

3. Syllabus properties

Typical properties (none new to Schema.org):

Property name in Schema.org | Description | Appears on Type
-- | -- | --
schema.org/name | Title of a specific syllabus section. | schema.org/Syllabus
schema.org/description | Description of a specific syllabus section. | schema.org/Syllabus
schema.org/timeRequired | Expected duration for a specific syllabus section. | schema.org/Syllabus

```

issues.title: schemaorg.owl releases since 3.9 uses typo'd term "xsd:dat"
issues.author: ajnelson-nist
issues.body:
[This line](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/15.0/schemaorg.owl#L9) in schemaorg.owl version 15.0 should use `http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#date`.  `dat` is not one of the [XML Schema datatypes](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#built-in-primitive-datatypes) (primitive or derived).  A `grep` shows this typo seems to have been present since release 3.9.

This can cause a runtime error in tools that consider certain namespaces to have a closed membership set, such as the XML Schema datatypes (i.e. the tool does typo checks for standard IRIs).

Can this typo be corrected for the next release?

issues.title: schemaorg.owl "attendee" property erroneously expanded range from RDFS definition
issues.author: ajnelson-nist
issues.body:
[These lines](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/15.0/schemaorg.owl#L8769-L8791) in schemaorg.owl version 15.0 show five members in the `rdfs:range` of the `owl:ObjectProperty` `schema:attendee`.

[These lines](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/15.0/schemaorg-all-http.rdf#L8656-L8662) show two members in the `schema:rangeIncludes` of the `rdf:Property` `schema:attendee`.

This appears to be a bug in the system that converts the RDF schema to the OWL ontology.  `property:attendee` came up in discussion on an unrelated issue.  But, I compared these two queries' results, and found between the two files, there are 5,167 property:class-in-range associations in the OWL render, and 1,997 property:class-in-range associations in the RDF schema.  I found no pairs in the RDF schema that were not in the OWL render.

```sparql
PREFIX owl: <http://www.w3.org/2002/07/owl#>
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
SELECT ?nProperty ?nRangeMember
WHERE {
  ?nProperty rdfs:range / owl:unionOf / rdf:rest* / rdf:first ?nRangeMember .
}
```

```sparql
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX schema: <https://schema.org/>
SELECT ?nProperty ?nRangeMember
WHERE {
  ?nProperty schema:rangeIncludes ?nRangeMember .
}
```

issues.title: Markup errors in AggregateOffer examples
issues.author: jvandriel
issues.body:
The https://schema.org/AggregateOffer markup examples contain a couple of errors:
```
"offers": {
    "@type": "AggregateOffer",
    "highPrice": "$1495",
    "lowPrice": "$1250",
    "offerCount": "8",
```
and

```
"offers": {
    "@type": "AggregateOffer",
    "lowPrice": "$35",
    "offerCount": "1938"
```

In both case there's a price currency symbol in the pricing values. Providing number values and adding a `priceCurrency` property instead would be better. Secondly in JSON-LD `Number` values should be without double quotes.
```
"offers": {
    "@type": "AggregateOffer",
    "priceCurrency": "USD",
    "highPrice": 1495,
    "lowPrice": 1250,
```
And the second example only has a `lowPrice`. Since there's no `highPrice` it'd be better to use `price` instead.

```
"offers": {
    "@type": "AggregateOffer",
    "priceCurrency": "USD",
    "price": 35,
    "offerCount": 1938
```

issues.title: [Workflow simplification] Is pending.schema.org/pending.webschemas.org still used for documentation?
issues.author: epaulson
issues.body:
I am a bit confused by the ['How We Work'](https://schema.org/docs/howwework.html) page and what I deployed to the web, so I wonder if either I'm missing something or if the state of things are nowadays perhaps a bit different than how things used to work, but I don't get what is different on pending.schema.org these days and was hoping someone could clarify. 

As a hypothetical, let's say we wanted to extend Trip to yet another class of trip, this time for Space trips. I'd make an issue (let's 9999) and we'd talk about it, and decide it's a good idea, and someone would make a pull request to add a file as data/ext/pending/issue-9999.ttl with some new turtle and refine that as a community for a while, iterating on the PR.

At some point folks come to consensus and that PR gets merged into the main repo, still with the ttl file as an standalone small fragment living in data/ext/pending/issue-9999.ttl. (This is where another trip extension seems to be at, boattrip from issue 1755)

However, just because it's been merged into the tree hosted at github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg doesn't mean that it's entirely ready to go, and it might stay as a 'pending' item for a couple of releases, e.g. maybe for a year or two - it's part of the 'pending' set of classes and properties in schema.org - we'd have a triple inside of issue-9999.ttl it says thats SpaceTrip `:isPartOf <https://pending.schema.org>`

but once issue-9999.ttl is merged into the tree at github.com.schemaorg/schemaorg, new runs of buildsite.py will pick it up, because that script looks for all .ttl files in data/ and in data/ext/*/*.ttl

This is where I get a little confused - BoatTrip from issue-1755 shows up in the schema.org documentation as https://schema.org/BoatTrip - it's clearly marked as being 'pending' and the ttl that defines it is in data/ext/pending/ and not in data/schema.ttl but the 'How we work' makes it sound like it should only be on https://pending.schema.org/BoatTrip for documentation

I also see BoatTrip in https://schema.org/version/latest/schemaorg-current-https.ttl in the main namespace, though again with an isPartOf pending triple to at least let folks know that it might not become "official"

I haven't exhaustively dug through it, but it does look like pending.schema.org and schema.org have the same content? Maybe in the past that was different?

Some day data/ext/pending/issue-1755.ttl will get deleted and those triples will get moved into data/schema.ttl at which point 'boattrip' will cease to be pending - but I think the only changes that will be noticeable will be a slight change to the documentation that shows up on schema.org/BoatTrip and the 'isPartOf <https://pending.schema.org>' triple will get dropped. 
 
(I also get that webschemas.org is more of a 'nightly build' of schema.org releases - v15 came out in Oct of 2022, it looks like maybe v16 is forthcoming sometime in early summer 2023 - if we had gotten 'SpaceTrip' merged into the schemaorg/schemaorg tree in say December of 2022, you could find it online in https://webschemas.org/SpaceTrip without having to wait 6 months for the next regular release of schema.org - but you shouldn't rely on it because it could get yanked out the next release gets blessed and moved onto schema.org)

issues.title: sameAs: Update example to use the Wikidata URI
issues.author: fjjulien
issues.body:
In the documentation, the example for the property [sameAs](https://schema.org/sameAs) is "utilising Wikidata as a source of URIs for entities in a sameAs relationship." Wikidata sure is a great source for sameAs relationships. However, the examples provided use the Wikidata the URL format rather than the URI format.

Current example: 
`https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q836821`

Correct URI format:
`http://www.wikidata.org/entity/Q836821`

While this make no difference for humans, it does make a difference for machines.

I acknowledge that the Wikidata URI is not easily visible nor accessible to human users (one has to right click on the link "Concept URI" and then copy the link), but that's besides the point. If we want Schema to generate reusable data, we should set the example by using a proper URI in our examples.

issues.title: Solving for Spamming of Dataset Provenance
issues.author: icy-td
issues.body:
The page ecb929(dot)com(slash)clinton-body-count-spreadsheet (URL has be obfuscated) is a scraped, corrupted version of tesladeaths.com that sports an equally fraudulent version of the site's dataset structured data. Because of the scraped and doctored structured data, the spam site apparently hijacked the provenance of the dataset and influenced the Google Dataset Search: https://datasetsearch.research.google.com/search?src=3&query=tesla%20deaths&docid=L2cvMTF0X3Q0a3dwcg%3D%3D . "Tesla Lethality Dataset" is **not** the canonical version.

Besides attempting to alert Google about the spam site (which hasn't helped at all) I want to propose adding a new, negative property. Ideally, the property would indicate that a dataset, a website, any creativework is distinct from some provided URL and that the provided URL is spam. I recognize that disambiguatingDescription exists, but also that it is description-based and unlikely to be useful for crawlers, etc. Ideas welcome.

issues.title: Bug: `startTime` does not accept durations
issues.author: Seirdy
issues.body:
The [schema.org documentation for `startTime`](https://schema.org/startTime) states:

> For media, including audio and video, it's the time offset of the start of a clip within a larger file.

A time offset is a duration, not a date. The acceptable types for `startTime` are `DateTime` and `Time`; `Duration` is not an acceptable format.

[This page is a live example that triggers an error in the structured data linter](https://seirdy.one/notes/2022/05/29/soulless-pride/). I used Microdata to annotate a `time` element with `startTime` for a `VideoObject`, adding an ISO 8601/HTML5 duration to the `datetime` attribute. The error reads:

```
property schemas:startTime: Object "PT38M30S"^^<http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema#duration> not compatible with rangeIncludes (schemas:DateTime,schemas:Time) 
```

This is a specific instance of [issue 53](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/53).

issues.title: Description inconsistency in `addressCountry` property
issues.author: miller79

The description for the `addressCountry` property currently says "The country. For example, USA. You can also provide the two-letter [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1)."

As you can see, the example is using [ISO 3166-1 alpha-3](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1_alpha-3) but it then says you can provide a [ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code](http://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO_3166-1). This feels like it was more than likely a mistake and should have either all been the alpha-2 or all be alpha-3 or potentially support both.

The selection should be clearer and match the example.

issues.title: Revisiting parentItem
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
This is an extension of https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/851 because that issue seems to be closed/old.

The current state that left off was "Comment parentItem Comment".  This still doesn't make full sense because "CreativeWork comment Comment" is essentially the inverse edge of this (I don't know if that was the intention but it's very close semantically).  If the top level item that the comment is attached to is not a Question/Answer (let's say a DiscussionForumPosting or a VideoObject or something), there's no way to specify it.

I am proposing expanding the range of parentItem to be CreativeWork.

issues.title: sharedContent on Comment
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
For many online forums, a comment on an original post is nearly as extensive of a semantic type as the post itself.  Honestly, I think the whole Question/Answer/Comment hierarchy should probably be revisited with it's association with SocialMediaPosting (and DiscussionForumPosting).

But the immediate problem that I've seen with forums not knowing what to do is how to represent shared links in the context of replies (or even Question/Answers for that matter).  sharedContent is a field on SocialMediaPosting but not on Question or Answer (which is used on a lot of QA forums) or on Comment.

To solve that, I'm proposing **expanding the domain of sharedContent to include Comment as well**.  I think there may be better overall solutions, but that is the simplest thing that will unstick a bunch of representational problems.

issues.title: extend the domain and range of `specialty`
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
Currently [specialty](https://schema.org/specialty) is IMHO deficient:
- Range is [Specialty](https://schema.org/Specialty) but that's an enumeration with only one branch [MedicalSpecialty](https://schema.org/MedicalSpecialty). At least `URL` should be added to allow other domains
- Domain is [WebPage](https://schema.org/WebPage)
  - Why is it so limited, given that `Specialty` is defined as "Any branch of a field in which **people** typically develop specific expertise, usually after significant study, time, and effort."?
  - Extend the range to include at least `Person, Organization`

[medicalSpecialty](https://schema.org/medicalSpecialty) and [relevantSpecialty](https://schema.org/relevantSpecialty) are a bit better defined (eg the former also applies to [MedicalOrganization](https://schema.org/MedicalOrganization)  and [Physician](https://schema.org/Physician)). But they are limited to the Medical domain and have other defects.

issues.title: Defects of `medicalSpecialty, relevantSpecialty, MedicalEntity`
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
I don't see why [medicalSpecialty](https://schema.org/medicalSpecialty) and [relevantSpecialty](https://schema.org/relevantSpecialty) are needed: why can't we use simply [specialty](https://schema.org/specialty) (after #3379 is fixed?)

Conceptually, these are sub-props of `specialty` even though they are not declared so.
But creating sub-props just to restrict their domain/range to sub-classes is not a good idea because this proliferates props needlessly.

Furthermore:
- [MedicalEntity](https://schema.org/MedicalEntity) is unnecessary. Schema.org shuns abstract classes (eg `Agent` as superclass of `Person, Organization` was rejected after much discussion), so why has it accepted this one? "The most generic type of entity related to health and the practice of medicine" is ontologically unsound: why would you put syringes, nurses, eyes and ophtalmology in the same class?
- `relevantSpecialty` pollutes the global namespace since its name doesn't show it's related to the medical domain
- if `relevantSpecialty` is a relevant specialty, then is `specialty` an **irrlelevant specialty**?

issues.title: extend the domain and range of `skills`
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
Currently `skills` applies only to `JobPosting, Occupation`. IMHO it should also apply to `Person, Organziation`:
- To fill a posting, the Person must have the requisite skills: so it should be possible to record this against the person
- Similar for an org: it may possess collective skills being the sum of its employee's skills, or its own "emergent" skills

issues.title: add concept hierarchy property to DefinedTerm
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
https://schema.org/DefinedTerm lacks properties to make a concept hierarchy (eg like `skos:broader, narrower`).

Hierarchical structure is a crucial feature of thesauri, eg to enable query expansion in semantic search.

We're building the Ontotext Knowledge Graph and using schema.org (with a couple of custom additions).
But this omission prevents us from using DefinedTerm, and instead we use skos:Concept.

issues.title: Schema.org should have at least basic expressivity helping sites declare generative AI technologies were used
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
We should initiate activities in this area, move quickly to reflect the speed with which AI technologies are developing and being deployed, and do so incrementally and in a way that can be composed usefully with other aspects of schema.org.

This proposal that has several sources - I've been talking with members of the factchecking community regularly since we added ClaimReview and related terms. While we developed MediaReview, it doesn't directly go very deep into the fast growing generative AI world. Meanwhile, Schema.org also added https://schema.org/acquireLicensePage a few years ago, which enables a landing page about a media object to provide helpful metadata pointing to ways of licensing that content. Google (see [their docs](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/image-license-metadata)) and others can use both in-page schema markup, and within-the-image-file metadata, which most often uses IPTC fields. In practice it has proved useful for content publishers to be able to add markup via HTML rather than by reprocessing 1000s of images. This is likely to be also true for genAI content publishing sites.

Alongside all this, the most basic metadata task, describing who made something, and how, remains an undersolved problem. It should be easier (and/or better documented) to do things like list authors, list them in order (this is materially important to many in academia), and list their roles from a wider pallete of known role types. Last time we touched the Role aspect of the problem we introduced a very very general mechanism which has proved both unpopular and largely (but not entirely) unused. It will take some careful work to untangle that. We should also not rush a design that says "made with AI" without thinking through the different classes of tool that are appearing (accessibility and inclusiveness tools, simple visual filters, and prompt/LLM-based mechanisms). We will also need to distinguish the case where entire works are heavily AI-powered (eg. a fake essay) from those which feature items (like photos) in a less controversial manner, or which discuss them criticially - e.g. a fact check.

Some but not all of these issues are being discussed elsewhere, and implemented elsewhere.

As a first step, we can reflect into the Schema.org namespace a semi-external extension drawing from the relatively short list of codes assigned at IPTC. While they don't address all the issues above, the ability to use simple (as simple as we can make it) Schema markup as an alternative to within-the-image-file embedded metadata is of immediate value. I'll file a separate ticket for that work. This can be done primarily as an Enumeration type with the potential for other approaches to use other subtypes alongside it in the hierarchy. We'll want a basic way of linking it into a description of MediaObject too.

issues.title: Create an enumeration that echos the IPTC synthetic media codes, plus a property pointing to it
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
As a task within workarea #3391, we should have a schema.org native enumeration matching the codes standardized at IPTC for synthetic media. Also a property to use them on a MediaObject.

IPTC docs:
 * https://www.iptc.org/std/photometadata/documentation/userguide/
 * https://www.iptc.org/std/photometadata/documentation/userguide/#_about_the_iptc_photo_metadata_user_guide
 * https://iptc.org/news/iptc-releases-draft-of-digital-source-type-vocabulary-to-support-synthetic-media/


See https://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/ for details. Here's a copy of their current wording format for one term, see link for full version:

```
Concept ID (QCode) = digsrctype:positiveFilm, ID (URI) = http://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/positiveFilm
--
Type: cpnat:abstract | created: 2008-01-01T01:00:00+00:00 | modified: 2010-12-15T21:54:47+00:00 | retired:
Name(en-GB): Digitised from a positive on film
Definition(en-GB): The digital image was digitised from a positive on a transparency or any other transparent medium
Member of scheme: http://cv.iptc.org/newscodes/digitalsourcetype/
```

As always there is the question of adapting vs leaving unchanged when bringing in external mappings. Having tried some variations, I propose this:

 * DigitalCaptureDigitalSource
 * NegativeFilmDigitalSource
 * PositiveFilmDigitalSource
 * PrintDigitalSource
 * MinorHumanEditsDigitalSource
 * CompositeCaptureDigitalSource
 * AlgorithmicallyEnhancedDigitalSource
 * DataDrivenMediaDigitalSource
 * DigitalArtDigitalSource
 * VirtualRecordingDigitalSource
 * CompositeSyntheticDigitalSource
 * TrainedAlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource
 * CompositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource
* AlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource

All of these within IPTCDigitalSource which is a subtype of (for now, we can add more and more structure) MediaEnumeration. I will also move the MediaReview enumeration beneath there.

To reference this list, for now we can simply use a digitalSource property. Other designs could reference these, or these plus others, in more ambitious ways. Note that in schema.org we never write enumeration types, enumeration members or anything else but properties using an initial lower case letter. This is why "print" becomes "PrintDigitalSource". The "DigitalSource" also stops us "using up" very general terms when we mean something quite specific. This is more of an issue for us at Schema.org since we do not use explicit sub-namespacing mechanisms, whereas at IPTC these terms are within an area already scoped to "digital source types".

issues.title: Schema.org/Recipe AggregateRating should require associated written reviews
issues.author: AdamGal18
issues.body:
Schema.org/Recipe documentation should be updated to require that ratings/reviews that are added to the aggregaterating (star rating) for recipes are required to have an associated written review. 

**Rational For Schema.org/Recipe Disallowing Anonymous Reviews**

Highly trafficked recipe websites (Many top 50 food websites by traffic) are using Schema.org/Recipe to mislead users into giving recipes a 5-star rating with one simple click since anonymous reviews are allowed per the current Schema.org/Recipe documentation. 

**Popular Plugin Collecting Anonymous Reviews on Large Food Websites**

An extremely popular Wordpress recipe plugin ([WP Recipe Maker](https://help.bootstrapped.ventures/article/27-user-ratings)) allows anonymous non logged in 5-star reviews with no associated text review. On average, for every one written review there are 4-8 anonymous reviews collected. This is done, simply by counting the reviews written on the page vs hidden 5 star anonymous reviews. Users are forced to leave a written review for a rating of 4-1. This is not clear to users at first glance, and many users may accidentally save a 5-star vote without intending to do so. The fact that the star hover system only take users to the comments section if they hover and click on 4 or less stars makes it very misleading. This is because it implies that the comments section is only for negative reviews. In reality, the comments section can and should be used for both positive and negative schema reviews.

**Here are some specific examples of how this practice uses Schema.org/Recipe aggregaterating to mislead users:**

* Users trust the schema aggregate rating in Google search results. Users click the higher reviewed websites. When the user visits the site the number of reviews written doesn't match what they clicked on. 
* A user may be quickly scrolling through the recipe page and accidentally hover over the stars, saving a 5-star vote without intending to do so.
* A user may be thinking that the stars are a way to navigate to the comment section of the website. A common website design used for many review based recipe websites among other review website types. 
* A user may be hesitant to leave a negative review, especially if they are not sure how to do so. The fact that the stars only take users to the comments section if they hover over 4 or less stars may make users think that negative reviews are not welcome.
* In general, anonymous single click ratings cause extreme aggregaterating inflation. 

**Public Perception** 

This practice is eroding Schema.org/Recipe's trust as a useful schema in Google search. Anonymous reviews are causing most of the inflation since they can't be accounted for on the recipe page. [Danny Sullivan even responded](https://twitter.com/searchliaison/status/1720519486825230381) saying that he is lobbying to remove Schema.org/Recipe reviews from search results because they are easy to inflate.
