issues.title: Reopening a discussion on representing user accounts
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
At Google we are starting to release more guidelines for conveying creator/author/person information but the lack of a type for account makes the markup awkward.

There has been previous discussion for something like a user account or social profile account or whatever we want to scope it (see https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/267).  There is no representation AFAIK for something like that in schema.org.  Representationally this leads to problems figuring out how to represent domain-specific information that is separate from the real-world person that the account/profile represents.  Some examples:

- How do we represent when a profile was created?  That's not when the person was created.  At Google we are recommending hanging that on a ProfilePage node (so the page implicitly is created when the account is created) but that is not ideal.
- Naming is confusing distinguishing between a system handle and a real world name.  There is little specification for whether name (or alternateName) represents the canonical representation of the thing in its system context or something more objective.
- Ambiguity in entity type.  Some systems cannot tell whether something is a Person or Organization and yet many of our author properties have to use a specific type to be valid.

issues.title: 'Decision' missing as Schema type?
issues.author: romjansen
issues.body:
Whereas there is a type for legislation, there currently is no type for decisions. This is unfortunate because public authorities, ranging from municipalities to regulatory agencies and the judiciary, are increasingly publishing their decisions online. Moreover, similar to the ELI initiative, the European Union is rolling out the ECLI standard for its (supra)national judicial decisions. Several national jurisdictions are also looking into further metadata standards, but these shouldn't be to different from what is already supported under Legislation and Creative Works.

Concluding; it would be nice if there was a Shema type 'decision' with subtypes such as 'administrative decision', 'judicial decision' and 'arbitral decision'.

issues.title: Suggestion for New Schema Property - "workedAt"
issues.author: WilkoMarketing
issues.body:
Hi Schema.org Team,
I am writing to suggest the introduction of a new schema property, which I believe could significantly enhance the utility and specificity of data markup regarding professional experiences. The proposed property is titled "workedAt." 

The current schema.org vocabulary includes properties like "worksFor" and "alumniOf," which are immensely useful. However, there is a noticeable gap when it comes to representing an individual's past employment at an organization, particularly when the organization is not an educational institution.

Suggested Property: workedAt
Purpose: To denote a past employment relationship between a person and an organization.
Applicability: This would be especially useful for individuals who have significant professional histories, allowing them to indicate previous employers that have contributed to their career development.
Flexibility: It could be designed to include additional information such as the duration of employment, the role held, and the department or division within the organization.

Implementing "workedAt" would provide a more comprehensive framework for individuals to present their professional journey, especially on digital platforms like LinkedIn, online resumes, or personal websites. It also aligns with the evolving nature of modern careers, where changes in employment are frequent and formative experiences.
I believe the introduction of "workedAt" would be a valuable addition to the Schema.org vocabulary, offering a nuanced way to represent professional histories and affiliations beyond current roles or educational alumni status.

Thank you for considering this suggestion. I look forward to any thoughts or feedback you might have on this proposal.
Best regards!

issues.title: Add second-level administrative division to PostalAddress
issues.author: FilippoVigani
issues.body:
Currently [addressRegion](https://schema.org/addressRegion) should be used for the "region" in which the locality of an address is. For the United States, it's the state, for other countries it should contain a first-level administrative division, as specified by it description: 

> The region in which the locality is, and which is in the country. For example, California or another appropriate first-level [Administrative division](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_administrative_divisions_by_country).

Often it is required to store information about second-level administrative division, for instance a county in the US or a Provincia in Italy. We currently lack a term for that in the schema.org dictionary.

As for third-level administrative division, usually it encompasses cities, towns, etc, so I imagine the proper term to use is `addressLocality`, which makes it very clear that we are lacking a term for the second-level.

I'm not sure what term would be appropriate, but to be fair using `addressRegion` as first-level administrative division isn't very clear, as technically there are countries where their "regions" are considered second-level divisions. At the same time using something like `addressProvince` for second-level divisions isn't great, as there are many countries where a "province" is the first-level. Maybe we should steer away from such names and use "administrative divisions" with different levels, the same way [Google APIs structure](https://developers.google.com/maps/documentation/geocoding/requests-geocoding#Types) their data?

issues.title: cleanup Physician per #806 to clarify that a physician is not a place, adding /usNPI identifiers
issues.author: danbri
issues.body:
We have a longstanding issue (partially cleaned in #806) due to the choice of naming for the type Physician, which represents "a doctor's office" and has a variety of supertypes:

* [Thing](https://schema.org/Thing) > [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) > [LocalBusiness](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) > [MedicalBusiness](https://schema.org/MedicalBusiness) > [Physician](https://schema.org/Physician)
* [Thing](https://schema.org/Thing) > [Place](https://schema.org/Place) > [LocalBusiness](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) > [MedicalBusiness](https://schema.org/MedicalBusiness) > [Physician](https://schema.org/Physician)
* [Thing](https://schema.org/Thing) > [Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) > [MedicalOrganization](https://schema.org/MedicalOrganization) > [Physician](https://schema.org/Physician)

The current poor typing as a LocalBusiness (via MedicalBusiness) brings in the subtype of Place. In #806 we decoupled MedicalOrganization from this hierarchy (although note that such organizations can have an address). We should continue this cleanup by removing the assertion that a Physician is a MedicalBusiness, leaving it typed just as a MedicalOrganization. For association with places we can draw attention to the [address](https://schema.org/address) and [hospitalAffiliation](https://schema.org/hospitalAffiliation) properties, with potential to add /practicesAt for more specificity and to cover clinics etc.

# Changes

1.) remove: Physician subClassOf LocalBusiness.

2.) Reword definition. Instead of "A physician's office", something like:
 
> An individual physician, considered as a [[MedicalOrganization]]. For their official address use [[address], for affiliations to hospitals use [[hospitalAffiliation]]. The (*todo*) [[practicesAt]] property can be used to indicate [[MedicalOrganization]] hospitals, clinkics, pharmacies etc. where this physician practices. If there is a need to describe the physician as a [[Person]], the [[founder]] property can be used.

3.) add /usNPI, a /Property whose value is /Text (using /Number doesn't add much here); domainIncludes /Physician.

> A US [NPI](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Provider_Identifier) (National Provider Number) is a unique 10-digit identification number issued to health care providers in the US.

4.) Add /practicesAt, a /Property whose value is a /MedicalOrganization; domainIncludes /Physician.

Definition:
> Indicates a medical organization where this physician practices.

issues.title: Add a new property to support color swatches
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org [Product](https://schema.org/Offer) markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand the colors of products sold online.

**Proposal** - Schema.org supports the specification of product colors through property [color](https://schema.org/color) of type [Text](https://schema.org/Text). A disadvantage of only allowing a free-form textual description of a color is that it provides a lot of room for interpretation. For example "Charcoal" and "Ash" are both shades of the color Gray, but it is hard for a user to understand the difference just based on the textual description. Many popular apparel websites therefore show a color swatch image together with the color name to allow the user to visualize the color of a product variant. 

Given the common use of color swatches in the industry we propose to add a new _colorSwatch_ property as sub-property of [image](https://schema.org/image) with values of type [URL](https://schema.org/URL) or [ImageObject](https://schema.org/ImageObject).

However, the `recipeInstructions` properties point to `HowToStep`s without any `position` or `nextItem` properties that could establish an order for the instructions. As https://schema.org/itemListElement says, "The order of elements in your mark-up is not sufficient for indicating the order [of] elements. Use ListItem with a 'position' property in such cases.". A recipe's steps need to be followed in order, so this should cause a validation error.

This recipe page is just one of many that make this mistake. The mistake might be in the majority of recipes on the internet, since without Google telling them about the mistake, they have no way to notice.

issues.title: new properties for Things? DigitalEntity and MaterialEntity
issues.author: wouteraddink
issues.body:
Natural history museums preserve material objects (specimens) from nature. These are digitally catalogued and further digitized for science. The catalogued items on the internet we would like to make better findable using schema.org. I am new on this platform so forgive my ignorance but I struggle to find the right property for these objects. Specimens are things but not products and not creative works either. The same applies to material samples for e.g. DNA analysis.

Maybe a new property should be added to schema.org like **MaterialEntity**?

In our biodiversity informatics domain we are now also starting to create new digital objects as digital twins for these material objects. These have PIDs and contain all digital information known about the physical object.  We call these Digital Specimens. These could perhaps be seen as CreativeWork but are rather just a collection of facts and measurements, there is no creativity involved. They could perhaps be seen as Dataset under CreativeWork but are rather structured data objects (similar to a database record) where a collection of such objects would usually be treated as a dataset.

To support **digital twins** (e.g. to run simulations) such as our digital specimens but also digital twins used in industry, maybe another new property should be added as well, which could be **DigitalEntity**. 

A possible issue with that may be that a digital media could both be a digital entity and a creative work. If it is the result of a scanning device we do not see it as creative work (at least not in our domain), but if it is a digital photo created by a professional photographer it would be a creative work. That would leave the question though which property to use for a digital media file created by e.g. a scanning device that is published online. Or should **Intangible** be used for digital twins and digital media that are not creative works?

Note that we plan to use DOIs as PIDs for our digital specimens and this is relevant for the DOI Foundation too, which is currently revising their schema and could base their referentType on the schema.org properties for Thing. They already have the issue that they now need to support DOIs for both physical and digital entities. 

Note also that GBIF, the Global Biodiversity Information Facility which deals with occurrences, is working on a new data model/standard that includes digital and material entities and connects these with taxon.

issues.title: add property `oid`
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
@danbri and @alex-jansen:

https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/2915 added https://schema.org/iso6523Code (see that issue and https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_6523 for a description).

However, ISO 6523 is just the `1.3` branch of the ITU/ISO/IEC object ID (`oid`) hierarchy. See https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_identifier and https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P3743.

OIDs can be browsed and resolved at http://oid-info.com/, eg http://oid-info.com/get/1.3.60 is DUNS.

OID can also be used as URN, eg `urn:oid:1.3.60`. 
We could even use this as a property (not that I'd recommend it), and eg declare:
```ttl
s:duns owl:equivalentProperty urn:oid:1.3.60.
s:leiCode owl:equivalentProperty urn:oid:1.3.199.
# CAGE is urn:oid:1.3.141
```
Now consider https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q7095072 Ontotext and its DUNS "053393007" and CAGE "6H8F4".
We could express them as the following alternatives (assuming that ":" is used as a separator):
```ttl
<https://kg.ontotext.com/resource/agent/ontotext> a s:Organization;
  s:duns "053393007"; s:iso6523Code "60:053393007"; s:oid "1.3.60:053393007"; urn:oid:1.3.60 "053393007";
  s:iso6523Code "141:6H8F4"; s:oid "1.3.141:6H8F4"; urn:oid:1.3.141 "6H8F4";
```

---
Here's a proposed definition:

```ttl
s:oid a rdf:Property;
  rdfs:label "object id";
  rdfs:comment """
ITU/ISO/IEC object identifier as per ITU X.660 standard.
Can be used for organizations, registered companies, locations (GS1 GLN), goods (GS1 GTIN), banks, ATMs, application layer protocols, IP address registrants, file & document formats, information objects, local/remote procedures, etc etc.
`oid` uses a dotted numeric notation that represents a tree of values, eg `1.3.6.1.4.1` represents IANA enterprise numbers, and `1.3.6.1.4.1.343` is Intel Corporation.
The oid `1.3` represents the ISO/IEC 6523 International Code Designator (ICD) that corresponds to the property `iso6523Code`.
ITU object IDs allow only numbers, but schema.org allows as an extension the last part to be separated by `:` and to consist of any characters.
For example, the NATO Commercial And Government Entity (NCAGE) code has oid `1.3.141`. Since "04KE8" is one of the NCAGE codes of Intel, we can use oid `1.3.141:04KE8` to represent Intel.
Standard numeric OIDs can be browsed and resolved at http://oid-info.com/, eg http://oid-info.com/get/1.3.141 is NCAGE.
OIDs can also be used as URNs, e.g. `urn:oid:1.3.141` can represent the NCAGE property, and `1.3.141:04KE8` can be used as a URN for Intel.
""";
  rdfs:seeAlso <https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Object_identifier>,
    <https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Property:P3743>,
    <http://oid-info.com/>.
```

There are these two sets using equal names, meaning the same,
but neither of the two links to the other:

- ***schema.org*** (`http://schema.org/`): \

- ***DC Metadata Terms*** (`http://purl.org/dc/dcam/`): \
  [dcam:domainIncludes] & [dcam:rangeIncludes]

If deemed inappropriate, some other kind of reference should exist,
to prevent confusion about which to use by external ontology designers.

[schema:domainIncludes]: http://schema.org/domainIncludes
[schema:rangeIncludes]: http://schema.org/rangeIncludes
[dcam:domainIncludes]: http://purl.org/dc/dcam/domainIncludes

issues.title: Example IDs (data/ext/..) conflicts with new example IDs in data/examples.txt
issues.author: izwicky
issues.body:
# What
The example IDs are globally registered, thus creating conflicts with newly added example IDs in `data/examples.txt`. This conflict makes the build fail and abort the process. Thus it's not possible to build.

# Why
The `data/examples.txt` has a sequential ID structure and in order to keep it organized, all IDs need to be documented there and not spread out between `data/examples.txt` and the examples in `data/ext/bib`, `data/ext/health-lifesci`, etc.

Further, this doesn't make it easy to track the next ID to be used.

# How
### Possible solutions:
- Update the example IDs to a number that's far from what's in production. Example: `#eg-99999` Therefore, contributors can add IDs sequentially without interfering with the examples.
- Not update the example IDs and continue the sequence from the last ID found in `data/ext/bib`, `data/ext/health-lifesci`, etc. -- This will break the sequence in `data/examples.txt` and make it harder to track IDs.

I can open a PR, but wanted to make sure that I'm not missing a detail or if there's a consensus to fix this.

issues.title: Add a digital link field to products and organizations (possibly other types).
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
# Problem

[GS1's digital link](https://www.gs1.org/standards/gs1-digital-link) (DL) is presented as the successor to the linear encoding of various identifiers like GTIN. Digital links are typically encoded in QR-codes printed on products or their packaging. 

An example of a digital link is https://gs1.appareldemo.com/01/09506000164908/10/ABC123

The path contains the following AI (Application Idenfitiers)

- 01 – GTIN `09506000164908`
- 10 – Lot number `ABC123`


The digital link solves some long standing issues with GTIN, in particular they allow to encode the Consumer Product Variants (CPV) field, which allows to distinguish products which share a GTIN, because they don't need to be distinguished in retail. Often they need to be distinguished in online commerce. 

Technically, DLs could be represented in multiple ways:

- Inside the `[identifier](https://schema.org/identifier)` field. _Pros_: no change needed. _Cons_, identifier is the grab-bag for identifiers, so this makes validation and reporting complicated. 
- Inside the `url` field.  _Pros_: no change needed. _Cons_, `url` is pretty vague, agains this makes validation and reporting vague. 
- Inside a dedicated attribute like `hasDigitalLink`. _Pros_: role and parsing rules are clear . _Cons_, new attribute needed. 


# Level and AI culling 

One problem that will require some documentation is the fact that different AIs are only applicable at certain levels. 

- A DL that contains a serial number (AI 21) should only be present on instances of [IndividualProduct](https://schema.org/IndividualProduct) 
- A DL that contains a lot number (AI 10) could make sense at the product level (if the seller only sells products from that lot), but more probably it should be a the IndividualProduct level.
- A DL that contains a global model number (AI 8013) or an NSN but no GTIN could be attached to a Product or a ProductModel.

issues.title: Support Certification rating with scale, e.g. EPREL ratings: B(A to G)
issues.author: duckladydinh
issues.body:
# Problem

[Certification](https://schema.org/Certification) has been published (requested in https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3230). However, there isn't yet an attribute in the schema to represent the rating of a certification. For example:

- EPREL certifications would have ratings in the form of `Rating(Best to Worst)`, e.g. B(A to G), C(A to G)...
- EPEAT, ENERGY STAR certifications would have textual ratings, e.g. Gold, Silver, Bronze...
- Vehicle certifications in France, Germany... would also have textual rating such as A, B, C...

Currently, we can't find a suitable attribute on [Certification](https://schema.org/Certification) to best represent it. According to the name, we think that [Certification::hasMeasurement](https://schema.org/hasMeasurement) may look like a good attribute to represent the rating BUT... it doesn't support rating with a textual scale like EPREL because it is a [QuantitativeValue](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue) with min/max values being [Number](https://schema.org/Number) rather than [Text](https://schema.org/Text).

# Proposal

Therefore, we would like to propose make [Certification::hasMeasurement](https://schema.org/hasMeasurement) a [Rating](https://schema.org/Rating) instead of a [QuantitativeValue](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue) whose best/worst value attributes can be both [Text](https://schema.org/Text). *Or maybe if you know that this property is used for something else, we can consider adding a completely new rating property to it*.

Thanks a lot

issues.title: Meta-issue: Provide guidance for proposing extensions and modifications via issue templates
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
Many users of schema.org end up in this repository because they find that the current state of the vocabulary does not fit their individual needs, e.g. missing properties, insufficient specificity, etc.

While feedback from users is essential for schema.org, such proposals often do not end up in actual extensions to the vocabulary, which creates frustration among the submitters and puts a workload on the schema.org core contributors.

It would be good to **create guidelines on (1) when and (2) how to propose changes or extensions to the vocabulary.**

This could be implemented as one or multiple [**Github issue templates**](https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository); for inspiration, see e.g. this [collection of issue templates](https://github.com/stevemao/github-issue-templates), maybe accompanied by a dedicated page in the documentation.

Here are some first ideas (maybe a bit too specific; we must not discourage users from proposing changes, of course):

## Checklist

- [ ] My proposal is about the **vocabulary,** not about problems with existing tools (like validators), the consumption of data by search engines or other applications, or the underlying syntaxes like JSON-LD, Microdata, or RDFa.
- [ ] I have read the [guidelines on naming and styling](https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html) in schema.org.
- [ ] I understand the basic conceptual model behind schema.org, namely the mechanism for domain and range.
- [ ] I am familiar with the [data types used in schema.org](https://schema.org/DataType)
- [ ] I checked the list of [existing types for values etc. (`schema:Intangible`)](https://schema.org/Intangible) and [`schema:Enumeration`](https://schema.org/Enumeration) insofar they are relevant for my proposal.
- [ ] I am familiar with the existing mechanisms for [qualitative values via `schema:QualitativeValue`](https://schema.org/QualitativeValue), [quantitative values via `schema:QuantitativeValue`](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue), and [property-value pairs defined outside of schema.org via `schema:PropertyValue`](https://schema.org/PropertyValue) insofar they are relevant for my proposal.
- [ ] I have considered the usage of external standards or numbering schemes for my proposal, e.g. via [`schema:additionalType`](https://schema.org/additionalType) or [`schema:additionalProperty`](https://schema.org/additionalProperty).

## Content

- Which applications can be expected to consume the enhanced data? (Very often, proposing an extension included the implicit expectation that major search engines will also actually use it, which will depend on many factors and take time.)
- Can you provide URLs of Web pages that contain the respective information (e.g. that would benefit from the proposed extension)? Ideally, the URLs would be from different sites.
- Did you check if the required information could be modeled with existing schema.org types and properties, e.g. with minor modifications to the text of existing definitions or by adding types to the domain or range?

issues.title: Add minimal documentation on using SHACL and ShEx for Validation
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
I just realized that there are now regularly updated SHACL and ShEx shape definitions for validating data included in each release, like 

- https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/26.0/schemaorg-shapes.shacl
- https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/26.0/schemaorg-subclasses.shacl

plus 

- the schema.org vocabulary [with http-based URIs as `schemaorg-current-http.ttl`](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/26.0/schemaorg-current-http.ttl) and [with http**s**-based URIs as `schemaorg-current-https.ttl`](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/26.0/schemaorg-current-https.ttl) and
-  [http-to-https mappings in the form of `httpequivs.ttl`](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/main/data/releases/26.0/httpequivs.ttl).

It would be great if anybody could provide a super-short how-to on how these are meant to be used, e.g. with [pySHACL](https://github.com/RDFLib/pySHACL).

1. Which degree of inferencing is needed (RDFS, OWL2-RL)?
1. Assuming we have two RDFlib graph objects, `data` and `shapes`, what is the intended workflow?

I envision something like this:

```python
import rdflib
from pyshacl import validate

# Which parts should go into the shape graph?
shape_components = [] # List of URLS
rules = rdflib.Graph()
for uri in shape_components:
    rules.parse(url, format="turtle")
# Which parts beside my data should go into the data graph?
data_components = [] # List of URLS or files
data  = rdflib.Graph()
for uri in data_components:
    data.parse(url, format="turtle")
# Which level of inferencing is expected? 
# none, rdfs, or owlrl?
status, results, text = validate(data, shacl_graph=rules, inference='none', serialize_report_graph=False)
````

But since the shape definitions reference schema-specific types, this leads to lots of violations. The http/https issue adds complexity, too.

So any help will be very much appreciated ;-)!

I am pretty sure many others would benefit.

/CC @danbri @ericprud @ashleysommer

issues.title: Consider supporting RDF-star and JSON-LD-star for temporal aspects of properties (and deprecating Role)
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
[RDF-star](https://www.ontotext.com/knowledgehub/fundamentals/what-is-rdf-star/) is a well-defined mechanism for describing the temporal aspects of a property or sets of properties (and more). There is now work on a proper specification for RDF-star in JSON-LD syntax called [JSON-LD-star](https://json-ld.github.io/json-ld-star/).

We have several properties in schema.org that are used to attach validity statements and other meta-data to an object or a related RDF node for an n-ary relationship, like [https://schema.org/validFrom](`validFrom').

I propose to consider using RDF-star as the future mechanism of choice **for validity statements and other meta-data**. 

For a detailed argument, see https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3098#issuecomment-2023333078

Required tasks:

- [ ] JSON-LD-star specification must be finalized and adopted
- [ ] Major consumers of schema.org markup must be able to process JSON-LD-star
- [ ] Decide which schema.org properties should be allowed for annotation objects 
- [ ] Update examples and guidance

issues.title: Support values of type TextObject for the name property to allow tagging of names as being AI generated
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org [Product](https://schema.org/Offer) markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand whether names are AI-generated. This extends on issues [#3391](https://github.com/schemaorg/schem) and  [#3392](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3392).

**Proposal** -
Through inheritance from [CreativeWork](https://schema.org/CreativeWork), [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject) has a property [digitalSourceType](https://schema.org/digitalSourceType), which allows specification whether a creative work (such as a [MediaObject](https://schema.org/MediaObject) or a [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject)  instance) was created using AI, e.g.,  using enumeration value [TrainedAlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource](https://schema.org/TrainedAlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource). 

Since values of type [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject) are allowed for property [description](https://schema.org/description), descriptions can be tagged as being created by AI. However, the [name](https://schema.org/name) property currently does **not** allow values of type  [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject), and can therefore not be tagged as created by AI. We propose, similar to [description](https://schema.org/description), to also allow values of type [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject)  for the [name](https://schema.org/name)  property so consuming systems can understand whether names are AI generated.

We also propose, similar to [MediaObject](https://schema.org/MediaObject), to change the description of [TextObject](https://schema.org/TextObject) to also support embedded text objects, and not just file-based text. 

A JSON-LD snippet of a name created using generative AI then looks as follows:


```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": {
     "@type": "TextObject",
     "digitalSourceType": "https://schema.org/TrainedAlgorithmicMediaDigitalSource",
     "text": "Stride & Conquer: Original Men's Blue & Orange Power Sneakers (Size 9)" 
   }
   ...
}

issues.title: Make RDF available under prefix URL
issues.author: hoijui
issues.body:
As suggested for example in: [Recommended IRI patterns for ontologies and their terms](
https://more.metadatacenter.org/recommended-iri-patterns-ontologies-and-their-terms),
It would be great if an HTTP(S) GET request on `schema.org/` (and optionally on `schema.org/SomeItem`)
with a [content-type header](https://www.geeksforgeeks.org/http-headers-content-type/) indicating any of the RDF serialization formats (for example `"text/turtle"`), would return the schema in that format.

This would make the development of tools browsing the semantic (RDF) web much easier, among other things.

An already quite elaborate version of doing this with `.htaccess` can be seen here:
https://github.com/perma-id/w3id.org/blob/master/valueflows/.htaccess

The respective content is already available here:
https://schema.org/docs/developers.html#defs

As of now, no matter which content-type is requested, one always gets HTML (without RDFa), which is not machine-readable (as RDF), and that is quite bad/unpractical.

issues.title: Many Place properties are not relevant to AdministrativeArea / City
issues.author: dr-shorthair
issues.body:
AdministrativeArea is positioned as a sub-type to Place 
While this may seem logical, many of the properties associated with Place are inappropriate and misleading for AdministrativeArea (including its sub-type City). 
In particular many Place properties are related to specific commercial activities, and really are not useful for adminstrative areas, and are highly distracting in the type description for AdministrativeArea or City: 
- [amenityFeature](https://schema.org/amenityFeature)
- [branchCode](https://schema.org/branchCode)
- [faxNumber](https://schema.org/faxNumber)
- [hasDriveThroughService](https://schema.org/hasDriveThroughService)
- [isAccessibleForFree](https://schema.org/isAccessibleForFree)
- [isicV4](https://schema.org/isicV4)
- [maximumAttendeeCapacity](https://schema.org/maximumAttendeeCapacity)
- [openingHoursSpecification](https://schema.org/openingHoursSpecification)
- [publicAccess](https://schema.org/publicAccess)
- [smokingAllowed](https://schema.org/smokingAllowed) ! 
- [specialOpeningHoursSpecification](https://schema.org/specialOpeningHoursSpecification)

Nevertheless, there are a set of properties that can usefully be associated with any Location. 
Perhaps this could be factored out, and then Place (of commercial significance) and AdministrativeArea (non-commercial) could be sibling sub-types.

v2.32.0

2.32.0 (2024-05-20)

🐍 PYCON US 2024 EDITION 🐍

Security

  • Fixed an issue where setting verify=False on the first request from a Session will cause subsequent requests to the same origin to also ignore cert verification, regardless of the value of verify. (https://github.com/psf/requests/security/advisories/GHSA-9wx4-h78v-vm56)

Improvements

  • verify=True now reuses a global SSLContext which should improve request time variance between first and subsequent requests. It should also minimize certificate load time on Windows systems when using a Python version built with OpenSSL 3.x. (#6667)
  • Requests now supports optional use of character detection (chardet or charset_normalizer) when repackaged or vendored. This enables pip and other projects to minimize their vendoring surface area. The Response.text() and apparent_encoding APIs will default to utf-8 if neither library is present. (#6702)

Bugfixes

  • Fixed bug in length detection where emoji length was incorrectly calculated in the request content-length. (#6589)
  • Fixed deserialization bug in JSONDecodeError. (#6629)
  • Fixed bug where an extra leading / (path separator) could lead urllib3 to unnecessarily reparse the request URI. (#6644)

issues.title: Clean-up PaymentMethod
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
The list of enum values for [PaymentMethod](https://schema.org/PaymentMethod) points to the [goodrelations web-site](http://www.heppnetz.de/ontologies/goodrelations/) which seems to have been updated last in 2008, the last messages on its mailing lists were in 2016. 

The list of payments is incomplete, it is missing big players like ApplePay while including dead projects like PaySwarm. 

I don't think that maintaining a complete list of online payment lists would scale. Instead I would suggest adding a `PaymentMethod` class between [`PaymentCard`](https://schema.org/PaymentCard) and [`FinancialProduct`](https://schema.org/FinancialProduct), which would include additional fields like:

* Currency
* Geographical scope


For insance 
```json 
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "PaymentMethod",
  "name": "Twint",
  "currency": "CHF",
  "provider": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "TWINT AG",
    "url": "https://www.twint.ch/"
   }
}
```
I would also update PaymentCard with a property to reflect security features like 3D secure.

issues.title: Improve markup for electric vehicles
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
The schema.org vocabulary defined in the Car extension back in 2015 did already define quite some vocabulary for electric and hybrid vehicles.

However, we need to fix a few things:

## Without changing / additions to the vocabulary

1. Add **additional unit of measurement codes** for [`schema:fuelCapacity`](https://schema.org/fuelCapacity).

We currently just have AMH for ampere-hours for electrical vehicles, but most KWH for kWh (from [UN/CEFACT](https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/rec20_rev3_Annex2e.pdf) would be more appropriate.

This just requires changing the description.

2. Add / **improve examples and the documentation**

It would be good to have examples directly attached to 

- [`schema:fuelCapacity`](https://schema.org/fuelCapacity) 
- [`schema:fuelConsumption`](https://schema.org/fuelConsumption)
- [`schema:fuelEfficiency`](https://schema.org/fuelEfficiency)
- [`schema:Car`](https://schema.org/Car).

and to update the HTML at <https://schema.org/docs/automotive.html>. 

In particular, we should show how to model the energy consumption and hence the range of electrical vehicles in [`schema:fuelConsumption`](https://schema.org/fuelConsumption).

This is not a big issue, but it **should be aligned with how major consumers of schema.org are using such markup.**

## Extending the vocabulary

There are already features for electric vehicles search in major search engines, e.g. [Google's deeper electric vehicle insights in Search](https://blog.google/outreach-initiatives/sustainability/google-transportation-energy-emissions-reduction/). It would be good to check if schema.org needs to be extended to support such features.

We may want to **add properties,** e.g. for 
- `batteryType` ("Lithium ion battery") 
- `vehicleRange` (while this can be computed, it would IMO be good to allow stating it)

and **values** for [consumption and range measurement standards](https://www.lifewire.com/ev-ranges-explained-5202261), like
- EPA
- WLTP
- NEDC.

Also, a small vocabulary extension for **charging information** would be good, see e.g. [here for examples](https://ev-database.org/car/1564/Toyota-bZ4X-FWD).

issues.title: Extend 'MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride' to enable overrides of more properties
issues.author: jlndr
issues.body:
The current [MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicySeasonalOverride) is quite limited in the set of attributes that it can override on [MerchantReturnPolicy](https://schema.org/MerchantReturnPolicy). For example, having free/no returns, store credits as refund or keeping the product as return method would be useful to be able to override during holiday/sale events.

On the extreme, the seasonal override *could* itself be an `MerchantReturnPolicy` with a start and end date, but simply extending the seasonal override with a few properties should be sufficient for most use cases. I propose extending with the following properties:

* `/refundType` - https://schema.org/RefundTypeEnumeration
* `/returnMethod` - https://schema.org/ReturnMethodEnumeration
* `/returnFees` - https://schema.org/ReturnFeesEnumeration

`/returnFees` then implies also adding:

* `/restockingFee` - https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount or https://schema.org/Number
* `/returnShippingFeesAmount` - https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount 

depending on the selected return fee.

issues.title: Third-party external extension technical standards
issues.author: jacohuman
issues.body:
I am very new to semantic web technologies and schema.org in particular, but have become heavily invested in this field through my studies in Computer Science.
I am unsure if this is the correct place to even raise these questions, so please redirect me if I should rather ask them elsewhere. (I was unable to find answers to these questions on the schema.org website).

When third-parties develop external extensions of schema.org, are there any technical standards these ontologies/vocabularies should comply with?
When a third-party extends schema.org in this way,  are there any direct/indirect benefits (as apposed to just hosting their own ontology scheme)?
Is there a specific process these third-parties should follow to be recognised as an official external extension of schema.org and whom should they consult to start this process? The community group or the steering group or a specific person?
Are there any specific terms of use or copyright permissions required when a third-party wants to extend schema.org in this way?

Also, am I correct in understanding that "hosted extensions" have basically been replaced by the --pending-- label or will some more "hosted extensions" (such as bib) be included in the schema.org namespace in the future?

Thanks
Jaco

issues.title: Add ratings for content suitability (children, teenagers, adults) to Schema.org
issues.author: mediaprophet
issues.body:
Issue Description:

**Proposal:**
Currently, Schema.org provides a robust framework for marking up various types of content on the web, but there is a gap in specifying the suitability of content for different age groups (children, teenagers, adults).

**Problem Statement:**
There is a growing need for websites and online platforms to indicate the age-appropriateness of their content. This information is crucial for parents, educators, and content filters to ensure that users are accessing material suitable for their age group. However, there is no standardized way in Schema.org to specify these age ratings.

**Objective:**
The objective of this proposal is to introduce new properties or extend existing ones in Schema.org to allow content creators to specify age ratings for their web content. These ratings would cover categories such as content suitable for children (e.g., under 12), teenagers (e.g., 13-17), and adults (18+).

**Example Use Cases:**

1. A children's educational website wants to mark its content as suitable for ages 5-10.
2. A streaming service wishes to mark certain movies and TV shows as suitable for teenagers aged 13-17.
3. An adult-oriented website needs to indicate that its content is intended for users 18 and older.

**Implementation Details:**

1. **New Properties**: Introduce new properties (e.g., contentRatingForChildren, contentRatingForTeenagers, contentRatingForAdults) under the existing Schema.org hierarchy.

2. **Integration with Existing Types**: Ensure compatibility with existing types such as CreativeWork and WebPage so that these ratings can be applied to various types of content.
  
3. **Documentation and Guidelines**: Provide clear guidelines and examples in the Schema.org documentation on how to use these new properties effectively; including, considerations about browser functionality and/or plugins that may restrict access to content for certain users.

**Benefits:**

- **Clarity for Users:** Users, especially parents and guardians, will have clearer information about the appropriateness of web content for different age groups.
- **Enhanced Filtering:** Content filters and parental controls can use these ratings to restrict access to content based on user-defined age settings.
- **Standardization:** Establishing a standard for age ratings on the web promotes consistency across different platforms and improves accessibility.

Next Steps:

- Discuss and refine the proposed properties and their integration within the Schema.org community.
- Develop consensus on the implementation details through community feedback.
- Update Schema.org documentation and schemas accordingly.

Additional Notes:
This enhancement aligns with evolving trends in content regulation and user protection on the internet, aiming to provide a safer and more informed browsing experience for all users.

Tags: enhancement, content-rating, schema-extension, community-feedback

issues.title: Proposal to support loyalty (membership) pricing by extending Organization and Offer
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
## Context

This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming schema.org Offer and Organization markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would allow merchants to add loyalty (membership) programs and pricing to their Organization and Offer structured data and allow us and other consuming systems to better understand the various pricing options for products sold online. See also #3190. 

## Description

Products advertised or sold online often have different prices, depending on whether the consumer is a member of the merchant's loyalty program and, if so, the program tier (for example, "bronze", "silver", and "gold") the consumer is a member of.

To support the specification of such loyalty programs and the associated preferred prices as well as other benefits (such as loyalty points) we propose to add a few additional types to allow (1) the definition of the loyalty program and its member tiers offered by a business, and (2) the specification of tier-specific prices for product offers.

### Defining the loyalty program for use on Organizations

#### Program and Tiers

We propose to add a new class _/MemberProgram_ as a subtype of[ /Intangible](https://schema.org/Intangible) to allow the specification of a membership program. The name, description, and signup URL for the program can be defined using the inherited properties _[/name](https://schema.org/name)_, [/description](https://schema.org/description), and _[/url](https://schema.org/url)_.

We propose to also introduce a related new property _/hasMemberProgram_ with values of type _/MemberProgram_ for use on [/Organization](https://schema.org/Organization) to allow the specification of the Membership program(s) provided by the organization (typically a merchant).

To specify the various membership tiers under the program we propose to introduce a new class _/MemberProgramTier_, a subtype of[ /Intangible](https://schema.org/Intangible). The name and signup URL for the tier can be defined using the inherited properties _[/name](https://schema.org/name)_ and _[/url](https://schema.org/url)_. 

We propose to also add a new property _/forProgram_ for use on _/MemberProgramTier_ to specify the membership program the tier is a part of, For reverse linking, we also propose to add a new property _/hasTiers_ for use on _/MemberProgram_ to specify the member tier(s) part of the program.

#### Tier Requirements

To specify the requirements of each member tier we propose to add a new property _/hasTierRequirement_ with values of a new enumeration type _/TierRequirementEnumeration_ with the following values:

*   _/TierFreeToJoin_ - the tier is free to join
*   _/TierSpendingAmountRequired_ - the tier requires a specific spending amount
*   _/TierCreditCardRequired_ - the tier requires the consumer to sign up for a credit card
*   _/TierPeriodicFeeRequired_ - the tier requires a fee to be a member of the tier for a specific period, e.g., monthly or annually.

To support these requirements we also propose to add the following properties for use on _/MemberProgramTier_:

*   _/minimumSpendingAmount_ of type [/MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) 
    *   to be provided when _/hasTierRequirement_= _/TierSpendingAmountRequired_
*   _/creditCard_ of type /[Text](https://schema.org/Text)
    *   to be provided when _/hasTierRequirement_ = _/TierCreditCardRequired_
*   _/periodicFee_ of type [/MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount)
    *    to be provided when _/hasTierRequirement_=_/TierPeriodicFeeRequired_
*   _/periodLength_ of type [/QuantitativeValue](https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue)
    *    to be provided when _/hasTierRequirement_=_/TierPeriodicFeeRequired_

#### Tier Benefits

To specify the benefits associated with a program tier we propose to add a new property /_hasTierBenefit_ with values of a new enumeration type _/TierBenefitEnumeration_ or of type /[Text](https://schema.org/Text) (for free-form benefits) with the following values:

*   _/TierBenefitLoyaltyPrice_
*   _/TierBenefitLoyaltyPoints_

To support these tier benefits we also propose to add existing property [/membershipPointsEarned](https://schema.org/membershipPointsEarned) to _/MemberProgramTier_,  to be provided if _/hasTierBenefit_= _/TierBenefitLoyaltyPoints_, indicating the number of loyalty points earned by the consumer per currency unit spent.

### Defining loyalty program pricing and loyalty points earned for Offers

We propose the following new properties to be able to tie an offered price to a specific member program and specify the benefits for each of its tiers:

*   Add a new enumeration value _/MemberPrice_ to existing enumeration type[ /PriceTypeEnumeration](https://schema.org/PriceTypeEnumeration) for use on property [/priceType](https://schema.org/priceType).
*   Add a new property _/validForMemberTier_ with values of type _/MemberProgramTier_ to specify that the price is only valid for members of the specific membership program and tier, when provided. Add this new property under [/PriceSpecification](https://schema.org/PriceSpecification).
*   Add existing property [/membershipPointsEarned](https://schema.org/membershipPointsEarned) to [/PriceSpecification](https://schema.org/UnitPriceSpecification) to indicate loyalty points the consumer can earn with the purchase, if different from the default specified under the tier.

### Example

The following example illustrates the definition of the member program and its tiers under an instance of an [OnlineStore ](https://schema.org/OnlineStore)(subtype of Organization), followed by a list and member price of an offer using [UnitPriceSpecification](https://schema.org/UnitPriceSpecification)


```
[
  {
    "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@type": "OnlineStore",
    "name": "Example Online Store",
    "url": "https://www.example.com",
    "sameAs": [
      "https://example.net/profile/example12",
      "https://example.org/@example34"
    ],
    "logo": "https://www.example.com/assets/images/logo.png",
    "contactPoint": {
      "contactType": "Customer Service",
      "email": "support@example.com",
      "telephone": "+47-99-999-9900"
    },
    "vatID": "FR12345678901",
    "iso6523Code": "0199:724500PMK2A2M1SQX229",
    "hasMemberProgram": {
      "@type": "MemberProgram",
      "name": "Membership Plus",
      "description": "For frequent shoppers this is our top-rated loyalty program",
      "url": "https://www.example.com/membership-plus",
      "hasTiers": [
        {
          "@type": "MemberProgramTier",
          "@id": "#plus-tier-silver",
          "name": "silver",
          "url": "https://www.example.com/membership-plus-silver",
          "hasTierRequirement": "https://schema.org/TierFreeToJoin",
          "hasTierBenefit": [
            "https://schema.org/TierBenefitLoyaltyPoints"
          ],
          "membershipPointsEarned": 5
        },
        {
          "@type": "MemberProgramTier",
          "@id": "#plus-tier-gold",
          "name": "gold",
          "url": "https://www.example.com/membership-plus-gold",
          "hasTierRequirement": "https://schema.org/TierCreditCardRequired",
          "creditCardRequired": "Example platinum card plus",
          "hasTierBenefit": [
            "https://schema.org/TierBenefitLoyaltyPrice",
            "https://schema.org/TierBenefitLoyaltyPoints"
          ],
          "membershipPointsEarned": 10
        }
      ]
    }
  },
  {
    "@type": "Product",
    "sku": "44E01-X1100000",
    "gtin14": "98766051104399",
    "image": "https://www.example.com/coat_large_lightblue.jpg",
    "name": "Large light blue coat",
    "description": "Large wool light blue coat for the winter season",
    "color": "light blue",
    "size": "large",
    "offers": [
      {
        "@type": "Offer",
        "url": "https://www.example.com/coat?size=large&color=lightblue",
        "itemCondition": "https://schema.org/NewCondition",
        "availability": "https://schema.org/Backorder",
        "shippingDetails": {
          "@id": "https://www.example.com/shipping#shipping_policy"
        },
        "hasMerchantReturnPolicy": {
          "@id": "https://www.example.com/com/returns#return_policy"
        },
        "priceSpecification": [
          {
            "@type": "PriceSpecification",
            "price": 15,
            "priceCurrency": "USD"
          },
          {
            "@type": "PriceSpecification",
            "priceType": [
              "https://schema.org/MemberPrice"
            ],
            "validForMemberTier": {
              "@id": "https://www.example.com/com/members#plus_tier_gold"
            },
            "price": 9.95,
            "priceCurrency": "USD"
          }        
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
]

issues.title: How to make conjunctive/disjunctive certification claims
issues.author: VladimirAlexiev
issues.body:
[Certification](https://schema.org/Certification) has prop `about` "The subject matter of the content" and says "for example Organizations can be ISO certified, Food products can be certified Organic or Vegan, a Person can be a certified professional, a Place can be certified for food processing".

It also says "Mapped from the [gs1:CertificationDetails](https://www.gs1.org/voc/CertificationDetails) class" (I participated in its definition during the EPCIS 2 effort). The analogous prop in that class is [gs1:certificationSubject](https://www.gs1.org/voc/certificationSubject), and it has an extra feature:
> References the object (e.g. product, asset, container), party or location being certified. If multiple values are specified, the certification details apply to the logical conjunction (AND) of groups of different types, while a logical disjunction (OR) applies within each group of the same type. For example, two sibling organisations O1 and O2 can process products P1 and P2 at locations L1 and L2: meaning that either organisation can process either product at either location (OR); but the certificate holds for the combinations of organisation (either O1 OR O2) AND product (either P1 OR P2) AND location (either L1 OR L2)

I think that conjunctive/disjunctive certification claims are a legitimate use case, eg:
- `AND`: Mike's Poultry is ISO 22000 certified for processing Chicken at Plant 123:
  - org=Mike's Poultry AND product=Chicken AND facility=Plant 123
- `OR`: Mike's Poultry and its sibling company Bob's Beef are both ISO 22000 certified to process meat at Plant 123 and Plant 124:
  - (org=Mike's Poultry OR Bob's Beef) AND (facility=Plant 123 OR Plant 124)
  
In the case of [gs1:certificationSubject](https://www.gs1.org/voc/certificationSubject) we went for simplicity and didn't design a structure to hold AND/OR but encoded this through "different kinds" of subjects. However, that's not very explicit nor clear because GS1 defines about 20 kinds of identifiers, and whether eg an individual asset (GIAI) and a returnable asset (GRAI) are of the same kind or not is subject to interpretation.

In schema.org it's better to capture the AND/OR structure explicitly. We only need 2 levels and COULD postulate that:
- the top level (multiple values of `about`) is AND
- the bottom level is OR. We nearly have the means of capturing this with existing terms: `Collection, hasPart` except that's only defined as CreativeWork but we need a collection of any subjects.

With these provisos, the second example (`OR`) can be expressed as follows:
```ttl
<certification> a Certification;
  about <Mikes_and_Bobs>, <Plant_123_and_124>.
<Mikes_and_Bobs> a Collection;
  hasPart <MikesPoultry>, <BobsBeef>.
<Plant_123_and_124> a Collection;
  hasPart <Plant_123>, <Plant_124>.
<MikesPoultry> a Organization.
<BobsBeef> a Organization.
<Plant_123> a Place. # closest I could find
<Plant_124> a Place. # closest I could find
```

Does this sound ok? The top level being AND may be counter-intuitive, eg:
```ttl
<certification> a Certification;
  about <MikesPoultry>, <BobsBeef>.
```
would mean the certificate is only valid when the two companies work TOGETHER, not SEPARATELY for each one.

issues.title: how to make statements about a schema.org document -- rdf/json-ld @id interpretation issues...
issues.author: smrgeoinfo
issues.body:
I'm working on distributed, federated catalog systems for data in which data providers 'publish' metadata for harvest by metadata aggregators who create indexes and search interfaces, for example the US NSF Decoder/[GeoCODEs catalog](https://geocodes.earthcube.org/#/landing), [Ocean Info hub](https://oceaninfohub.org/).  In this context, it is useful to be able include information about a metadata record-- e.g.  last modified date, creator, encoding format/profile, point of contact.  Schema.org includes several properties that can be used to embed information about the metadata record in the resource metadata: [**sdDatePublished**](https://schema.org/sdDatePublished), [**sdLicense**](https://schema.org/sdLicense), [**sdPublisher**](https://schema.org/sdPublisher), but lacks a way to provide an identifier for the metadata record distinct from the resource it describes, to specify other agents responsible for the metadata except the publisher, or to assert specification or profile conformance for the metadata record itself.

In the CDIF working group (see [WorldFAIR (D2.3) Cross-Domain Interoperability Framework (CDIF)](https://zenodo.org/records/11236871) we are having a [discussion](https://github.com/Cross-Domain-Interoperability-Framework/Discovery/issues/13) about the approach to serializing this information using json-ld/schema.org.  

Given this metadata record (bare bones...):

```
{   "@context": "https://schema.org",
    "@id": "ex:URIforSomething",
    "@type": "ImageObject",
    "name": "Picture of analytical setup",
    "description": "Description of the resource",
    "identifier":"identifierStringForThing_in_the_world"
... lots of other stuff }
```

I need another graph node like
```
{
        "@id": "ex:URIforAnotherSomething",
        "@type": "DigitalDocument",
        "dateModified": "2017-05-23",
        "encoding": {
            "@type": "MediaObject",
    	    "dcterms:conformsTo": {"@id":"ex:cdif-metadataSpec"}
          },
          "creator": {
              "@type": "Person",
              "name": "Some Person",
              "identifier":"https://orcid.org/0000-0001-4021-9302"
            },
            "maintainer": {
              "@type": "Organization",
              "name": "Some Org",
              "identifier": "https://ror.org/02e2tgs60"
            }
        ?"about":"ex:URIforSomething"  OR... ?"identifier":"ex:URIforSomething"
    }
```
the idea is that dateModified, creator, maintainer, and encoding are about the metadata record

How to interpret some things here: 
-  I'm interpreting the json object with `"@id": "ex:URIforSomething" ` as a metadata record about some resource (physical or digital) that we're interested in.
- `"@id": "ex:URIforSomething"`  identifies a graph node. -- is that the thing in the world (image in this case), or the information about that thing represented in this json object.  
- `"@type": "ImageObject"`  does this mean `"@id": "ex:URIforSomething"` is a thing in the world that is an image object, or that the data type (i.e. the schema) for this json object conforms to 'ImageObject'
- does the "identifier": string identify something different from `"@id": "ex:URIforSomething"`.  Should it be there at all?


in the graph node about the other graph node (metadata about the metadata), is 
`<ex:URIforAnotherSomething>  <about>  "ex:URIforSomething" `
or 
`<ex:URIforAnotherSomething>  <identifier>  "ex:URIforSomething" `
or something else?

It seems that these are getting used lots of different way; I'm just wondering if there's any logically coherent consensus, or do we just define our CDIF profile the way we think it works best?

issues.title: New Schema to Represent Energy and Transportation Incentives
issues.author: dswen
issues.body:
**Motivation**
Governments, utilities, and other organizations offer financial incentives to help make efficient appliances and vehicles more affordable for consumers. These incentives save people money, but can be difficult to find and understand. Information is fragmented across multiple sources and is often formatted inconsistently, sometimes in ways that are hard to understand by typical consumers. This can limit awareness and adoption.

**Description**
We propose a new type, SustainabilityFinancialIncentive, which contains information about financial incentives related to electrification, carbon emissions reduction, or other sustainability initiatives. This schema aims to balance ease of adoption while still providing consumers with the highest priority information they need to understand incentives.

Our goals in this effort are to develop schema guidance that:
*   Is easy for incentive providers to adopt
*   Applies globally as well as domestically in the United States
*   Provides unique incremental value over existing data sets
*   Will generate data that can be shared broadly for public use (e.g. via DataCommons.org)

We do not want to:
*   Develop competing standards 
*   Design a schema that fits every possible use case
*   Design a schema that only works for specific domains (e.g. only solar incentives)

The core use case we have in mind is providing basic information about available incentives. In particular, we want to answer these questions:
*   What general category of purchase (e.g. solar panels or heat pumps) is being incentivized?
*   How much money can I access to help defray the cost of purchase and installation? We can approximate that with:
    *   How much money do people typically receive?
    *   What's the maximum amount of money possible?
*   Is it available in my area?
*   Is the incentive still active or has it expired or lost funding?
*   Where can I learn more about this incentive?

Here are the proposed fields:

## FinancialIncentive

| Field | Data type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| display\_name | string | A human-readable display name for this incentive  e.g. "Faster Adoption and Manufacturing of (Hybrid and) Electric Vehicles (FAME-II)" |
| eligible\_region | [DefinedRegion](https://schema.org/DefinedRegion) | The region in which the incentive is applicable. |
| value | [IncentiveValue](\#incentivevalue) | The amount of money the consumer can receive. |
| status | enum | Whether this incentive is currently active. ACTIVE | ON\_HOLD | IN\_DEVELOPMENT | RETIRED |
| provider | [Provider](http://schema.org/provider) | The entity / organization that is providing this incentive.  |
| url | string | A URL where people can find more information about this incentive, including a description of what it is, eligibility criteria, and how it can be redeemed. |
| incentivized\_item\_category | enum | The general category of the item being incentivized. ELECTRIC\_VEHICLE | SOLAR\_PANEL | HEAT\_PUMP | … |
| purchase\_type | enum (optional) | The type of purchase the consumer must make in order to qualify for this incentive.  NEW\_PURCHASE | USED\_PURCHASE | LEASE | TRADE\_IN |
| goods\_or\_services | enum (optional) | The types of purchases that are covered by the incentive. For example some incentives are only for the goods (tangible items) but the services (labor) are excluded. GOODS\_ONLY | SERVICES\_ONLY | GOODS\_AND\_SERVICES |
| redemption\_type | enum (optional) | The manner in which the incentive is redeemed.  TAX\_CREDIT | REBATE |POINT\_OF\_SALE\_FRONTLOADED\_TAX\_CREDIT | … |
| requirements | [IncentiveRequirements](\#incentiverequirements) (optional) | The requirements that must be met in order to redeem this incentive. |
| valid\_range | daterange | Which dates this incentive is valid on. |
| marked\_up\_by | enum | The type of entity that marked up this incentive. INCENTIVE\_SOURCE means the organization administering this incentive also marked up the webpage providing this data. AGGREGATOR means a third party group found this incentive and included it in their own markup. INCENTIVE\_SOURCE | AGGREGATOR | UNSPECIFIED |

## IncentiveValue

| Field | Data type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| typical\_amount | [MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) (optional) | A typical amount that people receive, if applicable. |
| absolute\_max | [MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) (optional) | The maximum amount of money that this incentive can be redeemed for. |
| absolute\_max\_percentage | [Number](http://schema.org/Number) (optional) | The maximum percentage of the cost of the incentivized item that can be redeemed. For example, "You can claim up to 30% of the total cost" would be represented as absolute\_max\_percentage=30 |
| amount\_per\_unit | [AmountPerUnit](\#amountperunit) (optional) | For incentives that are based on amounts other than price, how much per which unit the claimant can get. |

## AmountPerUnit

| Field | Data type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| amount | [MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) | The money value per unit. In other words the numerator. |
| unit | enum | The unit that is measured to determine the amount given. In other words the denominator. |

## IncentiveRequirements

| Field | Data type | Description |
| :---- | :---- | :---- |
| has\_income\_limit | boolean (optional) | Whether the incentive has an income limit. |
| price\_limit | [MonetaryAmount](https://schema.org/MonetaryAmount) (optional) | The maximum price the incentivized item can have and still qualify for this incentive (e.g. German EV incentives have different amounts for under 40.000e vs. over 40.000e) |

**Example**

```
{   
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",  
  "@type": "SustainabilityFinancialIncentive",  
  "displayName": "Inflation Reduction Act ITC",  
  "eligibleRegion": {  
    "@type": "Country",  
    "addressCountry": "US"  
  },  
  "value": {  
    "@type": "ValueSpecification",  
    "typicalAmount": {  
      "@type": "Money",  
      "currency": "USD",  
      "amount": 9000,  
    },  
    "absoluteMaxPercentage": 30,  
  },  
  "provider": {  
    "@type": "GovernmentOrganization",  
    "name": "Internal Revenue Service",  
  },  
  "url": "https://www.energy.gov/eere/solar/homeowners-guide-federal-tax-credit-solar-photovoltaics",  
  "incentivizedItemCategory": 'SOLAR\_PANEL',  
  "purchaseType": 'NEW\_PURCHASE',   
  "goodsOrServices": 'GOODS\_AND\_SERVICES',  
  "redemptionType": 'TAX\_CREDIT',  
    
  "validRange": {  
    "startDate": "2022-08-31",  
    "endDate": "2034-12-31",  
  },  
  "status": 'ACTIVE',  
}
```

issues.body:
A client had a rather rare and expensive guitar stolen from him several years ago and has offered a reward for its return.  I  am sitting down to brainstorm how to create a script that will expose the model and serial number to the internet, marking it as stolen property and therefore destroy any value in the resale market. 

- A Reward schema might also be useful for brand loyalty programs. (Concert tickets that include the latest CD etc.)

- The Reward schema might be useful for the investment community. I.E., rate of return over a period, cryptocurrency and NFT drops etc.   

Of course, there would also need to be a method to represent that stolen property had been recovered, perhaps a way to represent how many rewards were given in a brand loyalty program.

For instance, my cell phone provider (Helium Mobile) gives their cryptocurrency in their loyalty program.

issues.title: Proposal: "Reserved" enumeration for ItemAvailability
issues.author: shakyjake
issues.body:
Hiya,

Got a client who sells a lot of one-off, big-ticket items where prices are negotiated with prospective buyers and products are unavailable to others while negotiations are ongoing. It would be nice to have a `Reserved` enumeration for such situations. It could also be useful for situations like event ticketing, auctions or cinema seating.

My current strategy is to use `SoldOut` then switch back to `InStock` if an agreement isn't reached, which feels a bit wrong. `Reserved` would more accurately describe the current status of the item and the possibility of it becoming available again in the future.

issues.title: Proposal to add a value for strikethrough (regular) pricing to PriceTypeEnumeration
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
Enumeration type [PriceTypeEnumeration](https://schema.org/PriceTypeEnumeration) currently has enumeration values such as [`ListPrice`](https://schema.org/ListPrice), [`SalePrice`](https://schema.org/SalePrice),  and [`MSRP`](https://schema.org/MSRP). 

There are a few more price types that are common in the industry such as `MemberPrice` (proposed in #3563), and also `RegularPrice`  or `StrikethroughPrice` (a previously advertised and charged price). A `RegularPrice`  or `StrikethroughPrice` is typically lower than a [`ListPrice`](https://schema.org/ListPrice) or [`MSRP`](https://schema.org/MSRP), but higher than a [`SalePrice`](https://schema.org/SalePrice), and we therefore propose to add either  `RegularPrice`  or `StrikethroughPrice` as new values under [PriceTypeEnumeration](https://schema.org/PriceTypeEnumeration).

`StrikethroughPrice` represents a more intuitive and visual form of a previous charged price, while `RegularPrice` might fit better with the existing enumeration values under [PriceTypeEnumeration](https://schema.org/PriceTypeEnumeration).

issues.title: Proposal: Link-in-Bio Identity Verification
issues.author: farnazlt
issues.body:
**Context**
With the proliferation of social media, the need to establish verified online identities has become increasingly important. This proposal is around including properties that indicate the verified status of an individual's social media accounts, enhancing trust and authenticity.

**Glossary**

- Verified Account: An account that has been confirmed by a social media platform to be authentic.

- Microdata: A specification used to nest structured data within HTML content. JSON-LD (JavaScript Object Notation for Linked Data), is a method of encoding Linked Data using JSON.

- Consumers: search engines and other sources interested in verifying profile claims.

- OAuth: An open standard for access delegation, commonly used as a way for Internet users to grant websites or applications access to their information on other websites but without giving them the passwords. Social network sites use this or variations of this.

Inspirations

- ProfilePage tag: https://schema.org/ProfilePage 

- Account tag: https://schema.googleapis.com/Account. An extension to schema.org by Google.

- Fact Checking: https://schema.org/ClaimReview 

- WebPage: https://schema.org/WebPage 

**Solution**
The proposed solution is two-fold: 

- Website tags: Part one is metadata added to the link-in-bio profile using the ProfilePage and Account tags.

- Signature Proof: This part has its own URI and is served on a different endpoint as a way for the provider to verify claims. This provides control over data that may require more stringent access control. 

**On-Profile Tags**
Google’s proposed Account tag https://schema.googleapis.com/Account already provides a way to represent an account a user owns. For example: a bank account, a brokerage account, a utility service account, etc. In our case we will be using this for representing social media provider accounts:

In the proposed schema, the ProfilePage now includes a verificationStatus attribute with an extensible enum (Verified, NotVerified, Pending), which reflects the verification status of the profile. It also introduces an accounts attribute that lists social media account entities, each described by attributes like accountHolder, accountId, provider, serviceType, verificationStatus, and verificationProofURI. The verificationStatus for each account is also an extensible enum, providing a clear indication of each account's verification level. The verificationProofURI attribute offers a URL for verifying the claims of each account.
```
{
  "@context": "http://schema.org",
  "@type": "[ProfilePage](https://schema.org/ProfilePage)",

  // (New) extensible enum for verification status
  "verificationStatus": "Verified|NotVerified|Pending", 

  // (New) attribute to reference account ownerships
  "accounts": [
    {
      "@type": "[Account](https://schema.googleapis.com/Account)",
      "accountHolder": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "Person's Name"
      },
      "accountId": "Unique Identifier",
      "provider": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "Service Provider Name"
      },
      "serviceType": "Type of Service", // e.g., Social Media, Shop, etc.

      // (New) extensible enum for verification status
      "verificationStatus": "Verified|NotVerified|Pending", 

      // (New) URI providing proof of verification
      "verificationProofURI": "URL to Verification Proof" 
    }
  ]
}
```


An example of HTML markup to be added to a website that represents the link-in-bio profile of a Jane Due:

```
<script type="application/ld+json">
{
  "@context": "http://schema.org",
  "@type": "ProfilePage",
  "verificationStatus": "Verified",
  "accounts": [
    {
      "@type": "Account",
      "accountHolder": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "Jane Smith"
      },
      "accountId": "jane.smith83",
      "provider": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "TikTok"
      },
      "serviceType": "Social Media",
      "verificationStatus": "Verified",
      "verificationProofURI": "https://api.linktr.ee/profile/verifyIdentityClaim?oid=123"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Account",
      "accountHolder": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "Jane Smith"
      },
      "accountId": "jane.smith",
      "provider": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "Instagram"
      },
      "serviceType": "Social Media",
      "verificationStatus": "Verified",
      "verificationProofURI": "https://api.linktr.ee/profile/verifyIdentityClaim?oid=456"
    }
  ]
}
</script>
```
 
Signature Proof URI
This is an end point that the provider can hit to verify claims

```
{
  "@context": "http://schema.org",
  "@type": "AccountVerificationProof",
  "itemReviewed": "https://URL",  // Thing type referencing the profile website URL 
  "verificationMethod": "OAuth|Backlink|etc", // Enum for verification methods
  "dateCreated": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ", // Timestamp in ISO format
  "dateModified": "YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ", // Timestamp in ISO format
  "claimVerificationMethod": "ApiCall", // Description on how to verify the claim
  "claimVerificationData": {
    "apiToken": "1a2b3c4d5e6f..." // meta data required to support the verification method for API call
    "": "<HEX>", // Digital signature in hex format
  },
}
```

OR 

```
GET https://api.linktr.ee/profile/verifyIdentityClaim?oid=123
Content-Type: application/ld+json
{
  "@context": "http://schema.org",
  "@type": "IdentityVerificationProof",
  "verificationMethod": "OAuth",
  "howToVerifyOurClaim": "CheckFollowers"
  // Hashes and such go here.
  "signature": "<HEX>",
  "timestamp": "YYYY
}
```

issues.title: Proposal: add SocialMedia to contactPointOption
issues.author: WeaverStever
issues.body:
It is generally accepted that social media urls are not appropriate in the sameAs property.   

As mentioned in #3403, I came to the realization that social media accounts are actually contactOptions, and in many cases, the only (or preferred) contact options.  (The op in #3403 is looking for a creation date property for social media profiles).

Currently, [ContactPointOption](https://schema.org/ContactPointOption) has two enumerations for use in contactOptions.

Enumeration members in ContactPointOption

- [HearingImpairedSupported](https://schema.org/HearingImpairedSupported)
- [TollFree](https://schema.org/TollFree)


I suggest adding the third enumeration

- SocialMedia


(In the example below, we could use a startTime property into potentialAction to indicate the creation date of the social media acct.)

~~~
<script type="application/ld+json">
{ "@context" : "https://schema.org",
  "@type" : "Organization",
  "url" : "http://www.t-mobile.com",
  "contactPoint" : [
    { "@type" : "ContactPoint",
      "telephone" : "+1-877-746-0909",
      "contactType" : "customer service",
      "contactOption" : "TollFree",
      "areaServed" : "US"
    } , {
      "@type" : "ContactPoint",
      "telephone" : "+1-505-998-3793",
      "contactType" : "customer service"
    } , {
      "@type" : "ContactPoint",
      "alternateName" : "@TMobile",
      "contactType" : "Twitter account",
      "contactOption" : ["SocialMedia"],
      "url": "https://x.com/tmobile",
      "potentialAction": {
        "startTime": "1999-12-01"     
      }
    }
  ] 
}
</script>
~~~

issues.title: Proposal to support organization-level shipping information more extensively
issues.author: pascalfleury
issues.body:
This is a proposal from Google to support a richer representation of shipping details (such as delivery cost and speed) and make this kind of data explicit. If adopted by schema.org and publishers, we consider it likely that search experiences and other consuming systems could be improved by making use of such markup.

This change introduces a new type, `ShippingService`, that groups shipping constraints (delivery locations, time, weight and size limits and shipping rate). Redundant fields from `ShippingRateSettings` are therefore been deprecated in this proposal.

As a consequence, the following changes are also proposed:

- some fields in `OfferShippingDetails` have moved to `ShippingService`;
- `ShippingRateSettings` has more ways to specify the shipping rate, proportional to the order price or shipping weight;
-  linking from the `Offer` should now be done with standard Semantic Web URI linking.
 
Given the size of the proposal, an external [Google Docs](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1kTJJKnnWtnoJuUK0cmtDdPH3JLZILyfN6IXICXti4wQ/edit?usp=sharing&resourcekey=0-BernNphrZhVov9lX7u2aNg) document is created for review and inline comments.
