issues.title: Extend the subtypes of collection
issues.author: rhdunn
issues.body:
So far `Collection` only has a generic `ProductCollection` subtype for products being sold. Comparing with other parts of the hierarchy:
- `CreativeWorkSeries` has a lot of subtypes for books, movies, comics, newspapers, podcasts, radio shows, TV shows, and video games;
- `CollectionPage > MediaGallery` has subtypes for image and video galleries;
- `MediaObject` has subytpes for 3D models, audio, data, image, legislation, music video, text, and video objects.

It would make sense to mirror the `Collection` and `CollectionPage` hierarchies (where a `CollectionPage` is effectively a view of a `Collection`) and extend them to contain only specific types:
1. Extend `MediaGallery` and a new `MediaCollection` subtype to have `*Gallery` and `*Collection` variants for various `MediaObject` types -- `3DModel*`, `Audio*`, `Image*`, `Legislation*`, `MusicVideo*`, `Text*`, and `Video*`.
2. Extend `Collection` and `CollectionPage` to have `*Collection` and `*CollectionPage` variants of the `CreativeWorkSeries` subtypes for general (unordered) collections of these types of work -- `BookCollection(Page)? > AudiobookCollection(Page)?`, `MovieCollection(Page)?`, `ComicCollection(Page)?`, `PodcastCollection(Page)?`, `RadioCollection(Page)?`, `VideoGameCollection(Page)?`.

My use case is that I have an application managing creative works (images, audio, etc.) and want to restrict the parts of a collection to specific subtypes, e.g. to have an `ImageCollection` contain parts of type  `ImageObject`, `Drawing`, etc. but not `Play` or `MusicRecording`. This helps with things like searching for parts to add to a collection, like can be done when e.g. searching for parts to add to a `BookSeries` or `PodcastSeason`.

issues.title: Add a ComicVolume type
issues.author: rhdunn
issues.body:
There is a `ComicIssue` subtype of `PublicationIssue` but no corresponding `ComicVolume` subtype of `PublicationVolume`.

The use case of this is manga (e.g. Detective Conan or Spy x Family) that are initially released as single issues and then bundled into a volume.

Thus, you would have:

```
Comic Issue #1
  - ComicCoverArt -- issue #1 cover
  - ComicStory -- story for issue #1
...
Comic Issue #n
  - ComicCoverArt -- issue #n cover
  - ComicStory -- story for issue #n

Comic Volume #1
 - ComicCoverArt -- volume cover
 - ComicStory -- story for issue #1
 - ...
 - ComicStory -- story for issue #n
```

issues.title: Add a story arc type and associated subtypes
issues.author: rhdunn
issues.body:
The use case here is to model a group of episodes or works that form a single story arc within a series or season. Examples include:
- Story arcs in comics and manga over several issues (stories) that when bundled into volumes may span volumes, e.g. [One Piece Story Arcs](https://onepiece.fandom.com/wiki/Story_Arcs);
- Podcasts of RPG playthroughs (game scenarios) where multiple scenarios are played in a season and over multiple episodes;
- TV shows such as adaptations of Manga;
- Radio dramas.

NOTE: These can be non-consecutive e.g. in the case of manga arcs, e.g. adding interludes between long arcs or at the end of a volume.

This would have the same properties as `CreativeWorkSeries` and the following hierarchy:
```
- CreativeWork
  - StoryArc
    - ComicStoryArc
    - PodcastStoryArc
    - RadioStoryArc
    - TVStoryArc
```

issues.title: Suggestion: add age recommendation example to https://schema.org/Book
issues.author: ell1e
issues.body:
I suggest that you add an example of how to specify an age recommendation for a book. This would have real world use, because age recommendations are commonly used to categorize book in automated web shop categories and for actual physical placement in a physical book shop. So having this information in a machine-readable format would be useful.

Sadly, the example given seems to only use some "isFamilyFriendly" which seems somewhat detached from real world scenarios:
```
    <script type="application/ld+json">
    {
      "@context": "https://schema.org",
      "@type": "Book",
      "accessibilityAPI": "ARIA",
      "accessibilityControl": [
        "fullKeyboardControl",
        "fullMouseControl"
      ],
      "accessibilityFeature": [
        "largePrint/CSSEnabled",
        "highContrast/CSSEnabled",
        "resizeText/CSSEnabled",
        "displayTransformability",
        "longDescription",
        "alternativeText"
      ],
      "accessibilityHazard": [
        "noFlashingHazard",
        "noMotionSimulationHazard",
        "noSoundHazard"
      ],
      "aggregateRating": {
        "@type": "AggregateRating",
        "reviewCount": "0"
      },
      "bookFormat": "EBook/DAISY3",
      "copyrightHolder": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "Holt, Rinehart and Winston"
      },
      "copyrightYear": "2007",
      "description": "NIMAC-sourced textbook",
      "genre": "Educational Materials",
      "inLanguage": "en-US",
      "isFamilyFriendly": "true",
      "isbn": "9780030426599",
      "name": "Holt Physical Science",
      "numberOfPages": "598",
      "publisher": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "Holt, Rinehart and Winston"
      }
    }
    </script>
```
At least in Europe, books are sorted by age recommendation with the granularity of years, so 13+, 14+, etc. This doesn't map to this "isFamilyFriendly" tag presented in the example.

For movies and other visual media, where a minimum age may even be legally binding, this tag would be useful as well.

issues.title: Separate the two meanings of `isPartOf`
issues.author: pascalfleury
issues.body:
In the schema.org model, `http://schema.org/isPartOf` is used for two distinct meanings:
 1. as a way to describe parts of a creative work, as in Movies or TV shows
 2. as separate sections of the schema, eg. parts that are *pending* or in a particular extension.

It would make tooling easier if there was a mechanical way to distinguish these two. The proposal is to continue using the current representation for meaning #1, and simply use Dublin Core's [`isPartOf`](https://www.dublincore.org/specifications/dublin-core/dcmi-terms/#http://purl.org/dc/terms/isPartOf) for the schema's internal structure.

This would entail changing a bit the generation tools to ensure this distinction when deploying and releasing a new version.

Schema.org [has "result" (which can be semantically mapped to PROV "generated"), but no inverse](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17g16wDMtP8RMIUZlknN3c5t8qKYxLXY46vUi8WuehvM/edit?gid=0#gid=0&range=13:13).  

Could we please add this for completeness? It's quite awkward to query in only one direction, and queries like "what was this Dataset generated by?" will be more natural to dataset-focused users.

issues.title: BookFormatType, GraphicNovel
issues.author: joric3
issues.body:
https://bib.schema.org/BookFormatType lists the following types:

- [AudiobookFormat](https://bib.schema.org/AudiobookFormat)
- [EBook](https://bib.schema.org/EBook)
- [GraphicNovel](https://bib.schema.org/GraphicNovel)
- [Hardcover](https://bib.schema.org/Hardcover)
- [Paperback](https://bib.schema.org/Paperback)

EBook, Hardcover and Paperback are publication formats for various types of content, mostly for (written) text or text with illustrations. It might be images and nothing else. In other words, these types describe an outer form and not the content. The primary mode for the content presentation is visual, but otherwise content is undefined. (Some books include multimodal content like haptic elements or sound, e.g. in children's books, but that is beside my point here.)

An Audiobook is for spoken text, obviously using auditory modality. I can understand that is practical to list it as a BookFormatType even though it is primarily used for text and cannot adequately convey images. (It can convey sound beyond spoken word, obviously - sound effects or music.)

A graphic novel is a longform comic, a specific kind of content or medium (in which text and images combine in specific ways). A graphic novel can be published in print (Hardover or Paperback) or electronic format (EBook). To me, it does not make sense to conceptualize as a BookFormatType next to the others. It's like listing "artbook" or "short story collection" on the same level as EBook, Hardcover, Paperback. That's mixing type of content with output formats. Therefore, I think graphic novel should be removed here.

(I'm new to this, apologies if I made mistakes.)

issues.title: JobPosting Schema for Job Videos, Hiring Team Information, and Interview Process
issues.author: cameronlevy1
issues.body:
## Description & Overview

### Goal
The primary goal of this proposal is to standardize the representation of job videos, hiring team information, and the interview process across job boards to significantly improve the candidate experience.

### Context  
In today’s competitive job market, candidates greatly benefit from transparency and clarity in the hiring process. By providing structured data for job videos, details about the hiring team, and the interview process, we can empower candidates with the information they need to make informed decisions. Clear and accessible information can alleviate uncertainty, help candidates prepare effectively, and ultimately lead to a more positive experience.

### Commitment to Consumption  
Chatstrike is dedicated to implementing this structured markup within its jobs platform, ensuring that these enhancements are actively utilized to improve the candidate experience. Additionally, Chatstrike will be collaborating with Google For Jobs to integrate the new schema, aiming to significantly enhance the candidate experience on a global scale.

## Recommended Additions:

### New Properties of `JobPosting`

| Property      | Expected Type      | Description      |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| `recruiter`    | `Person`    | The person responsible for recruiting candidates for the job.    |
| `hiringManager`    | `Person`    | The person overseeing the hiring process for the position.    |
| `jobVideo`   | `VideoObject`    | A video associated with the job posting (e.g., job overview).    |
| `interviewProcess`    | Array of `Interview` objects    | A sequence of interviews associated with the job posting, detailing each stage of the interview process.   |


### New Instances of `Person`

| Property      | On Types      | Description      |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| `recruiter`    | `JobPosting`    | The person responsible for recruiting candidates for the job.    |
| `hiringManager`    | `JobPosting`    | The person overseeing the hiring process for the position.    |


### New Type: `Interview`... Thing > Intangible > Interview

| Property      | Expected Type      | Description      |
|----------------|----------------|----------------|
| `interviewer`    | `Person`    | The individual conducting the interview (e.g., hiring manager, team lead).    |
| `interviewmode`    | `Text`    | The mode of the interview (e.g., "phone," "video," "in-person," "messaging").    |
| `durationOfInterview`   | `Text`    | The expected duration of the interview itself (e.g., “30 minutes”, “1 hour”).    |
| `timeToNextStage`    | `Text`    | The expected time until the next stage of the interview process (e.g., "2-5 days").   |


### Example
```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "JobPosting",
  "title": "Software Engineer",
  "description": "We are looking for a Software Engineer to join our team.",
  "datePosted": "2024-10-28",
  "validThrough": "2024-11-28T00:00:00Z",
  "employmentType": "FULL_TIME",
  "recruiter": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "John Doe",
    "image": "https://example.com/johndoe.jpg",
    "jobTitle": "Recruiter",
    "url": "https://example.com/johndoe",
    "video": {
      "@type": "VideoObject",
      "name": "John Doe - Recruiter Introduction",
      "description": "An introductory video about John Doe, the recruiter.",
      "thumbnailUrl": "https://example.com/johndoe-thumbnail.jpg",
      "uploadDate": "2024-10-28",
      "duration": "PT1M30S",
      "contentUrl": "https://example.com/johndoe-video.mp4",
      "embedUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/embed/samplevideo"
    }
  },
  "hiringManager": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Jane Smith",
    "image": "https://example.com/janesmith.jpg",
    "jobTitle": "Hiring Manager",
    "url": "https://example.com/janesmith",
    "video": {
      "@type": "VideoObject",
      "name": "Jane Smith - Hiring Manager Overview",
      "description": "An introductory video about Jane Smith, the hiring manager.",
      "thumbnailUrl": "https://example.com/janesmith-thumbnail.jpg",
      "uploadDate": "2024-10-28",
      "duration": "PT1M45S",
      "contentUrl": "https://example.com/janesmith-video.mp4",
      "embedUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/embed/samplevideo"
    }
  },
  "jobVideo": {
    "@type": "VideoObject",
    "name": "Job Overview for Software Engineer",
    "description": "A video explaining the responsibilities and benefits of the Software Engineer position.",
    "thumbnailUrl": "https://example.com/job-thumbnail.jpg",
    "uploadDate": "2024-10-28",
    "duration": "PT2M30S",
    "contentUrl": "https://example.com/job-video.mp4",
    "embedUrl": "https://www.youtube.com/embed/samplejobvideo"
  },
  "interviewProcess": [
    {
      "@type": "Interview",
      "interviewer": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "The hiring manager"
      },
      "interviewMode": "Phone",
      "timeToNextStage": "2-5 days"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Interview",
      "interviewer": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "The technical lead"
      },
      "interviewMode": "Video",
      "timeToNextStage": "3-7 days"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Interview",
      "interviewer": {
        "@type": "Person",
        "name": "The HR representative"
      },
      "interviewMode": "In-person",
      "timeToNextStage": "1-2 weeks"
    }
  ]
}
```

issues.title: Implement protections against spam
issues.author: mfhepp
issues.body:
The amount of spammy new issues and comments in issues has reached a level that is putting collaboration in its entirety at risk.

The problem is not limited to the schema.org repository (others are facing similar problems), but we cannot wait for Github to offer a solution.

## Immediate Action

- [x] **Limiting interaction to exiting users and contributors for a certain period,** see <https://docs.github.com/en/communities/moderating-comments-and-conversations/limiting-interactions-in-your-repository#about-temporary-interaction-limits>
- [x] **Blocking ~~and reporting~~ all user accounts engaged in spam** for all repositories of the schemaorg organization on Github.
- [x] **Ideally, also delete the old spam issues, as they might contain links to malicious content.**

For the moment, I see no other way than to disable notifications from this repository, which basically blocks effective collaboration.

~~These steps require admin rights for the repository - who has those?~~

/CC @danbri @rvguha @tmarshbing 

## Long-Term Approach

- [ ] Evaluate how suitable Github issues are for soliciting feedback and suggestions from the large, heterogeneous group of stakeholders.
- [ ] **Adding a template for new issues that (1) increases the effort for creating a new issue and (2) eases the detection of spammy issues**, see <https://docs.github.com/en/communities/using-templates-to-encourage-useful-issues-and-pull-requests/configuring-issue-templates-for-your-repository>.
- [ ] Identify and block origins of spam on a regular basis.

issues.title: Proposal for New Schema Type: "OrganicCertification"
issues.author: MLSpyShop
issues.body:
Overview

The proposed organicCertification schema type would support businesses, products, and organizations that follow recognized organic standards, enabling them to present structured data about organic certifications, including the certifying body, standard, status, and purity percentage (e.g., 100%, 95%, 70% organic). This schema type will provide consumers with transparent, structured information on organic certifications, enhancing trust and search visibility for certified organic products.

1. Purpose

The organic market has seen exponential growth as consumers increasingly prioritize organic and sustainable products. To support this demand for transparency, the organicCertification schema type can serve as a way for businesses and producers to display verified organic certifications within search results, fostering trust and simplifying decision-making for consumers. This schema type would also offer search engines structured information to deliver rich results, better matching consumer queries with certified organic products.

2. Proposed Schema Details

Type: organicCertification

	•	Properties:
	•	certificationBody (Text): Name of the organization that issued the certification (e.g., USDA, EU Organic, Canada Organic).
	•	certificationStandard (Text): Specific standard or regulation for organic certification (e.g., USDA Organic, EU Organic Regulation 2018/848).
	•	dateIssued (Date): Date the certification was issued.
	•	expirationDate (Date): Expiration date of the certification, if applicable.
	•	certificationID (Text): A unique identifier for the certification, such as a registration or document number.
	•	certificationStatus (Text): Current status of the certification (e.g., “active,” “expired,” “revoked”).
	•	scope (Text): The specific scope of certification (e.g., “Crop,” “Livestock,” “Processing”).
	•	certifiedEntity (Thing): Reference to the product or organization that has been certified.
	•	organicPurity (Text): Percentage of organic purity in the certified product, specified as “100%,” “95%,” “70%,” etc., reflecting common standards for organic purity.

Example in JSON-LD:

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Organic Hemp Oil",
  "organicCertification": {
    "@type": "organicCertification",
    "certificationBody": "USDA",
    "certificationStandard": "USDA Organic",
    "dateIssued": "2024-01-01",
    "expirationDate": "2025-01-01",
    "certificationID": "12345-USDA",
    "certificationStatus": "active",
    "scope": "Crop",
    "certifiedEntity": "Hemp Oil",
    "organicPurity": "95%"
  }
}

3. Key Use Cases

	•	Product Transparency: Organic products can specify purity levels such as “95% Organic” or “100% Organic,” along with full certification details, helping consumers make informed choices based on certified organic content.
	•	Visibility for Organic Businesses: Organizations involved in organic production, farming, or processing can display their certification status, enhancing visibility for organic products.
	•	Structured Data for Certifiers: Certifying bodies or organizations can leverage this schema to structure data about their issued certifications, including the purity level, scope, and validity.

4. Benefits

Consumer Trust and Transparency

This schema type allows consumers to see certification details, including purity percentage, certification body, and scope, directly in search results. This transparency is critical in organic markets, where consumers are often willing to pay a premium for genuinely certified organic products.

Enhanced SEO for Organic Products

By providing structured data specific to organic certifications, products and businesses gain the opportunity for rich results that distinguish certified products in search results, potentially increasing click-through rates and conversion.

Compliance with Organic Standards

Most organic certification standards include defined purity levels (e.g., “95% Organic” for USDA Organic). Including the organicPurity property in the schema aligns with these standards, ensuring structured data accurately represents regulatory compliance.

Support for Certification Bodies and Market Growth

Certifiers and brands can use this schema to provide structured, verifiable information about organic certifications, fostering growth in the organic and sustainable product market.

5. Similar Types and Gaps

Existing schema types, such as Product and Organization, provide a general structure but do not support the specific data needed for organic certification. The offers property covers general offers but lacks specificity for compliance or certification, particularly for international organic standards.

The organicCertification type fills this gap by adding critical properties directly related to certification status, scope, and purity level.

6. Community Impact

As the global organic product market grows, consumers, certifiers, and producers will benefit from structured data representing organic certifications. This schema type aligns with the mission of Schema.org to support evolving data needs, creating a more meaningful and transparent web. The inclusion of organic certification data within Schema.org vocabulary could lead to broader adoption across search engines, e-commerce platforms, and organic certifying bodies.

7. Implementation Roadmap

	1.	Community Feedback: Initial community review of the organicCertification proposal, gathering input on the proposed properties and any additional requirements.
	2.	Initial Draft: Create and publish an initial draft specification on Schema.org, including detailed documentation, usage guidelines, and JSON-LD examples.
	3.	Testing and Validation: Schema.org and community members test the new type, refining properties as necessary for optimal implementation.
	4.	Finalization: Following feedback, finalize the organicCertification type and integrate it into the Schema.org vocabulary.
	5.	Promotion and Adoption: Work with certifying bodies, e-commerce platforms, and SEO professionals to promote the adoption of organicCertification for organic products.

This proposal for organicCertification is designed to meet the demands of a growing organic marketplace, supporting transparency, consumer trust, and accurate representation of certification standards across digital platforms.

This structured proposal provides all the necessary details to guide Schema.org maintainers and community members in reviewing and discussing the new schema.

issues.title: Proposal for new Type: WebSerial
issues.author: ladyisidore
issues.body:
I searched the issues to see if this has come up before, and it seems not — if it has and I just overlooked it, I apologise.

There's a vast and growing body of prose fiction published chapter-by-chapter online, constituting a single work. The current extant types (`Book` and `BookSeries` in specific) don't quite seem to cut it, given the nature of serialised fiction. Each discrete update/chapter may be a more-or-less standalone short story or novella, or a short story or novella that constitutes part of a series (think modern TV series). There _is_ a generic `CreativeWorkSeries` Type, but it seems to mostly exist to group together `BookSeries`, `TVSeries`, etc.

Granted, quite a lot of the really popular series go on to be published as books, but in those cases, the final published books and the original serial vary somehow, or at least the chapter numbering is different.

I think mirroring `TVSeries` and applicable properties would form the bulk of the work. I _personally_ think there ought to also be a `collectedAs` property with an expected type of `Book`, and a corresponding `serialisedAs` property for `Book`, and a `originallySerialisedAt` property for `Book`. Specifying in which volume a specific `WebSerialChapter` was published might or might not need a new property — maybe `isPartOf` would do? 

Another alternative is having a `WebSeries` Type, with a `format` property expecting a `WebSeriesFormat` Type (comprising `Book`, `Podcast`, `Video`, etc.)? 

I don't know, maybe this is too niche a concern. Figured I'd float it anyway. Apologies for any (n)etiquette gaffes, first time trying something like this!

issues.title: Proposal for New Schema.org Types: `Sitemap` and `SitemapIndex` with Extended Properties
issues.author: ghost
issues.body:
### Problem Description:  
Currently, Schema.org provides excellent tools for structured data, but it lacks specific types to describe **sitemaps**, which are critical for indexing and understanding website structures. Sitemaps play a vital role in connecting content for search engines and other automated tools. Introducing `Sitemap` and `SitemapIndex` types will unify the description of sitemaps and offer the following benefits:  

1. **Unified Vocabulary:**  
   A standardized approach for defining sitemaps within Schema.org.  

2. **Consistent Terminology:**  
   Using Schema.org properties eliminates ambiguity and redundancy.  

3. **Enhanced Connections:**  
   Allows linking sitemaps with rich metadata and related resources (e.g., media, datasets).  

4. **Extensibility of Sitemaps:**  
   Additional properties like `priority`, `expires`, `changeFrequency`, and others can be used to enrich sitemap descriptions.  

---

### Proposal:  
Add the following new types:  

1. **`SitemapIndex`:**  
   A type representing an index of multiple sitemaps.  

2. **`Sitemap`:**  
   A type representing a single sitemap containing links to resources.  

Additionally, include a new property `changeFrequency`, which specifies how often a resource is expected to change. The format for `changeFrequency` would be a number followed by a time unit, e.g., `5min` (5 minutes) or `1year` (1 year). Supported units include:  

- `ms` (milliseconds)  
- `sec` (seconds)  
- `min` (minutes)  
- `hour` (hours)  
- `day` (days)  
- `week` (weeks)  
- `month` (months)  
- `year` (years)  

---

### Example 1: Sitemap Index  
```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "SitemapIndex",
  "@id": "http://example.com/SitemapIndex.jsonld",
  "name": "Sitemap Index",
  "itemListElement": [
    {
      "@type": "Sitemap",
      "url": "http://example.com/sitemap_1.jsonld",
      "dateModified": "2024-11-07",
      "priority": 1.0,
      "changeFrequency": "1day"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Sitemap",
      "url": "http://example.com/sitemap_2.jsonld",
      "dateModified": "2024-11-07",
      "priority": 0.8,
      "changeFrequency": "1week"
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Example 2: Detailed Sitemap  
```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Sitemap",
  "@id": "http://example.com/sitemap_1.jsonld",
  "name": "Sitemap",
  "dateCreated": "2024-12-01T08:00:00Z",
  "itemListElement": [
    {
      "@type": "WebPage",
      "url": "http://example.com/en/brand_502/",
      "dateModified": "2024-12-01T08:00:00Z",
      "changeFrequency": "1day",
      "expires": "2024-12-10T08:00:00Z",
      "inLanguage": "en",
      "keywords": ["brand", "products"]
    },
    {
      "@type": "ImageObject",
      "url": "http://example.com/images/brand_502.jpg",
      "contentSize": "2MB",
      "encodingFormat": "JPEG",
      "dateModified": "2024-12-01T08:00:00Z",
      "changeFrequency": "1month",
      "expires": "2024-12-10T08:00:00Z",
      "keywords": ["image", "brand"]
    },
    {
      "@type": "VideoObject",
      "url": "http://example.com/videos/brand_502.mp4",
      "contentSize": "100MB",
      "encodingFormat": "MP4",
      "duration": "PT3M25S",
      "dateModified": "2024-11-25T08:00:00Z",
      "changeFrequency": "1year",
      "keywords": ["video", "brand"]
    }
  ]
}
```

---

### Suggested Properties for `Sitemap` and `SitemapIndex`:  
- `priority` (Number): Importance of the resource relative to others.  
- `expires` (DateTime): Expiration date of the resource.  
- `changeFrequency` (Text): Frequency of changes using time units (`1sec`, `5min`, `1day`, etc.).  
- `keywords` (Text): Keywords describing the resource.  

Other unspecified properties should be logically acceptable and support flexible extensibility, allowing developers to adapt the `Sitemap` and `SitemapIndex` types to their unique use cases without conflicting with the overall semantic framework.  

---

### Benefits for the Community:  
1. **Semantic Consistency:** Provides a unified way to describe sitemaps using structured data.  
2. **Improved Indexing:** Helps search engines and tools better understand sitemaps and their contents.  
3. **Scalability:** Supports additional properties and extensions for advanced use cases.  
4. **Cross-Resource Connections:** Enables rich linking of web pages, media, datasets, and more within sitemaps.  

---

issues.title: Proposal for Schema.org: Create an XML Schema.org Vocabulary
issues.author: ghost
issues.body:
### Proposal for Schema.org: Create an XML Schema.org Vocabulary #### **Problem Statement** Currently, existing XML standards like `sitemap.xml`, `RSS`, `Atom`, and others are limited in scope and fail to provide comprehensive semantic descriptions of data. They require extensions, which leads to incompatible implementations tailored for each platform (Google, Bing, Yandex, etc.). This approach creates barriers to interoperability and harms SEO, as developers must adapt their data to meet the specific requirements of each search engine. Consequently, the core idea of standards—uniformity and semantic compatibility—is lost. #### **Proposed Solution** We propose creating an XML-based Schema.org vocabulary that combines the advantages of existing standards and XML extensibility to address compatibility issues. This vocabulary will adhere to Schema.org specifications, enabling a highly detailed semantic description of data. #### **Example Implementation** Here is an example of a publications feed using the proposed format: ```xml Web-Lexicon-Blog https://example.com/feed.xml A feed of publications about new articles and/or products SEO en 2024-12-04 https://example.com/images/icons/icon-192x192.png 192 192 image/png Jane Doe https://example.com/About/team#Bob mailto:bob-doe@xyz.com (425) 123-4567 https://example.com Web-Lexicon https://example.com/logo.png
2014-07-01 https://example.com/Alice Advanced SEO Strategies for 2025 article description Alice SEO https://example.com/images/articles/image.png 512 512 image/jpg
2015-01-02 https://example.com/Bob Advanced SEO Strategies for 2024 article description Bob SEO https://example.com/images/articles/image.png 512 512 image/jpg How Web Semantics, SEO, and Creating a CMS from Scratch Change the Approach to Development

Modern web development is not just about writing code and creating attractive interfaces...

]]>
``` #### **Advantages of XML as a Format for the Vocabulary** 1. **Standards for Linking and Connectivity:** - XML is ideal for describing complex relationships between data (via technologies like `XLink`, `XInclude` and `XPointer`). - It supports referencing other resources, both local and remote. 2. **Standards for Data Processing:** - XML is easy to parse and transform using standards like XSLT. - Validation through XSD (XML Schema) ensures adherence to structure and rules. 3. **Wide Support:** - XML is supported by numerous programming languages and libraries. - It integrates seamlessly with existing systems. 4. **Universality and Extensibility:** - XML can describe virtually any data structure. - New elements can be added without breaking compatibility. 5. **Cross-Platform Consistency:** - XML files are rendered the same across all devices and systems. #### **Single Drawback** The verbosity of XML may be seen as a drawback, but modern compression and data transfer technologies (e.g., GZIP) effectively mitigate this issue. #### **Conclusion** The creation of an XML-based Schema.org vocabulary will open up new possibilities for unifying data processing and resolving the issues caused by incompatible semantic standards. This is especially crucial for improving SEO and simplifying the development of universal parsers.

issues.title: Average/aggregate information in a list
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
We (Google) have a desire to represent rolled up information about a set of items in a list.

For example, you have a list of Products (some of which are not present on a given URL) and you want to capture the "average price". 

Or you have a list of LocalBusiness and you want to capture "average rating".

In both of those cases, it's very possible the full data to represent is not present in the invididual items and/or are not fully possible to include.

I've brainstormed a couple of different approaches for this, but the least impactful proposal is to attach a so:aggregateElement predicate with a range of so:Thing and then we can use the schema in the attached thing to hold the value.

So for the first case you'd have:
```
ItemList
   -name-> "Cool Products to buy"
   -numberOfItems -> 2
   -aggregateElement -> Product
        -price-> "40 USD"
   -itemListElement -> Product1
        -price-> "30 USD"
   -itemListElement -> Product2
        -price-> "50 USD"
```
  
This has the advatnage of a) being attached to the list itself for context, b) using composition instead of some sort of list inheritance or webpage subtype, c) reusing the item-level schema fields, though this is double-edged because the semantics are going to be different even though the fields may be reusable.

We could do things like use AggregateOffer and AggregateRating on those aggregate items, but I'm worried that we might need more flexibility in the future than just those two concepts for aggregateElement.

Thoughts?  Alternate suggestions?

issues.title: Link the primitive data types with XSD
issues.author: multimeric
issues.body:
The primitive data types such as `Text`, `Number`, `Boolean` etc should be linked to the same primitives in other systems. Otherwise it's difficult to translate data and schemas.

Currently the class definition for `Text` looks like this:
https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/blob/9e1c416bc446c54ffc823e54b9d9d9ff6588ce9a/data/schema.ttl#L3062-L3065

It is fairly common to use XSD definitions for primitives, for example they're used by OWL already. 

Therefore I suggest we add:
```diff
+ :sameAs xsd:string .
```

And do the same for the other primitives.

issues.title: Certified Organic Search
issues.author: MLSpyShop
issues.body:
Below is a proposal for expanding structured data to fully recognize the certified organic market. This proposal is designed to address the needs of SEO practitioners, search engine companies, organic market participants, and certification agencies. It leverages existing schema properties while extending them with organic-specific details—ensuring compatibility, clarity, and credibility.

Made with ChatGPT 03-Mini

Proposal: Enhancing the “certifications” Schema for Organic Products

1. Leverage the Existing “certifications” Property

Why:
	•	Compatibility & Simplicity: Using the established “certifications” property on schema.org/Product ensures that we build on a well-understood foundation. This minimizes the risk of incompatibility with search engines and existing data consumers.
	•	Avoid Redundancy: Instead of introducing a redundant field like “certificationType,” the very use of an organic-specific type (OrganicCertification) inherently conveys that the certification is for organic standards.

2. Define the OrganicCertification Type

Purpose:
Create a dedicated type that extends the standard certification schema with organic-specific attributes. This helps to clearly signal the organic nature of the product certification without adding unnecessary or redundant fields.

Core Attributes:
	•	@type:
Set to "OrganicCertification", indicating that the certification pertains specifically to organic standards.
	•	certificationBody:
An object (referencing schema:Organization) representing the authority issuing the certification (e.g., “USDA Organic” or “EU Organic”).
	•	certificationID:
A unique identifier that allows traceability back to the certification agency’s records.
	•	organicPurityLevel:
A property to indicate the level of organic purity (expressed as “100%”, “95%”, “70%”, etc.), which is a key detail for consumers and regulatory purposes.
	•	validFrom / validThrough:
Date fields that denote the validity period of the certification, ensuring that only current and active certifications are presented.

Why:
	•	For SEO Practitioners: This structure provides rich, relevant details that can enable enhanced search snippets (rich results), leading to better user engagement.
	•	For Search Engines: Clear, non-redundant, and well-documented data simplifies automated parsing and improves indexing.
	•	For Organic Market Participants & Certification Agencies: Detailed, standardized information builds trust, ensures transparency, and facilitates verification across the organic certification ecosystem.

3. Sample JSON‑LD Implementations

Direct Association on the Product

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Organic Apple Juice",
  "certifications": {
    "@type": "OrganicCertification",
    "certificationBody": {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "name": "USDA Organic"
    },
    "certificationID": "USDA-ORG-123456",
    "organicPurityLevel": "100%",
    "validFrom": "2021-01-01",
    "validThrough": "2026-12-31"
  }
}

Nested Within an Offer (if the certification relates to a specific offer)

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Organic Almond Milk",
  "offers": {
    "@type": "Offer",
    "price": "4.99",
    "priceCurrency": "USD",
    "certifications": {
      "@type": "OrganicCertification",
      "certificationBody": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "USDA Organic"
      },
      "certificationID": "USDA-ORG-123456",
      "organicPurityLevel": "100%",
      "validFrom": "2021-01-01",
      "validThrough": "2026-12-31"
    }
  }
}

4. Additional Product-Level Attributes (Optional)

In scenarios where more than certification details are needed at the product level, consider adding:
	•	organicStandard:
A property that specifies the organic standard used (e.g., “USDA Organic”, “EU Organic”, “JAS Organic”).
	•	sourcingInformation:
Details on the origin of the organic ingredients.
	•	productionMethod:
A description or link to information about how the product is produced (e.g., “Cold-pressed extraction without additives”).

Why:
These additional attributes further support transparency and allow consumers and regulatory bodies to verify organic claims, reinforcing the credibility of the product in the organic market.

5. Controlled Vocabularies and Documentation

Recommendations:
	•	Controlled Vocabularies:
Where possible, link properties such as certificationBody and organicPurityLevel to controlled vocabularies or standardized term sets. This ensures consistency across implementations and simplifies data aggregation.
	•	Comprehensive Documentation:
Document the custom extension thoroughly. Explain that OrganicCertification is an extension of the generic certification data, detailing each property and providing usage examples. This documentation is essential for developers, SEO practitioners, and certification agencies alike.
	•	Fallback Options:
In environments where custom types are not fully supported, map OrganicCertification properties to widely accepted types like schema:PropertyValue or schema:DefinedTerm. This guarantees that the data remains interpretable.

Why:
Documentation and controlled vocabularies enhance the overall reliability and interoperability of the data, ensuring that all stakeholders—from search engines to certification bodies—can interpret the information accurately.

6. Validation and Future-Proofing

Action Steps:
	•	Regular Testing:
Use tools such as the Bing Markup Validator and other structured data testing tools to validate your implementation.
	•	Community Engagement:
Monitor updates on schema.org and consider engaging with the community to propose the formal adoption of the OrganicCertification extension. This will help future-proof your implementation and ensure ongoing compatibility.

Why:
Regular validation and community engagement not only guarantee that your markup remains accurate but also help adapt to evolving standards and search engine requirements over time.

Final Thoughts

This proposal presents a comprehensive, multi-stakeholder approach to enhancing structured data for organic product certifications. By leveraging the existing “certifications” property and defining an OrganicCertification type with specific, non-redundant attributes (such as organicPurityLevel and validity dates), we create a robust system that:
	•	For SEO Practitioners: Increases visibility and supports rich search results, driving user engagement.
	•	For Search Engines: Provides clear, well-structured data that simplifies parsing and indexing, leading to better search result quality.
	•	For Organic Market Participants: Enhances transparency, builds consumer trust, and aids in product differentiation.
	•	For Certification Agencies: Ensures accurate, traceable, and verifiable certification data, supporting regulatory compliance and market integrity.

By adhering to these principles and documenting the implementation thoroughly, the organic certification ecosystem can benefit from increased clarity, consistency, and efficiency in both online search and industry operations.

Sources for Further Reading:
	•	Bing Webmaster Tools Structured Data Guidelines
	•	Bing Markup Validator
	•	Schema.org/Product

This proposal balances technical feasibility, industry needs, and SEO best practices—ensuring that organic certifications are communicated effectively and remain future-proof.

issues.author: TobiasNx
issues.body:
I saw that schema.org does not have DOI as property.

You surely know that DOIs are in context of  academic, professional, and government publications and research important persistent identifiers that should enable DOI resolvers to link to the identified object. DOIs are also important for libraries and publishers.

Therefore I suggest DOI as a new subproperty of `identitifer`.

issues.title: Proposal - rebrandedTo to describe Organization merging / rebranding into another Organization
issues.author: redphoenix2uk
issues.body:
I am writing a big piece of structured data for a large organization who have acquired many organizations over the years, merging the old organisation names into the current company. 

There isn't currently a way to accurately describe this. 

I am currently using Organization (Company A) > subOrganization (Company B) 
Company B then has a dissolutionDate specified
Company A's sameAs also contains Company B's sameAs

I therefore propose a new schema property called "**rebrandedTo**". 

This would only accept the following types:
- Organization (and all its subtypes)
- LocalBusiness (and all its subtypes)

and be used on the following types:
- Organization (and all its subtypes)
- LocalBusiness (and all its subtypes)

This new property would be used to describe Organizations or LocalBusinesses which have been acquired by another business or merged into that business. 

It would be even better if we could have a property such as "rebrandDate" to say the date when Company B was rebranded as Company A. 

I imagine it would look something like this: 
`        {
          "@type": "Organization",
          "name": "Company A",
          "@id": "https://www.example.com/#organization",
          "alternateName": ["Company B"],
          "legalName": "Company A Inc.",
 		  "subOrganization": [
            {
              "@type": "Organization",
              "name": "Company B",
              "legalName": "Company B, Inc.",
              "dissolutionDate": "2022-11-03",
              "rebrandedTo": {
              	"@type": "Organization",
              	"name": "Company A",
                "@id": "https://www.example.com/#organization",
                "rebrandDate": "2022-11-03"
              }
           }`

If there is currently a better way of doing this that I've not found, please can you let me know. Thank you very much

issues.title: Cloud resource modeling vocabularies
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
We're interested in establishing some flexible but tighter than key-value pair schema associations to describe cloud resources in a cross-platform way.

For example:

```
{ "@type": "CloudResource",
  "additionalTag": [{ "@type": "StructuredValue", "name": "foo", "value": "bar" }],
  "environment": "http://schema.org/EnvironmentProduction",
  "costCenter": "http://schema.org/CostCenterEngineering"
}
```
(note the mixture of enum-ranged fields along with key-value pairs).

I'm unfamiliar with the schema/vocabularies in this space and was curious if there were some existing enums/predicates in some other vocabulary.  Generally we wouldn't want to duplicate a lot of the work in schema.org if one already existed.

# Background regarding the legal information required on company run websites in Europe
Germany, Austria and other jurisdiction require companies (organizations) to publish all legal information of a company on their website. Also Google does that for example here:
[Google Germany Imprint](https://www.google.de/contact/impressum.html)

In fact for example to be eligible to run Google Ads [you are required to ad the information to your own website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/14675634?hl=en).

It is advised by many search engines to use this page (or any other about us page) to contain the structured data about the website publishing organization. Facebook for example also allows to add the information to pages:
[Add an Impressum to your Facebook Page](https://www.facebook.com/help/342430852516247)

We seemingly have everything in there inside organization, but not the basic legal fields that are even required by Google to do certain things.

Fixes: #4366 

# Addition of new properties to Organization

To allow standardisation of the information set I have tried with this PR to align the organization structured data with the legal requirements of the imprint by allowing more values. 

- legalRepresentative (Person): the legal representative of a company such as CEO or managing director.
- company registration (certification): the company registry number and the issuer of the number. 

Upon close inspection following values are not mandatory but can be contained in the Imprint:
- Common Stock Capital of your LLC or unlisted company (eg. 10.000 EUR of which 2.500 EUR Paid up);
legal representative

# Example Implementation

The example below contains also a proposal for stock capital, if desired. 

```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "url": "https://www.google.com",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://example.net/profile/example1234",
    "https://example.org/example1234"
  ],
  "logo": "https://www.google.com/images/logo.png",
  "name": "Google",
  "legalName": "Alphabet LLC",
  "legalRepresentative": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Larry Page"
  },
  "hasCompanyRegistration": {
    "@type": "Certification",
    "issuedBy": {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "name": "Chamber of Commerce of Wondertown"
    },
    "name": "Company Registration",
    "certificationIdentification": "WT-123456"
  },
  "description": "The example corporation is well-known for producing high-quality widgets",
  "email": "contact@example.com",
  "telephone": "+47-99-999-9999",
  "address": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "Rue Improbable 99",
    "addressLocality": "Paris",
    "addressCountry": "FR",
    "addressRegion": "Ile-de-France",
    "postalCode": "75001"
  },
  "legalAddress": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "Rue Improbable 99",
    "addressLocality": "Paris",
    "addressCountry": "FR",
    "addressRegion": "Ile-de-France",
    "postalCode": "75001"
  },
  "vatID": "FR12345678901",
  "iso6523Code": "0199:724500PMK2A2M1SQQ228"
}
```

issues.title: The suggestedAge page could use a JSON-LD example
issues.author: ell1e
issues.body:
Coming from #3688 the page explaining "suggested age" seems to be so minimal that it's hard to understand how it's meant to be used: https://schema.org/suggestedAge For example, it says "The age or age range for the intended audience or person, for example 3-12 months for infants, 1-5 years for toddlers." but it doesn't say how that would be expressed in JSON. While it links https://schema.org/QuantitativeValue if I go there, I can find this JSON example:

```
{
    "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
    “minValue”: 2500,
    “maxValue”: 7500,
    "unitCode": "USD"
}
```
This would suggest that a suggested age may be intended to look like this:
```
{
    "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
    “minValue”: 1,
    “maxValue”: 5,
    "unitCode": "???? year or what do I put here??"
}
```
However, this neither explains what unitCode to use for years and months, nor is it that quick to find given how complex `QuantitativeValue` is. If I follow two other links (which already seems like a lot to find this basic information) I find the explanation `The unit of measurement given using the UN/CEFACT Common Code (3 characters) or a URL` but again no common examples, particularly also not for months or years, and also not any link to any page that has a table with codes.

Furthermore, it's not obvious from any of the pages whether the upper bound of "suggestedAge" is meant to be optional. Based on this third-party page it is: https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product-variants This seems like vital information.

I therefore suggest that a few JSON-LD examples are added to https://schema.org/suggestedAge that 1. show how to specify a range in months, 2. show how to specify a range in years, and 3. show that the upper bound can be omitted.

issues.title: QuantitativeValue passes validation even if unitcode shouldn't
issues.author: fthobe
issues.body:
@alex-jansen @mfhepp this might interest you as you have worked on this in the past. 

schema.org provides the possibility to insert additional numeric values as properties to resources in form of a `QuantitativeValue`.

@ell1e raised the issue #4390 that `suggestedAge` that asked which unit code to use for years or months to indicate the suggested age range for an artwork as visible in the code below (example from [Google](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/product-variants) as she wanted to define a suggested audience for a book: 

```
        "audience": {
          "@type": "PeopleAudience",
          "suggestedGender": "unisex",
          "suggestedAge": {
            "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
            "minValue": 13,
            "unitCode": "ANN"
          }
```

In fact upon closer various inconsistencies can be found: 

UnitCode should according to documentation consist of 
> The unit of measurement given using the UN/CEFACT Common Code (3 characters) or a URL. Other codes than the UN/CEFACT Common Code may be used with a prefix followed by a colon.

Hereby it was noted that CEFACT does not provide units such as YEAR(S), MONTH(S) or DAY(S), but solely formatting schemes for dates as visible [here](https://unece.org/sites/default/files/2023-10/Rec07-WP4-INF-108E.pdf). 

During testing of a code snippet inside the validators (Google as well Schema) neither threw an error upon using a unit code that is neither UN/CEFACT compatible (as the Google example `"unitCode": "ANN"` according to docs can't be) nor a link.

So we have three cans of worms here: 
1) A CEFACT `unitcode` can't be used for `suggestedAge` as the underlying unit does not exist in the referenced specifications, but somehow unitcode still validates with any value inserted, in fact other uses for quantitative describe it better such as billingduration
> Specifies for how long this price (or price component) will be billed. Can be used, for example, to model the contractual duration of a subscription or payment plan. Type can be either a Duration or a Number (in which case the unit of measurement, for example month, is specified by the unitCode property).
leaving nevertheless space to be defined better;
2) [`unitText`](https://schema.org/unitText) could be used offering "years" and "months", but that would mean rendering something really interesting very variable in outcome;
3) the documentation needs to be adjusted, probably an example should be given.

In fact Google cooks an entirely different soup by using [this in merchant listing](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/merchant-listing): 
> [Number](https://schema.org/Number)
>
> The suggested maximum age for the product, in years. Google maps the maximum suggested ages for products onto the following fixed set of numerical values:
>
> 0.25: For newborns
> 1.0: For infants
> 5.0: For toddlers
> 13.0: For kids

And in addition AgeGroup for Google Shopping for [XML](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6324463?hl=en) and [rest](https://developers.google.com/shopping-content/reference/rest/v2.1/products?sjid=11354460860531256264-EU):

> Newborn [newborn]
0-3 months old. Newborn sizes are often identified by the age range in months (0–3) or just “newborn.”
Infant [infant]
3–12 months old. Infant sizes are often identified by the age range in months (3–12).
Toddler [toddler]
1–5 years old. Toddler sizes are often identified by the age range in months (12–24) or years (1–5).
Kids [kids]
5–13 years old. Children's sizes are often identified by the age range in years (5-13).
Adult [adult]
Typically teens or older (13 years old or more). All sizes within this age group have been manufactured to fit an adult or teen.

They are basically breaking everything down to 5 categories: 
1. Newborn at 0-3 months
2. Infant at 3-12 months
3. Toddler at 1-5 years
4. Kids at 5-13 years
5. Adult

Both (structured data guide as well as google shopping) therefore follow the same structure with different syntax.

# Considerations
In reality recommendedAge is displaying a [duration](https://schema.org/duration) and schema.org does already display them following an ISO standard, but that definition seems to be counterintuitive for age recommendations. 

In reality a couple of very similar age recommendations are spread across the standard: 
1. `suggestedAge` that can be applied to `peopleAudience` and `sizespecification` as discussed in #2811 and modified by #2914 
2. `requiredMaxAge` and `requiredMinAge` that can be attached to `PeopleAudience`
3. `typicalAgeRange` which seems to be very similar to `suggestedAge` as part of `CreativeWork` and `Event`. 

Maybe this would be a chance to fix unitCode for ages and also consolidate typicalAgeRange and suggestedAge as it's hard to imagine having both at the same time in the same context by introducing an `audienceAgeUnit` allowing "Years" and "Months", which would also allow a better visualisation on search frontends.  

# Examples 

All examples have been tried against schema and google validator.

issues.title: Proposal: New subclasses of Person: FictionalPerson, ArtificialPerson, MythologicalPerson, SymbolicPerson
issues.author: slavabelaev
issues.body:
## Summary

This proposal suggests adding new subclasses to `schema:Person` to represent categories of persons that differ fundamentally in their ontological nature and cannot be adequately modeled using properties alone:

- `FictionalPerson`
- `ArtificialPerson`
- `MythologicalPerson`
- `SymbolicPerson`

These subclasses reflect person-like entities whose essential nature is not merely contextual or role-based, but intrinsic and distinguishable from typical `Person` instances.

---

## Rationale

Many contextual roles (e.g., employee, student, volunteer) can and should be described using properties such as `worksFor`, `memberOf`, or `volunteerFor`. However, the following categories represent fundamentally distinct types of persons that are not reducible to such properties:

### 1. `FictionalPerson`
A person that exists only within a fictional universe or narrative.  
- Example: Sherlock Holmes, Lara Croft, Jon Snow  
- Not describable simply by setting `isFictional` or similar — needs semantic differentiation for disambiguation and structured data clarity.

### 2. `ArtificialPerson`
A digital agent or AI entity that simulates human-like interaction or presence.  
- Example: ChatGPT, Yandex Alice, Replika  
- These are neither software applications nor real people, but digital personifications deserving distinct treatment.

### 3. `MythologicalPerson`
A person-like entity from mythology, legend, or religion.  
- Example: Zeus, Odin, Osiris  
- Different from fictional characters in cultural and religious significance.

### 4. `SymbolicPerson`
A personification or anthropomorphic representation of a concept, nation, or ideology.  
- Example: Uncle Sam, Mother Russia, Britannia  
- These symbolic figures can be meaningfully described using many `Person` properties (e.g., `name`, `image`, `affiliation`) but are fundamentally distinct from real or fictional persons.

---

## Proposed Type Hierarchy

- `schema:Person`
  - `schema:FictionalPerson`
  - `schema:ArtificialPerson`
  - `schema:MythologicalPerson`
  - `schema:SymbolicPerson`

---

## Implementation

Initial implementations could define only the type itself with a minimal number of specific examples. No new properties are required to begin with, though extensions may follow based on community needs.

---

## Benefits

- Enhanced semantic clarity across cultural, fictional, and digital domains
- Better indexing and search capabilities for knowledge graphs and search engines
- Improved modeling for cultural heritage, AI/tech platforms, and semantic publishing

---

## Compatibility Note

These new types do not conflict with existing schema.org structures and follow the pattern of `schema:Patient` as a meaningful subclass of `schema:Person` based on identity rather than role or property state.

issues.title: Legal Information for Organizations (Issue #4366)
issues.author: fthobe
issues.body:
The following commit completes legal information of Organizations to comply with the optional properties of an Imprint. Following properties have been added: 

- companyRegistration with the range Certification
- legalAddress with the range PostalAddress
- legalRepresentative with the range Person.

Closes: #4366 

# Background regarding the legal information required on company run websites in Europe
Germany, Austria and other jurisdiction require companies (organizations) to publish all legal information of a company on their website. Also Google does that for example here:
[Google Germany Imprint](https://www.google.de/contact/impressum.html)

In fact for example to be eligible to run Google Ads [you are required to ad the information to your own website](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/14675634?hl=en).

It is advised by many search engines to use this page (or any other about us page) to contain the structured data about the website publishing organization. Facebook for example also allows to add the information to pages:
[Add an Impressum to your Facebook Page](https://www.facebook.com/help/342430852516247)

We seemingly have everything in there inside organization, but not the basic legal fields that are even required by Google to do certain things.

Fixes: #4366 

# Addition of new properties to Organization

To allow standardisation of the information set I have tried with this PR to align the organization structured data with the legal requirements of the imprint by allowing more values. 

- legalRepresentative (Person): the legal representative of a company such as CEO or managing director.
- company registration (certification): the company registry number and the issuer of the number. 

Upon close inspection following values are not mandatory but can be contained in the Imprint:
- Common Stock Capital of your LLC or unlisted company (eg. 10.000 EUR of which 2.500 EUR Paid up);
legal representative

# Example Implementation

The example below contains also a proposal for stock capital, if desired. 

```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Organization",
  "url": "https://www.google.com",
  "sameAs": [
    "https://example.net/profile/example1234",
    "https://example.org/example1234"
  ],
  "logo": "https://www.google.com/images/logo.png",
  "name": "Google",
  "legalName": "Alphabet LLC",
  "legalRepresentative": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Larry Page"
  },
  "hasCompanyRegistration": {
    "@type": "Certification",
    "issuedBy": {
      "@type": "Organization",
      "name": "Chamber of Commerce of Wondertown"
    },
    "name": "Company Registration",
    "certificationIdentification": "WT-123456"
  },
  "description": "The example corporation is well-known for producing high-quality widgets",
  "email": "contact@example.com",
  "telephone": "+47-99-999-9999",
  "address": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "Rue Improbable 99",
    "addressLocality": "Paris",
    "addressCountry": "FR",
    "addressRegion": "Ile-de-France",
    "postalCode": "75001"
  },
  "legalAddress": {
    "@type": "PostalAddress",
    "streetAddress": "Rue Improbable 99",
    "addressLocality": "Paris",
    "addressCountry": "FR",
    "addressRegion": "Ile-de-France",
    "postalCode": "75001"
  },
  "vatID": "FR12345678901",
  "iso6523Code": "0199:724500PMK2A2M1SQQ228"
}
```

issues.title: Exchange Rate Specification does not contain source currency by default
issues.author: deepyes02
issues.body:
I felt this schema was built probably thinking that USD is the base currency for everything and this might be confusing for exchange rate services, specially those that provide multiple currency exchanges ! 

For example: 
```json
"mainEntity": {
        "@type": "ItemList",
        "itemListElement": [
            {
                "@type": "ExchangeRateSpecification",
                "currency": "CAD",
                "currentExchangeRate": {
                    "@type": "UnitPriceSpecification",
                    "price": 1.3571,
                    "priceCurrency": "CAD"
                },
                "description": "1 USD to CAD"
            },
```
It seems like **currency** in itemListElement and **priceCurrency** in currentExchangeRate both means the currency in which the return value is being realized by the user, i.e CAD in this case, leaving no room for describing the source currency or the base currency. 

For example, there is no official place to define PHP as base currency: 
```json
 {
                "@type": "ExchangeRateSpecification",
                "currency": "CAD",
                "currentExchangeRate": {
                    "@type": "UnitPriceSpecification",
                    "price": 0.0243,
                    "priceCurrency": "CAD"
                },
                "description": "1 PHP to CAD"
            }
```

I think this is a huge issue ! If I am wrong I look forward to hear solutions for this. Thank you !

issues.title: regionsAllowed vs. eligibleRegion on MediaObject
issues.author: suchajazzyline
issues.body:
Hello. Wanted to bring this to the group for consideration. It appears that the property [regionsAllowed](https://schema.org/regionsAllowed) only appears on [MediaObject](https://schema.org/MediaObject), while MediaObject also contains the [ineligibleRegion](https://schema.org/ineligibleRegion), which appears on multiple schemas, to serve as its inverse. However, I would expect MediaObject to use [eligibleRegion](https://schema.org/eligibleRegion) instead for consistency. Both properties are expected to use ISO 3166 format and serve similar functions.

Taking a different approach, there was an [older issue 974](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/974) that auto-closed addressing the lack of a true regionsAllowed inverse like regionsNotAllowed. [Issue 1741](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/1741) also gets at this a bit. Ideally, if regionsAllowed and ineligibleRegion were to remain as-is on MediaObject, perhaps the ineligibleRegion property description can be modified so it does not refer back to its inverse as being eligibleRegion? Thank you!

issues.title: Make Classes and Datatypes Visually Distinct
issues.author: plroebuck
issues.body:
As I've already been burnt by this [as previously reported](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4452), please begin using a simple convention to make things clearer -- like **all plain old datatypes (POD) should be displayed in lowercase only**.

Pseudo-datatypes are fine (e.g., `url` is a textstring that forms a W3C URL).
`Text`  would become `text`. Classes would continue to be named just as they are.

No one should have to *un-learn* all their previous experience in order to use schemas successfully, conceptually not unlike the [Don't Make Me Think](https://topuxd.com/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/dont-make-me-think-a-common-sense-approach-to-web-usability-2nd-ed-2005.pdf) and [Keep It Simple, Stupid](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KISS_principle) (KISS) approaches.

Although I'm creating an issue for it, this problem has certainly bitten other people as well.

Simplicity resolves complexity.

issues.title: Proposal (Performing Arts 1) - New sub-class of CreativeWork: PerformanceWork
issues.author: beatestermann
issues.body:
In their assessment of the schema.org ontology, the [Canadian Association for the Performing Arts (CAPACOA)](https://capacoa.ca/en/) and [its partners](https://linkeddigitalfuture.ca/community/) have encountered a lack of expressiveness of schema.org when it comes to describing **performing arts events (live events)** and related entities. We therefore propose the definition of two new classes to complement the schema.org ontology - the first one of them being **a new sub-class of CreativeWork: PerformanceWork**.

### Rationale

There is currently no possibility to specifically describe Performance Works as such. Simply describing them as schema:CreativeWork may lead to confusion as the current ontology tends to overlook or ignore the existence of Performance Works. Furthermore, the description of Performance Works requires a particular set of properties characteristic of performing arts productions.

### Definition of PerformanceWork

The new class schema:PerformanceWork is defined as a subclass of schema:CreativeWork and is used to refer to any element (or combination thereof) of the WEMI stack of a Performance Work (in analogy to frbr:Work, frbr:Expression, frbr:Manifestation, frbr:Item).

The semantic scope of schema:PerformanceWork is specified to englobe all the branches of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports.

The textbox below contains the proposed definition and usage note of schema:PerformanceWork.

```
Thing > CreativeWork > PerformanceWork

Work of the performing arts, consisting of live performances in front of an audience. 

Note: To be used in combination with PerformingArtsEvent to describe productions / shows of the performing arts
(music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports (e.g. choreographed 
forms of martial arts, figure skating, competitive ballroom dancing).
```

### Additional Properties of PerformanceWork

As a subclass of schema:CreativeWork, schema:PerformanceWork inherits the properties of [schema:CreativeWork](https://schema.org/CreativeWork). For the class PerformanceWork, the following additional properties are proposed:

- **author** (see: [https://schema.org/author](https://schema.org/author))
- **composer** (see: [https://schema.org/composer](https://schema.org/composer))
- **musicBy** (see: [https://schema.org/musicBy](https://schema.org/musicBy))
- **choreographer** - new property, defined as **"The person or organization who created a choreography, or who is the choreographer of a work performed at some event."**

### Further Information

See also the related [proposal for the creation of a new sub-class of Event: PerformingArtsEvent](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4468).

The rationale and conceptual underpinning for the proposal of the two new classes have been described in more detail in the following document: [Modeling Performing Arts Events (Version 1.0)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HWEnT5_nAkAE_h8rOE7mug2F3vyuK6qi/). If you would like to comment directly on that document, please do so in the related [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WwPr0Olw1XU9nZ1kqsiNQDA4Ds4atYakE5I_bMcV-a0/).

issues.title: Proposal (Performing Arts 2) - New sub-class of  Event: PerformingArtsEvent
issues.author: beatestermann
issues.body:
In their assessment of the schema.org ontology, the [Canadian Association for the Performing Arts (CAPACOA)](https://capacoa.ca/en/) and [its partners](https://linkeddigitalfuture.ca/community/) have encountered a lack of expressiveness of schema.org when it comes to describing **performing arts events (live events)** and related entities. We therefore propose the definition of two new classes to complement the schema.org ontology - the second one of them being **a new sub-class of Event: PerformingArtsEvent**.

### Rationale

There is currently no possibility to describe live performance events of the performing arts in general. The existing approach of defining specific event types only partly lends itself to the description of such events: Whereas schema:TheatreEvent (“Theatre performance.”) might be used for this purpose, schema:MusicEvent (“Music event.”) is not limited to live music events, and schema:DanceEvent (“A social dance.”) does not include dance performances at all. Furthermore, there would be a variety of mixed types that combine several of these main genres, such as opera or ballet, leaving it unclear whether each of them should get their own type in schema.org or whether a complex combinatory of specific event types should be used instead.

### Definition of PerformingArtsEvent

The new class schema:PerformingArtsEvent is **defined as an equivalent of the class [LRMoo-F31 Performance](https://ontome.net/class/1288/namespace/218)**, which comprises activities where an instance of schema:CreativeWork is presented or communicated directly or indirectly to an audience, in the form of a theatrical play, a musical work or a choreographic work.

It is defined as a sub-class of schema:Event, which is described as: “An event happening at a certain time and location, such as a concert, lecture, or festival. Ticketing information may be added via the schema:offers property. Repeated events may be structured as separate Event objects.”

The semantic scope of schema:PerformingArtsEvent is specified to englobe all the branches of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), including performance art and performative sports. 

It is implied that events of the type schema:PerformingArtsEvent involve a live audience. Thus, recording events or rehearsals may be described using this class if they occur in front of an audience. In all other cases, its use is discouraged. For reasons of conciseness, this is not explicitly stated in the proposed definition and usage note. 

The textbox below contains the proposed definition and usage note of schema:PerformingArtsEvent.

```
Thing > Event > PerformingArtsEvent

Live performance event of the performing arts (music, theatre, dance, acrobatics, spoken word), 
including performance art and performative sports (e.g. choreographed forms of martial arts, figure skating, 
competitive ballroom dancing). 

Note: Use additionalType to differentiate between productions / shows (PerformanceWork, EventSeries), 
tours (EventSeries), and individual performances.
```
### Additional Properties of PerformingArtsEvent

As a subclass of schema:Event, schema:PerformingArtsEvent inherits the properties of [schema:Event](https://schema.org/Event). At the time of writing, no additional properties have been suggested for the newly proposed class schema:PerformingArtsEvent.

### Further Information

See also the related [proposal for the creation of a new sub-class of CreativeWork: PerformanceWork](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4467).

The rationale and conceptual underpinning for the proposal of the two new classes have been described in more detail in the following document: [Modeling Performing Arts Events (Version 1.0)](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1HWEnT5_nAkAE_h8rOE7mug2F3vyuK6qi/). If you would like to comment directly on that document, please do so in the related [Google Doc](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1WwPr0Olw1XU9nZ1kqsiNQDA4Ds4atYakE5I_bMcV-a0/).

issues.title: Proposal to add a new OnlineMarketplace type as subtype of OnlineStore
issues.author: alex-jansen
issues.body:
**Context** - This is a proposal from Google based on our experience consuming Schema.org markup and working with similar data from online merchants. If it were accepted, it would make it easier for us and others to understand online marketplaces.

**Proposal** - An online marketplace is a collection of online stores, which are independent 3rd party sellers offering their products on the marketplace. The marketplace itself can also have its own online inventory, which it is selling alongside the inventory of the 3rd party sellers. [Schema.org](http://schema.org/) currently only models individual online sellers (through the [OnlineStore](https://schema.org/OnlineStore) type), but not online marketplaces. We therefore propose to add a new type *OnlineMarketplace* (as subtype of [OnlineStore](https://schema.org/OnlineStore)), with a new property *hasStore* (and inverse property *isStoreOn*)

issues.title: Add accessibilityException property to describe undue/disproportionate burden in accessibility metadata
issues.author: monikagithub
issues.body:
I propose a new property accessibilityException (or alternatively accessibilityLimitationReason) for use on CreativeWork and related types. This property would describe reasons why accessibility features could not be provided, such as undue burden, disproportionate burden, or technical infeasibility.

While the accessibilitySummary property allows for a general text summary, it is not semantically explicit, and not machine-readable for regulatory or audit purposes.

ONIX Code 196 already has properties to add this kind of metadata.

For Journal Articles to comply with ADA Title II legislation, we are using schema.org accessibility metadata properties and it would be really helpful to have this property.

Kind Regards

issues.title: Proposal: New property for JobPosting to indicate the expected end of employment
issues.author: Emosewaj
issues.body:
It is currently possible to use the [`jobStartDate`](https://schema.org/jobStartDate) property to indicate a "date on which a successful applicant for this job would be expected to start work". However, there is currently no such property to indicate the expected end of that employment.

Some job offers may be seasonal work and employment duration will be limited to a certain time period, or up to a certain date.

The property [`validThrough`](https://schema.org/validThrough) is not appropriate for this use case, as it appears to be intended to be used to indicate when the job *offer* itself expires.

My use case requires the proposed property to accept at least a date, in the same format that [`jobStartDate`](https://schema.org/jobStartDate) does ([`Date`](https://schema.org/Date) or [`Text`](https://schema.org/Text)). This date would indicate a clear date at which the working relationship is expected to end. A valid value would be expected to
1. be in the future and
2. greater than [`jobStartDate`](https://schema.org/jobStartDate), if set.

Additionally and optionally, I believe the following two types of values may be useful in some cases:
- A duration, e.g "3 months", or "2 years", or some other way of denoting a relative time span. This may be useful if there is no specific start date, but [`jobImmediateStart`](https://schema.org/jobImmediateStart) is set to `true`
- A non-specific point in time, e.g. "November 2025", "Summer 2026", to indicate a more flexible end of the working relationship

Thanks for the consideration.

issues.author: rvguha

Hello folks,

 After a period of relative hiatus, we are working on restarting  updates to http://schema.org/.

 As a first step, we are moving from hosting the Schema.org website as an application on AppEngine to a set of github pages. The goal is both to simplify the maintanence of the website and to make it easy for others to create extensions in a fashion where we can easily link to approved extensions.

 Before we switch over, it would make sense for us, as a community to take a close look at what the new site will look like and iron out the bugs. The site is available at https://schemaorg.github.io/gh_pages/. 

As a next step, it will also be made available at https://staging-github.schema.org/, sometime later this week.


Please give us your feedback.

thanks,

Guha, on behalf of the Schema.org team

issues.title: companyRegistration - description doesn't match schema definition
issues.author: bquinn
issues.body:
The description for https://schema.org/companyRegistration says "The official registration number of a business including the organization that issued it such as Company House or Chamber of Commerce."

But the range (values allowed) must be of type https://schema.org/Certification - which is far more than just a number.

There don't seem to be any examples of the use of companyRegistration but I guess the following should be valid:

According to the schema, it seems that this is how a Certification object should look:

```
    "companyRegistration": {
        "@type": "Certification",
        "certificationIdentification": "65786496",
        "issuedBy": {
            "@type": "Organization",
            "name": "State of Delaware"
        },
        "certificationStatus": "CertificationActive"
    },
```

But the description implies that we could simply say

`"companyRegistration": "65786496"
`
which would be invalid.

So a fix would be to either change the description to be "official registration information..." or to allow a text string as the value.
