issues.title: Proposal: Replace rating scale properties (bestRating / worstRating)
issues.author: jornmineur
issues.body:
**Problem**
The property names `bestRating` and `worstRating` are semantically misleading: they suggest the highest and lowest values observed in a set of ratings, rather than the bounds of the rating scale.

The confusion invites markup errors in structured data (for example, worstRating: 3 and bestRating: 4 when the scale is actually 1–5). While the [documentation](https://schema.org/Rating) explains the intended use, property names should ideally be self-explanatory and not require corrective clarification.

**Suggested alternative properties**
	•	`ratingScaleMin` (Number or Text):
The lower bound of the rating scale (for example, 1 when using a 1–5 star scale).
	•	`ratingScaleMax` (Number or Text):
The upper bound of the rating scale (for example, 5 when using a 1–5 star scale).

**Migration / implementation path**
To preserve backward compatibility:
	•	Introduce `ratingScaleMin` and `ratingScaleMax` as new properties.
	•	Mark `worstRating` and `bestRating` as `supersededBy` these new properties.
	•	Continue supporting both in consumers.
	•	When both are present, consumers should prefer the new properties.
	•	Update the [Rating](https://schema.org/Rating) documentation to recommend the new properties and include migration examples.

Individual terms from schema.org vocabulary are documented on html pages and offered for developers in ttl format (and other formats).
But it happens that the content of html page do not match exaclty the content of ttl.
The problem arises with properties that are "superseded". It can be spotted in the case of Course class.

The following properties are declared in ttl (with domainIncludes pointing at Course) but have no separate sections in html:
awards

The following properties are declared in ttl (without domainIncludes pointing at Course) and have no separate sections in html:

language
interactionCount
free
carrier
datasetTimeInterval

We can assume, that "superseded" properties are not documented in html by intension and the trace od changes is kept in ttl.
But what about misses in domainIncludes?
Should both representations match to each other?

issues.title: Proposal: previousStartDate rangeIncludes DateTime
issues.author: dpb587
issues.body:
Hello, I propose adding [DateTime](https://schema.org/DateTime) as an expected data type of [previousStartDate](https://schema.org/previousStartDate). Currently it expects a [Date](https://schema.org/Date).

In name and description, it seems like it should support the same values as [startDate](https://schema.org/startDate) (which expects both Date and DateTime).

> ... This property contains the previously scheduled start date. For rescheduled events, the startDate property should be used for the newly scheduled start date. ...

The addition of DateTime would help it match apparent usage, too.

* Only a couple examples include this property ([eg-0172](https://schema.org/Event#eg-0172), [eg-0202](https://schema.org/MusicEvent#eg-0202)), but they both use a DateTime value.
* Externally, Google's [Event Structured Data docs](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/event#previous-start-date) describe it as a DateTime.

It looks like [Release v3.1](https://schema.org/docs/releases.html#v3.1) (2016) added DateTime to startDate, but previousStartDate was unchanged.

issues.title: Proposal: Add `shippingMethod` to `OfferShippingDetails`
issues.author: cobaco1963
issues.body:
**Proposal: Add `shippingMethod` to `OfferShippingDetails`**

Currently, Schema.org allows us to define shipping destinations, origins, and settings via `OfferShippingDetails`, but there is no standardized way to specify the delivery method (e.g., Carrier, ParcelService, InStorePickup).

Although `DeliveryMethod` is defined as a type, it cannot be used within `OfferShippingDetails`, and attempting to include `"shippingMethod": "https://schema.org/DeliveryMethod/Carrier"` results in validation errors.

This limitation makes it difficult to express how a product is shipped, especially when the delivery method is an important part of the offer (e.g., courier vs. postal service).

**Suggested improvement:**
Introduce a new property `shippingMethod` (expected type: `DeliveryMethod`) within `OfferShippingDetails`, similar to how `returnMethod` is used in `MerchantReturnPolicy`.

**Use case:**
```json
"shippingDetails": {
  "@type": "OfferShippingDetails",
  "shippingMethod": "https://schema.org/DeliveryMethod/Carrier",
  ...
}
***************

This would allow publishers to clearly indicate the delivery method used for shipping products, improving semantic clarity and enabling richer search experiences.
Thank you for considering this proposal.

issues.title: Representation of login/authentication type actions
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
We're considering adding some sort of schema to represent communicating some basic authentication concepts about login flows and 2-factor authentication, and resetting passwords.  This came up a bit back in issue #1149.

- Login - representing that a link is used for logging in to a service/platform
- Authenticate - either a) a link that is used to verify an authentication/login attempt or b) an OTP that can be used to verify an authentication/login attempt
- Reset Password - representing the action to reset your password on a platform

The current thought is to use new Action subtypes.  The proposal is to add LoginAction (which often includes authentication generally as a subaction), AuthenticateAction (which may or may not have to do with logging in), and ResetPasswordAction.  They would all be subtypes of ControlAction.

Obviously you could get much more explicit here with the OTP object or more subtype-specific properties.  I was trying to keep it lean for now and reuse instrument or target for the information on the types.

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file. For info on how to format all future additions to this file please reference Keep A Changelog.

Unreleased

SPEC Changes

  • Define rack.response_finished callback arguments more strictly. (#2365, @​skipkayhil)

Added

  • Add Rack::Files#assign_headers to allow overriding how the configured file headers are set. (#2377, @​codergeek121)
  • Add support for rack.response_finished to Rack::TempfileReaper. (#2363, @​skipkayhil)
  • Add support for streaming bodies when using Rack::Events. (#2375, @​unflxw)

Changed

  • Raise before exceeding a part limit, not after. (#2362, @​matthew-puku)
  • Rack::Deflater now uses a fixed GZip mtime value. (#2372, @​bensheldon)

Fixed

  • Fix an issue where a NoMethodError would be raised when using Rack::Events with streaming bodies. (#2375, @​unflxw)

[3.2.0] - 2025-07-31

This release continues Rack's evolution toward a cleaner, more efficient foundation while maintaining backward compatibility for most applications. The breaking changes primarily affect deprecated functionality, so most users should experience a smooth upgrade with improved performance and standards compliance.

SPEC Changes

  • Request environment keys must now be strings. (#2310, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Add nil as a valid return from a Response body.to_path (#2318, [@​MSP-Greg])
  • Rack::Lint#check_header_value is relaxed, only disallowing CR/LF/NUL characters. (#2354, [@​ioquatix])

Added

  • Introduce Rack::VERSION constant. (#2199, [@​ioquatix])
  • ISO-2022-JP encoded parts within MIME Multipart sections of an HTTP request body will now be converted to UTF-8. (#2245, @​nappa)
  • Add Rack::Request#query_parser= to allow setting the query parser to use. (#2349, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Add Rack::Request#form_pairs to access form data as raw key-value pairs, preserving duplicate keys. (#2351, [@​matthewd])

Changed

  • Invalid cookie keys will now raise an error. (#2193, [@​ioquatix])
  • Rack::MediaType#params now handles empty strings. (#2229, [@​jeremyevans])
  • Avoid unnecessary calls to the ip_filter lambda to evaluate Request#ip (#2287, [@​willbryant])
  • Only calculate Request#ip once per request (#2292, [@​willbryant])
  • Rack::Builder #use, #map, and #run methods now return nil. (#2355, [@​ioquatix])
  • Directly close the body in Rack::ConditionalGet when the response is 304 Not Modified. (#2353, [@​ioquatix])

issues.title: Proposal — New property `onDisplay`
issues.author: vascosommernunes
issues.body:
## Problem statement (user need)

**“Where can I try this now?”**  
This is the everyday question for people looking to experience products before they buy and also for visitors deciding what art to see in person. Today, Schema.org can tell us if a thing is purchasable in a store (InStoreOnly), but it cannot say whether the item is actually on view for the public — on a showroom floor or on a gallery wall — right now.

- `InStoreOnly` ≠ on display. It simply says you can buy it offline, but not whether you can view and experience it.  
- For consumers and visitors, this leaves the key question unanswered.  

We have tried to make use of schema with an association of 40 design furniture retailers. But found that the schema ontology, which has such a great trait of being able to being explicit, lacks this addition which we feel would be of benefit for many.

## Proposal

### New property: `onDisplay` (Boolean)

- **domainIncludes:** `Product`, `VisualArtwork`  
- **rangeIncludes:** `Boolean`  
- **Definition:** Indicates whether the item is currently **publicly viewable** (e.g., on a showroom floor or on a gallery wall).  
- **Usage note:**  
  - Use `onDisplay: true` when the public can physically see or try the item at a `Place`.  
  - This complements commerce signals; it does not replace them.  
  - To indicate the place, reuse existing properties (e.g. `location` on the item page, or `hasPart` on the place page).  

## Affected types

- `Thing > Product` → add `onDisplay`  
- `Thing > CreativeWork > VisualArtwork` → add `onDisplay`  

## Compatibility

- This is a **non-breaking extension**. Existing mark-up remains valid.  
- `onDisplay` is complementary: it provides an answer to a distinct, high-value user question while preserving established commerce semantics.  

## Value to society

A minimal addition, but a meaningful one:  
- **For consumers:** answers the practical question “Where can I try this now?” across places.  
- **For retailers and museums:** makes visibility of their on-floor or on-wall inventory indexable, discoverable, and AI-friendly.  
- **For the web ecosystem:** promotes structured answers to a question that otherwise requires scraping, guessing, or manual updates.  

## References

- Blog post:  
  [See it in person: Proposing onDisplay for schema.org](https://blog.showroom.fm/index.php/2025/09/26/113/)

- Namespace definition (draft):  
  [https://blog.showroom.fm/index.php/152-2/](https://blog.showroom.fm/index.php/152-2/)

- Museum precedent: Rijksmuseum legacy OAI-PMH documentation (deprecated, but shows “on display” flag):
[https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/docs/oai-pmh/legacy-oai-pmh/](https://data.rijksmuseum.nl/docs/oai-pmh/legacy-oai-pmh)
 
## Acknowledgements

This proposal aims to follow the spirit of how to work with schema proposals. We feel this serves a widely felt gap, responds with the smallest possible addition, and delivers value for users and implementers alike.  

Thank you for your consideration. We appreciate your feedback.

issues.title: Help with incompatibility between multiple types
issues.author: eliseduverdier
issues.body: Hi, We have a news website, in which all pages use the schema `News Article` schema. In addition, we have some pages which use live posting, so we added the `LiveBlogPosting` schema. The problem is that when testing the whole page on the schema.org validator, we only see the `NewsArticle` one. When we remove it, we see the `LiveBlogPosting`. So I thought there was a incompatibility between them, but I couldn't find docs anywhere about it. When I look at the inheritance between types, I see there do not inherit directly, which maybe is the reason ? Thanks for your help ! Don't hesitate if you need more details.

issues.title: Validator associates `typeof` with wrong node when used with `rel` and `resource`
issues.author: meiqinyan
issues.body:
Given the following markup:
```html
<body typeof="WebPage" vocab="http://schema.org/">
  <span rel="mentions" resource="urn:isbn:0-394-80497-X" typeof="Book">
    <meta property="name" content="Fantastic Mr Fox">
```
The validator incorrectly takes the `typeof="Book"` to be referring to the webpage, instead of the book. The correct validation is given if the `rel` attribute is replaced with `property`.

This bug similarly affects the `rev` attribute.

issues.title: Add a economic operator attribute to Product
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
The EU defines the notion of _economic operator_ which is the entity responsible for a product within a given market. 
This notion is different from the _manufacturer_ – although a manufacturer can the economic operator for a product.
This concept is more general than that of _importer_ which would be the end-buyer in case of drop shipping.
This attribute would work for the EU market, but also in India, which has similar requirements.

issues.title: Proposal: Schemas for Systems' States and Error Messages
issues.author: AdamSobieski
issues.body:
## Proposal Hello. I would like to propose creating schemas for [error reports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Exception_handling), [stack traces](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stack_trace), [call stacks](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_stack), [stack frames](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Call_stack#STACK-FRAME), and related concepts. A motivating use case is enabling and enhancing AI-related scenarios via JSON-LD representations of systems' [states](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/State_(computer_science)) and [contexts](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Context_(computing)). There are several other interesting uses to consider; some are indicated below. Firstly, there are Web scenarios to consider such as embedding JSON-LD representations of systems' states and error messages in `

Hello world!

``` Secondly, today, developers and end-users can share error-report data in Web-based discussion forums. This sharing often involves copying and pasting formatted text output by software systems for these systems' developers to make use of. What if software systems' states and error messages could be output into, processed into, and/or pasted into standard machine-readable formats or schema? Perhaps new software tools could, then, be created to enhance technical communication, enabling the indexing of, searching for, retrieval of, analysis of, and visualization of these data. Perhaps, resembling [Mermaid diagrams](https://docs.github.com/en/get-started/writing-on-github/working-with-advanced-formatting/creating-diagrams) on GitHub, developers and end-users could paste systems' states and error messages into [markdown code blocks](https://markdown.land/markdown-code-block) for convenient formatting and visualization features. ````markdown ```state { ... } ``` ```` ````markdown ```error { ... } ``` ```` Thirdly, having a standard means of representing systems' states and error messages would enhance a number of protocols, e.g., [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro), which include error-handling capabilities, enabling or enhancing the exchange of systems' states between AI agents and/or systems' other components. Fourthly, software system observability can be delivered by using telemetry solutions (e.g., [OpenTelemetry](https://opentelemetry.io/)). These solutions enable developers to mark, make, measure, and transmit [spans](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/trace/api/#span), [traces](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/otel/overview/#traces), [logs](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/logs/), and [metrics](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/concepts/signals/metrics/) to observers. Schemas for representing systems' states would enhance observability scenarios. Fifthly, having a standard means of representing systems' states and error messages would enhance software [development](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_development), [testing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Software_testing), and [debugging](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Debugging#Techniques) scenarios, e.g., remote debugging. Sixthly, many software systems overwise only capable of being viewed as "black boxes" could have their states snapshotted during execution, either manually or automatically. Software systems could be paused, have their states obtained, and then be resumed without there needing to have been an error. Seventhly, as software systems and their stateful subsystems can be distributed across multiple computers, new schemas for systems' states and error messages would simplify the exchange, gathering, and collation of these data for such distributed systems. This would be useful, in particular, for distributed systems comprised of software components or services from multiple vendors. ## See Also * https://www.w3.org/TR/trace-context-1/ – the W3C Trace Context Recommendation. * https://mcpcat.io/guides/error-handling-custom-mcp-servers/ – discusses error handling in MCP. * https://github.com/WICG/proposals/issues/188 – ideas for representing state and context in business processes and/or workflows.

issues.title: Proposal: Public Figure (Person - Address)
issues.author: WeaverStever
issues.body:
**Problem:**

Public Figures (government workers, law enforcement. entertainers) often need to obscure sensitive information from the internet. (home address / legacy phone numbers). Exposing this real world  data can expose them to threats, intimidation, stalking etc. 

AI and search engine snippets will often inadvertently expose sensitive information from public records (Home titles etc.).  Removing the information requires visiting the website exposing the data, finding an Opt-Out procedure link. Then, waiting for the data to be removed and then requesting the removal of the search snippet from the search result as a follow up. 

**Proposal:**

Create a type, perhaps in Person > homeLocation for a publicFigure.  In this case, the Public Figure could provide partial address (State, City, Zipcode) or a partial phone number (on official website) that should not be associated / solicited in search engine results. Search engines and AI can then voluntarily omit search results containing the contactPoints or Place(s) listed under publicFigure.

**Solution:**
This would solve a portion of the problem, search engines could obfuscate the search result snippet(s) that promote the pages that host the personal information.  I.e., by design, the search engine aggregates several matching home addresses on Page 1, basically confirming to the adversary that the home location is correct and up to date.

issues.title: New properties proposed for live event content
issues.author: gmackenz
issues.body:
The current schema.org vocabulary, while excellent for VOD content, has several gaps that prevent it from being a comprehensive standard for ingesting modern, OTT and broadcast schedules from major content providers.
The core problem we found is that live broadcasts involve multiple layers of timing (e.g., the broadcast window vs. the actual event), complex regional rights and embargoes, and a variety of audio tracks (e.g., home/away commentary) that the current schema does not adequately support.
This proposal introduces a set of new properties, primarily for the [BroadcastEvent](https://schema.org/BroadcastEvent) and [SportsEvent](https://schema.org/SportsEvent) types, to address these gaps.

New properties to add to schema.org:

- `eventSchedule` on type `BroadcastEvent`  Expected type is [Schedule](https://schema.org/Schedule)
Distinguishes the precise start and end of the core event (e.g., kick-off to final whistle) from the wider `startDate`/`endDate` of the broadcast window (which includes pre/post-show content).
- `programActuality` on type `BroadcastEvent` Expected type is either [Text](https://schema.org/Text) or [Enumeration](https://schema.org/Enumeration) (still under discussion)
A flag to indicate the airing status of the program. Values include `Live`, `Premiere`, `New`, `Repeat`, and `Delayed`.
- `broadcastImage` on type `BroadcastEvent`  Expected type is `ImageObject`
Provides a set of images specific to an individual broadcast, allowing for tune-in creative or overlays. This is distinct from the `image` property of the underlying program.
- `audioTrack` on type `BroadcastEvent`  Expected type is `AudioObject`
A structured object to provide detailed information about an available audio stream, including language, codec, a descriptive name (e.g., "Home Commentary"), and a stream PID.
- `regionalAudioPreferences` on type `BroadcastEvent`  Expected type is `AudioConfiguration`
Defines a different default audio track or an ordered list of fallback preferences for specific geographic regions.
- `gameId` on type `SportsEvent`  Expected type is `Text`
A league-specific, official identifier for a sports game (e.g., an NFL-provided Game ID).

issues.title: Define text subtypes for defined types of text
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
Currently the `Text` type is used wildly in schema.org for basically two different purposes: text that is understood by human beings and identifiers that have a textual form. This makes makes the documentation more complicated, as the type of many fields is not self explanatory, and also mashes together two types which are basically distinct (see https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4545) 

I would suggest we add sub-types for the following _text_ types:

* Country codes used in [returnPolicyCountry](https://schema.org/returnPolicyCountry), [addressCountry](https://schema.org/addressCountry) , [applicableCountry](https://schema.org/applicableCountry), [countriesNotSupported](https://schema.org/countriesNotSupported), [countriesSupported](https://schema.org/countriesSupported), [countryOfAssembly](https://schema.org/countryOfAssembly), [countryOfLastProcessing](https://schema.org/countryOfLastProcessing)

* Language codes, used [inLanguage](https://schema.org/inLanguage), [knowsLanguage](https://schema.org/knowsLanguage), [subtitleLanguage](https://schema.org/subtitleLanguage), [availableLanguage](https://schema.org/availableLanguage)

As these types would inherit from Text, this would mean no functional change, just more clarity in the documentation.

issues.title: New meta property schemaAuthor to credit JSON-LD creators
issues.author: SEOLadyUK-Ltd
issues.body:
### Proposal: Add `schemaAuthor` property to the Schema.org vocabulary

#### Summary
This proposal introduces a new meta property, **`schemaAuthor`**, to acknowledge the creator of a custom JSON-LD implementation or schema framework.  
Its purpose is to provide transparent attribution and provenance for structured data created by developers, SEOs, or agencies — especially in cases where their contribution is not reflected in on-page authorship or published content.

---

#### Context and Use Case
As a **freelance SEO and structured data consultant**, I frequently design and deploy **custom JSON-LD frameworks** for clients who commission technical implementation but are not the authors of the underlying schema logic.

A typical example is when building **video watch-page schema**:  
I implemented a **unique VideoObject framework** nested within an Article schema to improve entity understanding across multiple video hosting and search platforms.  
In this case, the creative and technical work was mine, yet the client — whose site hosted the data — was listed as the publisher.  

While this is standard in SEO projects, it raises an important question of **authorship and provenance** within the **Knowledge Graph**.  
The schema itself is a creative work, distinct from the web page it describes.

---

#### Rationale
Structured data is increasingly central to **GEO (Generative Experience Optimisation)** and **AEO (Answer Engine Optimisation)** — both of which rely on high-quality, well-attributed data to train search, CC bots, and AI agents.  

By introducing `schemaAuthor`, Schema.org can help standardise a way to record:
- Who engineered the schema logic  
- When it was deployed  
- What framework or creative rationale informed it  

This property would not influence SEO rankings directly. Instead, it supports **E-E-A-T principles** (Experience, Expertise, Authoritativeness, and Trustworthiness) by providing traceable authorship for structured data assets.  

It also aligns with the Knowledge Graph’s broader goal of **entity-level accountability**: making the web’s technical layer as transparent and attributable as its visible content.

---

#### Proposed Definition

schemaAuthor
	•	Expected type: Person or Organization
	•	Domain: CreativeWork, Dataset, SoftwareApplication, or any schema implementation
	•	Description: Identifies the individual or organisation responsible for creating or authoring the JSON-LD structured data logic or framework used on a webpage or dataset.

---

#### Benefits
- Establishes a clear line of **provenance** for technical schema design work  
- Enables AI systems and CC bots to recognise **trusted structured data creators**  
- Strengthens **Knowledge Graph authority** for verified experts in structured data  
- Encourages transparency between agencies, clients, and developers  

---

#### Status
Early concept — experimental and based on professional use cases from freelance schema consultants working across SEO and AI entity optimisation projects. 

#### Benefits
- Establishes a clear line of **provenance** for technical schema design work  
- Enables AI systems and CC bots to recognise **trusted structured data creators**  
- Strengthens **Knowledge Graph authority** for verified experts in structured data  
- Encourages transparency between agencies, clients, and developers  

---

#### Inspiration
Inspired by the meta property **`inverseOf`**, which I’ve implemented in the wild across two related domains using nested person schema   @fredlegaucher
That experiment showed how bi-directional schema relationships reinforce entity connection and recognition —  
and it sparked this idea for `schemaAuthor` as a formal way to capture authorship and provenance within structured data.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/fd275245-1930-41f1-8e1a-1f2ba5590fbc)

issues.title: Proposal: Schemas for Kinds of Reports
issues.author: AdamSobieski
issues.body:
## Introduction

In the Schema.org model, there exists [`NewsMediaOrganization`](https://schema.org/NewsMediaOrganization) and [`NewsArticle`](https://schema.org/NewsArticle) which has the subtypes of [`ReportageNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/ReportageNewsArticle), [`AnalysisNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/AnalysisNewsArticle), [`AskPublicNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/AskPublicNewsArticle), [`OpinionNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/OpinionNewsArticle), [`ReviewNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/ReviewNewsArticle), and [`BackgroundNewsArticle`](https://schema.org/BackgroundNewsArticle).

Analogously, there exists [`GovernmentOrganization`](https://schema.org/GovernmentOrganization) and [`Report`](https://schema.org/Report) for reports generated by governmental or non-governmental organizations.

Proposed, here, is that [`Report`](https://schema.org/Report) should have subtypes. There exist a variety of kinds of governmental and government-funded reports including, but not limited to: financial, economic, annual, sustainability, sales and marketing, industry, project, research, risk-assessment, investor, audit, progress, performance, technical, and environmental reports [1].

## Discussion

### Government-funded Reports

In addition to governmental reports, there are government-funded reports. With respect to reports which were funded in part or entirely by a public-sector organization, one can utilize services such as [USASpending.gov](https://www.usaspending.gov/) to search for awards which did result in or are expected to result in reports.

### Policy-related Reports

Perhaps a subtype of `Report` could be `PolicyReport` which would be for reports pertaining to a stage of a [policy cycle](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Policy#Cycle) for a considered or realized policy item. A policy-related report could, for example, be proposing, developing, implementing, maintaining, analyzing, or evaluating a policy item. `PolicyReport` could have its own subtypes for kinds of reports produced with respect to each stage of the policy cycle.

### Political Science and Policy Studies

[Policy studies](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Policy_studies) is a subdiscipline of political science that includes the analysis of the process of policymaking and the contents of policy.

Politcal science, in particular its subdiscipline of policy studies, would be advanced as a result of: collating vast collections of policy-related reports, artificial intelligence technologies, and new search engines.

### New Search Engines

By enhancing the Schema.org model, as proposed, governments' and public-sector organizations' [content-management systems](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_management_system) could ping such search engines as governmental and government-funded reports were published or revised. These search engines could then spider those resources referenced in the pings and utilize resultant resource metadata to index the resources and provide more advanced features for end-users.

End-users could make use of new specialized AI-enhanced search engines to search, explore, and ask natural-language questions about vast collections of governmental and government-funded reports (see also: [2]).

## Conclusion

Thank you for any feedback or comments with which to improve upon this proposal.

## Bibliography

[1] https://msnbis.com/2025/02/01/understanding-government-reports-key-types-importance-and-their-role-in-informed-decision-making/
[2] https://ntrl.ntis.gov/NTRL/

issues.title: Add HearingAidStore as a subset of MedicalBusiness and LocalBusiness
issues.author: leonardmajere-stack
issues.body:
Overview

This proposal requests the addition of a new Schema.org subtype called HearingAidStore, representing businesses that sell, fit, and service hearing aids and related accessories.
Currently, there is no dedicated type for hearing aid retailers under MedicalBusiness, despite similar categories such as Optician, Pharmacy, and Dentist.

Rationale

Hearing aid centers occupy a unique space between retail and healthcare.

They:

Provide medical device fittings and aftercare under professional supervision (licensed hearing instrument specialists, audiologists).

Operate as local businesses with physical storefronts.

Offer medical-grade diagnostic and rehabilitative services related to hearing loss.


The absence of a HearingAidStore type limits structured data precision for:

Search engines and assistive AI interpreting medical services.

Accessibility and healthcare directories.

Knowledge graph differentiation between general retail (e.g., “ElectronicsStore”) and clinical device providers.


Proposed Definition

HearingAidStore
A business that sells, fits, and maintains hearing aids, hearing protection, and assistive listening devices. Staffed by licensed hearing care professionals or audiologists.

issues.title: Proposal: Schemas for Policy
issues.author: AdamSobieski
issues.body:
## Introduction

This issue proposes a new schema type, `Policy`, for policies.

## Discussion

In #4560, @MatthiasWiesmann indicated that a `Policy` type should inherit from [`CreativeWork`](https://schema.org/CreativeWork).

For discussion, some of the notable inherited properties that a `Policy` type would have are indicated below:

| Property | Type | Inherited From |
|----------|------|----------------|
| [`abstract`](https://schema.org/abstract) | `Text` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`additionalType`](https://schema.org/additionalType) | `Text` or `URL` | `Thing` |
| [`author`](https://schema.org/author) | `Organization` or `Person` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`citation`](https://schema.org/citation) | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`comment`](https://schema.org/comment) | `Comment` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`contributor`](https://schema.org/contributor) | `Organization` or `Person` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`creativeWorkStatus`](https://schema.org/creativeWorkStatus) | `DefinedTerm` or `Text` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`dateCreated`](https://schema.org/dateCreated) | `Date` or `DateTime` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`dateModified`](https://schema.org/dateModified) | `Date` or `DateTime` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`datePublished`](https://schema.org/datePublished) | `Date` or `DateTime` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`description`](https://schema.org/description) | `Text` or `TextObject` | `Thing` |
| [`discussionUrl`](https://schema.org/discussionUrl) | `URL` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`hasPart`](https://schema.org/hasPart) | `CreativeWork` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`identifier`](https://schema.org/identifier) | `PropertyValue` or `Text` or `URL` | `Thing` |
| [`isPartOf`](https://schema.org/isPartOf) | `CreativeWork` or `URL` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`locationCreated`](https://schema.org/locationCreated) | `Place` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`mentions`](https://schema.org/mentions) | `Thing` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`name`](https://schema.org/name) | `Text` | `Thing` |
| [`potentialAction`](https://schema.org/potentialAction) | `Action` | `Thing` |
| [`sameAs`](https://schema.org/sameAs) | `URL` | `Thing` |
| [`sourceOrganization`](https://schema.org/sourceOrganization) | `Organization` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`sponsor`](https://schema.org/sponsor) | `Organization` or `Person` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`subjectOf`](https://schema.org/subjectOf) | `CreativeWork` or `Event` | `Thing` |
| [`text`](https://schema.org/text) | `Text` | `CreativeWork` |
| [`url`](https://schema.org/url) | `URL` | `Thing` |
| [`version`](https://schema.org/version) | `Number` or `Text` | `CreativeWork` |

For discussion, according to: [Policy § Content](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Policy#Content), policy documents tend to share components. These are sketched below:

| Property | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| `purpose` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | Outlining why the organization (i.e., the [`sourceOrganization`](https://schema.org/sourceOrganization)) is issuing the policy, and what the desired effect or outcome of the policy should be. |
| `applicabilityAndScope` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | Whom the policy affects. The applicability and scope may also expressly exclude certain people, organizations, or actions from the policy requirements. Applicability and scope are used to focus the policy on only the desired targets, and avoid unintended consequences where possible. |
| [`validFrom`](https://schema.org/validFrom) | `Date` or `DateTime` | When the policy comes into force. |
| [`expires`](https://schema.org/expires) | `Date` or `DateTime` | When the policy concludes. |
| `responsibilities` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | Which parties and organizations are responsible for carrying out individual policy statements. Many policies may require the establishment of some ongoing function or action. |
| [`text`](https://schema.org/text) | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | A statement indicating the specific regulations, requirements, or modifications to organizational behavior that the policy is creating. Policy statements are extremely diverse depending on the organization and intent and may take almost any form. |
| `background` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | Some policies may include background indicating any reasons, history, ethical background statements, and/or intent that led to the creation of the policy, which may be listed as motivating factors. See also: [`backstory`](https://schema.org/backstory). |
| `definitions` | `CreativeWork` or `DefinedTermSet` or `Text` | Provides clear and unambiguous definitions for terms and concepts found in the policy document. |

For discussion, some other components which tend to be shared across policy documents are sketched below:

| Property | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| `procedures` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` or `HowTo` | Detailed procedures for how the policy will be implemented and monitored should be included. This section outlines the steps that need to be taken to ensure compliance with the policy. |
| `exceptions` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | Circumstances under which the policy may not apply should be specified. This section outlines any exceptions or special circumstances that may be relevant. |
| `review` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` | This section describes the frequency and process for reviewing and updating the policy. Regular reviews ensure that the policy remains relevant and effective over time. |

For discussion, to reduce ambiguity, more structure could be distilled or extracted from these policy-document components, as sketched below:

| Property | Type | Policy Document Component | Notes |
|----------|------|---------------------------|-------|
| `setsGoal` or `setsObjective` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` or `Goal` or `Objective` | `purpose` | The goals or objectives of a `Policy` could be referenced by (justificatory) properties of a pertinent `Program` |
| `setsNonGoal` or `setsNonObjective` | `CreativeWork` or `Text` or `Goal` or `Objective` | `purpose` | The non-goals or non-objectives of a `Policy` |
| `includedParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `applicabilityAndScope` | |
| `excludedParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `applicabilityAndScope` | |
| `responsibleParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `responsibilities` | Could have subproperties? |
| `implementingParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `procedures` | |
| `monitoringParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `procedures` | |
| `reviewingParty` | `Person` or `Organization` or `Text` | `review` | |
| `reviewPeriod` | `Duration` | `review` | How often to review? |
| `reviewDate` | `Date` | `review` | When is the next review? |

For discussion, some other properties that a `Policy` type could have are sketched below:

| Property | Type | Notes |
|----------|------|-------|
| [`category`](https://schema.org/category) | `CategoryCode` or `PhysicalActivityCategory` or `Text` or `Thing` or `URL` | A folksonomic category of the policy, e.g., economics, education, environment, healthcare, science, or transportation |
| [`validIn`](https://schema.org/validIn) | `AdministrativeArea` or `Text` | Indicates a legal jurisdiction, e.g. of some legislation, policy, or where some government service is based. |
| `policyStatus` | `DefinedTerm` or `Text` | The status of a policy in terms of its stage in a lifecycle. |
| `precedes` | `Policy` | |
| `supercedes` | `Policy` | |

## Questions

* Which properties should a `Policy` type have?

  * Its structure and properties can enable useful new features, e.g., for search engines.

* As discussed in [#4560](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4560), a policy article or report would be an `Article` that was `about` a `Policy`. How might a policy article or report express which stage of a policy cycle or process that it was a part of – whether it was proposing, discussing, developing, implementing, maintaining, reviewing, analyzing, or evaluating a policy?

  * Could such an `Article` use the `additionalType` property to indicate which variety of a policy report that it was?

  * Perhaps the `creativeWorkStatus` and/or the `policyStatus` of a `Policy` could be clues as to the nature of an `Article` `about` that `Policy` – the stage of a `Policy` in a lifecycle at the time of a `datePublished` of an `Article` `about` it.

* In addition to `Policy`, should there be new schema types for `Program` and `Project` [1]?

  * With these, a program evaluation report could be an `Article` `about` a `Program` `implementing` a `Policy`.

## Related Schemas

* [`Certification`](https://schema.org/Certification)
* [`Legislation`](https://schema.org/Legislation)
* [`Permit`](https://schema.org/Permit)
* [`SpecialAnnouncement`](https://schema.org/SpecialAnnouncement)

## Conclusion

Thank you for any comments or feedback including about those questions, above, or with which to improve upon this proposal.

## Bibliography

[1] https://govfacts.org/explainer/how-government-actually-gets-things-done-policies-programs-and-projects-explained/

issues.title: Proposal: Schemas for Programs and Projects
issues.author: AdamSobieski
issues.body:
## Introduction

This issue proposes a new schema type, `Program`, which would be interrelated to an existing one, [`Project`](https://schema.org/Project).

The existing schema type for [`Project`](https://schema.org/Project) inherits from [`Organization`](https://schema.org/Organization). `Program` could also inherit from [`Organization`](https://schema.org/Organization) and would then, similarly, be able to use the [`subOrganization`](https://schema.org/subOrganization) property to indicate both any subprograms and any projects, these projects capable of having subprojects.

This proposal originated as a result of discussions in issues #4560 and #4569.

## Programs and Projects

"A **program** is an organized, ongoing set of activities and resources managed by a government agency to achieve specific objectives stemming from established policy. Programs are the primary vehicles through which policies get translated into tangible services or outcomes. They represent the 'how' of government work." [1]

"A **project** is a temporary and specific endeavor undertaken to create a unique product, service, or result. Unlike ongoing programs, projects have defined beginnings and ends, specific scopes of work, set budgets, and allocated resources. Projects are the tangible, often time-bound actions that help achieve broader program objectives." [1]

## Program Characteristics

**Ongoing / Sustained**: Unlike projects, programs typically operate over extended periods, sometimes indefinitely, as long as the underlying policy remains in effect and funding is available [1].

**Organized Efforts**: Programs involve structured approaches with dedicated staff, specific budgets, and established operational procedures [1].

**Specific Objectives**: Programs aim to achieve measurable outcomes directly related to those goals outlined in the parent policy [1].

**Agency-managed**: Programs usually fall under specific government departments or agencies (USDA for SNAP, HHS for Medicare) [1].

## Considered Kinds

* Government Programs and Projects
* [Pilot](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pilot_experiment) Programs and Projects

## Key Properties

The following key properties have been, thus far, considered:

| Type | Property | Property Value Type |
|------|----------|------|
| `Program` | `implements` | `Policy` |
| `Program` | `achieves` | `Goal` or `Objective` |
| `Program` | [`subOrganization`](https://schema.org/subOrganization) | `Program` or `Project` |
| `Program` | [`parentOrganization`](https://schema.org/parentOrganization) | `Program` or `Organization` or `GovernmentOrganization` |

## Use Cases

### Enabling New Search Engines

With schemas under discussion (`Legislation`, `Policy`, `Program`, and `Project`) designed, adopted, and subsequently utilized, new search engines could be developed for the public, students, policy analysts, and policymakers to be able to search for and explore these kinds of interrelated resources as well as other resources, e.g., thinktank reports, [`about`](https://schema.org/about) them.

## Related Schemas

* [`GovernmentOrganization`](https://schema.org/GovernmentOrganization)
* [`GovernmentService`](https://schema.org/GovernmentService)
* [`Project`](https://schema.org/Project)

## Conclusion

Thank you for any comments or feedback including about those questions, above, or with which to improve upon this proposal.

## Bibliography

[1] https://govfacts.org/explainer/how-government-actually-gets-things-done-policies-programs-and-projects-explained/

issues.title: Add an entity to represent a PaymentProcessor
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
Typical website use one or more payment processor, this is a special kind of [PaymentService](https://schema.org/PaymentService) which has [acceptedPaymentMethod](https://schema.org/acceptedPaymentMethod) field on behalf of the merchant, as most of merchants do not process payments themselves. 

The distinction matters because the set of accepted payment methods is processor dependant, as well as processor dependant payment methods and features (say pay later). 

The actual structure would be the following:

```
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "OnlineStore",
  "name": "OrientExpress",
  "acceptedPaymentMethod": {
      "@type": "PaymentProcessor",
      "name": "PayFriend",
      "provider": {
          "@type": "Organization",
          "name": "PayFamily"
      }
      "acceptedPaymentMethod": []
  }
}
```

The requested features would be the following:
* New type PaymentProcessor, inherits from [PaymentService](https://schema.org/PaymentService)
* PaymentProcessor has the [acceptedPaymentMethod](https://schema.org/acceptedPaymentMethod) attribute.

issues.title: DefinedTerm should have the about property.
issues.author: MatthiasWiesmann
issues.body:
[DefinedTerm](https://schema.org/DefinedTerm) as well as [DefinedTermSet](https://schema.org/DefinedTermSet) should have the [about](https://schema.org/about) property. 

Currently, the about property is defined on the following objects:
* [Certification](https://schema.org/Certification)
* [CommunicateAction](https://schema.org/CommunicateAction)
* [CreativeWork](https://schema.org/CreativeWork)
* [Event](https://schema.org/Event)

The definition of `DefinedTerm` is the following:

> A word, name, acronym, phrase, etc. with a formal definition. Often used in the context of category or subject classification, glossaries or dictionaries, product or creative work types, etc

In many cases, the defined term is about _something_. For instance the [Bach-Werke-Verzeichnis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bach-Werke-Verzeichnis) codes are used to represent music pieces by [Johann Sebastian Bach](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Johann_Sebastian_Bach). And would be defined in the following way:

```
 {
    "@context": "https://schema.org/",
    "@type": "DefinedTermSet",
    "name": "Bach-Werke-Verzeichnis",
    "about": {
        "@type": "Thing",
        "@id": "https://schema.org/MusicComposition"
     }
    "hasDefinedTerm": {
        "@type": "DefinedTerm", 
        "termCode": "BWV 565",
        "about": {
            "@type": "MusicComposition",
            "name": "Toccata and Fugue in D minor",
            "genre": "Organ Work"
        }
    }
}
```

issues.title: Outdated Style Guide - Naming Conventions
issues.author: dpb587
issues.body:
Hello - some of the terms recently introduced to schema.org do not seem to follow the Naming Conventions of the [Style Guide](https://schema.org/docs/styleguide.html). Assuming the recommendations have changed, can the guide be updated to reflect whatever the current policy has become?

I'm not familiar with past discussions on this topic, but the guide includes:

> Do not give the same name to a type and a property.
>
> * Note that schema.org has some legacy cases where this was done in the past. This practice should be avoided.
> * E.g. Avoid creating both ContactPoint and contactPoint.

I've seen the following come through in the past year. Before this, I think the last, new overlap came with `Downpayment` from v11.

* v28.0 - `PaymentMethodType`/`paymentMethodType`
* v29.0 - `IncentiveStatus`/`incentiveStatus`, `IncentiveType`/`incentiveType`, `PurchaseType`/`purchaseType`, `ShippingConditions`/`shippingConditions`
* main - `Error`, `OperatingSystem`, `RuntimePlatform`

From my perspective, I'm just looking to figure out what to expect going forward. Hopefully this issue isn't too pedantic. I have recommended the style guide in the past for making similar decisions on internal term names. Sometimes publishers seem confused on the difference or accidentally typo the case in their data; but, so far on the consumption side, terms can usually be corrected based on its position as a predicate, `@type` object, or a few hard-coded conventions.

Thanks for your time.

issues.title: Proposal: Extension for Digital Product Passport (DPP) & EU ESPR Compliance
issues.author: kevinbouti
issues.body:
### Problem Definition
The European **Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR)** will require digital product passports (DPP) for major product categories starting in 2027. This regulation mandates granular data on:
- Circularity (recyclability, spare parts availability)
- Carbon footprint (PCF)
- Repairability and durability
- Compliance documentation

Currently, `schema:Product` provides excellent baseline metadata, but lacks specific properties to fully describe a **Digital Product Passport** lifecycle (e.g., granular repair events, warranty scopes beyond duration, and specific circularity metrics).

### Proposal
I propose initiating a discussion on extending `schema:Product` or introducing a `DigitalProductPassport` type to support these upcoming regulatory requirements.

### Reference Implementation (VDOS)
To support this effort, we (Verisav) have released an open technical framework and vocabulary under CC-BY-4.0 that extends Schema.org concepts for DPP compliance.

**Resource:** Verisav DPP Open Standard (VDOS) v1.0
**DOI:** [10.5281/zenodo.18016854](https://zenodo.org/records/18016854)
**Namespace:** `https://ns.verisav.fr/dpp#`

### Proposed Mapping (Draft)
We suggest mapping the following concepts to Schema.org:

1. **Repairability:**
   - Extend `schema:Grant` or `schema:WarrantyPromise` to include `repairabilityIndex` (0-10 scale).
   - New property: `hasSparePart` linking to `schema:Product`.

2. **Lifecycle Events:**
   - New type: `ProductLifecycleEvent` (subclass of `schema:Event`).
   - Properties: `manufacturingDate`, `firstUsageDate`, `endOfLifeDate`.

3. **Traceability:**
   - Better support for Unique Identifiers (UID) beyond `gtin` (e.g., decentralized DIDs).

I have signed the Google CLA and am willing to contribute definitions or mappings based on our VDOS research to the core schema or a pending extension.

Looking forward to the community's feedback.

Best regards,
Kévin Boutillier
Founder, Verisav

issues.title: [DPP] Proposal: Align Product Parts & Consumables with UN/CEFACT Codes
issues.author: kevinbouti
issues.body:
> Follow-up to discussion in #4657 with @MatthiasWiesmann.

### Problem Definition
As discussed in #4657 with @MatthiasWiesmann, `schema:Product` currently lacks a standardized way to distinguish between different roles of a product component (e.g., Spare Part vs. Consumable vs. Raw Material).

For the Digital Product Passport (ESPR), alignment with industrial standards is critical for ERP/EDI interoperability.

### Proposal
We propose introducing support for **UN/CEFACT UNCL 1001** codes to classify product roles.

**Proposed Property:** `hasProductRole` (or `unCeFactCode`)
**Expected Values:**
- `233` (Spare part order)
- `711` (Supply item / Consumable)
- `380` (Commercial Item / Main Product)
- `220` (Component)

### Example Usage
{
"@context": "https://schema.org/",
"@type": "Product",
"name": "Laptop Battery Replacement",
"hasProductRole": {
"@type": "PropertyValue",
"propertyID": "UNCL1001",
"value": "711",
"name": "Consumable"
}
}

text

This ensures we don't reinvent the wheel and stay compatible with global supply chain standards.

issues.title: [DPP] Proposal: New Type "ProductLifecycleEvent" for Traceability
issues.author: kevinbouti
issues.body:
> Follow-up to discussion in #4657 with @MatthiasWiesmann.

### Problem Definition
Current Schema.org properties (`productionDate`, `purchaseDate`) capture static timestamps but fail to describe the full lifecycle mandated by ESPR (manufacturing, repair, refurbishment, recycling).

We need a way to model **discrete events** in a product's life, each with its own location, performer, and certification data.

### Proposal
Introduce a new type: `ProductLifecycleEvent` (subclass of `schema:Event`).

Key Properties:
- `eventType`: (Enum/String) "Manufacturing", "FirstPutOnMarket", "Repair", "Refurbishment", "Recycling"
- `relatedProduct`: Link to the specific `IndividualProduct`.
- `actor`: Who performed the event (Organization/Person).
- `location`: Where it happened.
- `result`: Outcome (e.g., "Repaired", "Scrapped").

### Example Usage
{
"@type": "ProductLifecycleEvent",
"eventType": "Repair",
"startDate": "2026-05-12",
"actor": {
"@type": "Organization",
"name": "Authorized Repair Center Paris"
},
"location": {
"@type": "Place",
"address": "Paris, France"
},
"description": "Screen replacement with generic spare part."
}

text
undefined

issues.title: [DPP] Proposal: Structured Identifiers for DIDs & Resolvable Links
issues.author: kevinbouti
issues.body:
> Follow-up to discussion in #4657 with @MatthiasWiesmann.

### Problem Definition
While `schema:serialNumber` exists for string-based IDs, the Digital Product Passport (DPP) requires more complex identification mechanisms, specifically:
1. **Decentralized Identifiers (DIDs):** For verifiable credentials.
2. **Resolvable Links:** QR codes/NFC tags that point to a dynamic DPP endpoint.

A simple string is insufficient to capture the *type* and *resolution method* of these modern identifiers.

### Proposal
Extend `identifier` to explicitly support complex `PropertyValue` objects for Web3/DPP contexts.

### Example Usage
"identifier": [
{
"@type": "PropertyValue",
"propertyID": "did",
"value": "did:web:verisav.fr:product:12345",
"description": "Decentralized Identifier for Verifiable Credentials"
},
{
"@type": "PropertyValue",
"propertyID": "dppLink",
"value": "https://id.verisav.fr/12345",
"description": "Resolvable GS1 Digital Link"
}
]

text

This aligns with W3C DID specifications and GS1 Digital Link standards.

issues.title: Allow recipeIngredient to be another recipe or a reference to one
issues.author: YaaL
issues.body:
The schema of a recipe does not support grouping ingredients/steps for components or creating complex recipes that combine two or more basic recipes into a single one.
Generic example 1: a cake that consists of three basic components:
1. Cake
2. Cream filling
3. Icing/frosting

Generic example 2: pierogi
1. Dough
2. Filling

Each of these components is a complete recipe using separate list of ingredients, steps, can be prepared independently and used in other recipes. The final recipe combines those components, potentially adding other ingredients and steps.

Without grouping ingredients/steps or linking recipes the current result is an unhelpful long list of ingredients that will be used several times at different times. Allowing entering an URL, WebPage or Recipe for an ingredient would make it possible to build recipes from reusable blocks, avoiding repetition and making the instructions clearer and easier to follow.

issues.title: MediaObject cannot signal surrounding context preferences to third-parties
issues.author: jcayzac
issues.body:
There is currently no reliable way of annotating media objects with, for instance, which of a light or dark theme they have a better affinity with. The information could be used by applications, including but not limited to search engines, to select the best variant of an image to render for their users.

Some current properties _could_ be abused for the purpose. For instance, either `pattern` or `version` could be set to `dark` to signal the media object has a better affinity with a dark theme, but this use case is not the primary motivator for the existence of either properties and there is no clear criterium for choosing which to use for this.

Beyond the limited concept of a single light theme and a single dark theme, where luminance is the only dimension, there could also be situations where variants have a better affinity to certain chroma values.

A new property of MediaObject could support these use cases or point to another resource of a schema offering a generalization of what a "surrounding context" might mean, whether it relates to visual perception as above or to other kinds of contexts.

issues.title: Expansion of hasCredential to generic Credential
issues.author: rrlevering
issues.body:
Right now `hasCredential` property was written for educational credentials, which is why it has a very education typed `EducationalOccupationalCredential`.  I would like to expand this to represent weak identity credentials more generally.

In particular, Google would like to use this to let platforms provide structured metadata on whether accounts are "verified" by the platform.  Now "verified" is a very loose statement here and I don't want to invoke [verifiable credentials](https://www.w3.org/TR/vc-data-model-2.0/) schema per se.  In particular, I want the subject assertion to be loose (it could even potentially indicate the paid Twitter bit for instance which is technically more of a quality marker and not an identity one) and the credential to not necessarily be proveable in the VC sense.

This issue is full of past opinions.  For instance #3230 and especially the initial issue #2289.

I also considered `Certification` because it already has a more generic semantic but both in internal conversations about it being more focused on identity and thoughts that @philbarker brought up, I think the semantics of `Certification` are not what we're looking for.

So practically, the only request is to create a new supertype of EOC called Credential and move some of the more generic predicates to that level (leaving `educationLevel` on the EOC level).  That should be non-controversial enough that even if there is disagreement on our specific usage of it, the schema request itself shouldn't be problematic.

According to the currently published documentation example files require the related issue number inside the example file:

In the attempt to revive the webAPI PR a progressive number was present that did not align with the documentation which in fact was confirmed by @danbri being an alternative numbering scheme with progressive numbers citing that tagging examples with the progressive number could easily be done through a Python script.

Personally I would add one consideration: while git is an open standard, GitHub is not. issues.title: Proposal: properties for brand personality and intended use context
issues.author: SaschaDeforth
issues.body:
## Problem
Schema.org describes *what* entities are but lacks properties for two dimensions AI recommendation systems need: **intended use context** (for whom?) and **brand personality** (how does it feel?). Publishers work around this with `additionalProperty` / `PropertyValue`, but without standardization.
## Proposal
### `intendedUseContext`
- **Type:** `Text`
- **On:** `Organization`, `Brand`, `Product`, `Service`, `LocalBusiness`, `CreativeWork`
- **Definition:** Descriptive statement of the intended audience, use case, or situation for which this entity is most relevant.
Complements `audience` (which expects a structured `Audience` object) with a lightweight natural-language alternative — similar to how `speakable` complements `description`.
```json
{
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "Organic Pepper Mix",
  "intendedUseContext": "Intended for home cooks seeking premium organic spices for Mediterranean cooking. Best suited when ingredient quality matters more than price."
}
```
### `brandPersonality`
- **Type:** `Text` or `DefinedTerm`
- **On:** `Organization`, `Brand`, `Product`, `Service`, `LocalBusiness`
- **Definition:** Descriptors characterizing the emotional identity of a brand or product, as defined by the publisher.
Accepting `DefinedTerm` allows linking to Wikidata concepts for verifiability — mitigating the "meta-keywords" spam risk.
```json
{
  "@type": "Organization",
  "name": "Example Spice Company",
  "brandPersonality": [
    { "@type": "DefinedTerm", "name": "Family business", "sameAs": "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q955824" },
    { "@type": "DefinedTerm", "name": "Organic food", "sameAs": "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q191067" }
  ]
}
```
## Compatibility
Non-breaking extension. Both properties are optional.
## Reference
- Open-source spec + implementation: [vibetags/vibetags-spec](https://github.com/vibetags/vibetags-spec) (MIT)

issues.title: Enhancement/Evolution: Support for PaymentMethod collections/profiles via @id
issues.author: itsgroup-co-nz
issues.body:
# Proposal: Support for PaymentMethod collections/profiles via @id to reduce duplication and modernize E-commerce Schema

## Is your feature request related to a problem? Please describe.
Currently, specifying `acceptedPaymentMethod` for large e-commerce catalogs results in significant payload bloat and architectural "mess." Because `acceptedPaymentMethod` expects individual `PaymentMethod` entities (or a flat array thereof), developers cannot define a "Payment Profile" (a group of methods) once and reference it via a single `@id` across multiple `Offer` objects.

Furthermore, the existing infrastructure is a fragmented "Frankenstein" of:
1. **GoodRelations (GR):** Last updated circa 2011. Its own documentation site is so dated it attempts to pull defunct jQuery v1.12.4 libraries.
2. **UNECE PaymentMeans:** Has not seen a significant update since 2008 and often contradicts modern Schema/GR definitions.
3. **Redundancy:** In a catalog of 10,000 products, a developer must either repeat the full `PaymentMethod` objects or an array of 10+ `@id` pointers in every single `Offer`, leading to massive JSON-LD files.

## Describe the solution you'd like
1. **Introduce a Collection Type:** A dedicated type such as `PaymentMethodCollection`, or allowing `ItemList` / `DefinedTermSet` to be a valid `expected type` for the `acceptedPaymentMethod` property.
2. **Single @id Referencing:** Allow an `Offer` to point to a single `@id` representing a "Payment Profile." Consumers (Search Engines, LLMs, AI Agents) should be able to "unpack" this reference to identify the collective set of accepted payments for that offer.
3. **Native Modernization:** Move toward a native Schema.org enumeration for modern Fintech (Apple Pay, Google Pay, Klarna, Afterpay, Crypto) to eliminate reliance on stagnant, 15-year-old external ontologies.

## Describe alternatives you've considered
* **Organization-level definition:** Defining methods on the `Organization` and linking via `offeredBy` or `seller`. While semantically valid in a graph, many legacy parsers and Rich Result validators still require the property to exist directly on the `Offer` for eligibility.
* **JSON-LD @graph references:** Using a flat array of `@id` pointers (e.g., `#visa`, `#mastercard`) in every offer. While this prevents re-defining the object, it still requires repeating a large array of IDs for every product, which is not "DRY" (Don't Repeat Yourself) at the catalog level.

## Additional context
The e-commerce landscape has shifted from simple "Credit Card vs. Cash" to complex gateway stacks (Stripe, Adyen, etc.) that provide dozens of sub-methods. Forcing modern AI-driven commerce to rely on UNECE codes from 2008 and GoodRelations logic from 2011 is a technical bottleneck. A "Payment 2.0" cleanup that allows for reusable, named payment profiles is overdue.

issues.title: Suggestion: Specify (modified) RFC 9557 timestamps for the Time type
issues.author: ideal-railroad
issues.body:
The [Time](https://schema.org/Time) type currently defers to the [XML time type](https://www.w3.org/TR/xmlschema-2/#time), which specifies ISO 8601.

I live in the United States, though, and so I'm subject to the devilry that is Daylight Saving Time, so it becomes a hassle to specify opening hours for a business:

```javascript
{
  '@type': 'OpeningHoursSpecification',
  dayOfWeek: ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday'],
  opens: '07:00-05:00',   // Valid only half the year
  closes: '18:00-05:00',
},
```

I've recently been exposed to the beautiful new JavaScript [Temporal API](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Temporal) and its use of [RFC 9557](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc9557), which allows specifying an IANA time zone in its timestamps. So I imagine a world in which I can do this:

```javascript
{
  '@type': 'OpeningHoursSpecification',
  dayOfWeek: ['Monday', 'Tuesday', 'Wednesday', 'Thursday'],
  opens: '07:00[America/Chicago]',   // Valid all year!
  closes: '18:00[America/Chicago]',
},
```

Although, now that I get a closer look at RFC 9557, they don't have a production for times without dates. Still, this is useful enough that I want to float the idea.

issues.title: Proposal: Add support for more protocols on EntryPoint
issues.author: joelacummings
issues.body:
## Problem

Currently [EntryPoint](https://schema.org/EntryPoint) is defined as such: "An entry point, within some Web-based protocol." However there is no property to specify the protoctol i.e. https/http/wss/sse. It also defines a property https://schema.org/httpMethod that implies this is intended only for Http protocols which feels orthogonal to the definition. 

In our case we'd like to markup a NL Web WebSocket Url that we have on our Schema App website and inform users they can connect using either websockets or server sent events and also provide a link to the definition of these events which make a machine discoverable way of interacting with this.


## Proposal

To make this more generic perhaps we could introduce a `protocol` or `protocolSchema` property that allows for support for other protocols. 

Event driven protocols like websocks are often defined using the open source async api: https://github.com/asyncapi so it would useful to have a property can link to the definition of the api. 


`schema:protocolSchema` a URL value that links to an AsyncApi defintion (or something similar)

We could combine this with a `schema:protocol` property to also be clear it is a WSS/SSE/HTTP etc. The protocol schema could then provide the definition for a REST API or a SSE/WSS depending the type of definition file. I'm open to ideas on better modelling this to make it more generic. 


The other option could be using a sub-type of EntryPoint for Event Driven Entrypoints that would contain websockets and other event driven protocols and that would also provide some separation since the protocolSchema for event driven types could be inferred to be a AsyncApi definition instead of OpenAPI for example.

issues.title: Proposal: WebPageSemanticRepresentation type for AI agent consumption
issues.author: dbhurley
issues.body:
## Summary

As AI agents increasingly consume web content, there is a growing need for a standardized way to describe machine-readable semantic representations of web pages.

We propose a new Schema.org type, `WebPageSemanticRepresentation`, that allows websites to advertise the availability of semantic page representations optimized for AI consumption.

## Motivation

AI agents currently interact with web pages by fetching raw HTML and parsing the DOM (often via headless Chrome). This is expensive, slow, and wasteful - 90%+ of tokens sent to LLMs are presentational noise.

Several projects now produce structured semantic representations:
- [Plasmate SOM](https://plasmate.app) (Semantic Object Model)
- Jina Reader API
- Firecrawl
- Accessibility trees

A Schema.org type would let websites signal that a semantic representation is available, its format, and where to fetch it.

## Proposed Properties

| Property | Type | Description |
|----------|------|-------------|
| `representationFormat` | Text | Format (e.g., 'SOM/1.0', 'markdown') |
| `representationUrl` | URL | Where to fetch the representation |
| `sourceUrl` | URL | The original page URL |
| `tokenCount` | Integer | Approximate token count |
| `compressionRatio` | Number | HTML tokens / representation tokens |
| `generatedBy` | SoftwareApplication | Tool that generated it |
| `contentScope` | Text | What's included (full-page, main-content, etc.) |
| `lastCrawled` | DateTime | When the source was last fetched |

## Example

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "WebPageSemanticRepresentation",
  "sourceUrl": "https://example.com/article",
  "representationUrl": "https://cache.example.com/som?url=https://example.com/article",
  "representationFormat": "SOM/1.0",
  "tokenCount": 1200,
  "compressionRatio": 14.2
}
```

## Context

This proposal comes from the [W3C Web Content Browser for AI Agents Community Group](https://www.w3.org/community/web-content-browser-ai/), where we are incubating the Semantic Object Model (SOM) and Agent Web Protocol (AWP) specifications.

Full proposal: https://github.com/plasmate-labs/plasmate/blob/master/docs/SCHEMA-ORG-PROPOSAL.md

We would welcome feedback on whether this fits within Schema.org's scope and how to best model it within existing type hierarchies.

issues.title: Proposal: extend schema:location domain to include Person
issues.author: ddeboer
issues.body:
## Summary

Extend the domain of [`schema:location`](https://schema.org/location) to include [`schema:Person`](https://schema.org/Person), so that generic place associations can be expressed on persons – just as they already can on organisations.

## Motivation

`schema:location` is currently defined on Action, Event, InteractionCounter, and Organization. Its range (Place | PostalAddress | Text | VirtualLocation) makes it a flexible, generic property for expressing 'where something is located'.

For Organization, `location` serves as a catch-all place property. Person, however, lacks an equivalent. The only place-accepting properties on Person are:

- `birthPlace` / `deathPlace` – life events
- `homeLocation` / `workLocation` – specific relationship types
- `address` – accepts PostalAddress | Text, but not Place

This leaves a gap: there is no schema.org-compatible way to express a generic place association on a Person. Real-world use cases include:

- **Cultural heritage**: an artist associated with various cities throughout their career (not necessarily as home or work, but as places of significance)
- **Biographical data**: a historical figure connected to places where the nature of the connection is unknown or unspecified
- **Genealogical records**: persons linked to locations that don't fit the birth/death/home/work categories

These are common scenarios in cultural heritage and archival data, where place associations are often recorded without a specific relationship type.

## Proposal

Add Person to the domain of `schema:location`. This would allow:

```json
{
  "@type": "Person",
  "name": "Piet Mondriaan",
  "birthPlace": {
    "@type": "Place",
    "name": "Amersfoort"
  },
  "location": [
    {
      "@type": "Place",
      "name": "Amsterdam"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Place",
      "name": "Paris"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Place",
      "name": "New York"
    }
  ]
}
```

## Rationale

- **Consistency**: Organization already has `location` for generic place associations. Person has analogous needs.
- **Minimal change**: no new types or properties are needed – just a domain extension.
- **Non-breaking**: existing Person data is unaffected; `location` becomes an additional option.
- **Complements existing properties**: `homeLocation` and `workLocation` remain available for more specific relationships. `location` fills the gap for cases where the relationship type is unknown or doesn't fit those categories.

issues.title: Community Example: CleaningService + LocalBusiness markup for multi-location service companies
issues.author: DaveCookVectorLabs
issues.body:
## Proposed Wiki Addition

I'd like to propose a new Community Example page for the wiki: **CleaningService and LocalBusiness Markup for Multi-Location Service Companies**.

This covers a gap in the current examples — there are no community examples showing how to use `CleaningService` (a subtype of `LocalBusiness > HomeAndConstructionBusiness`) with:

- Multiple `location` entries for multi-office businesses
- `areaServed` with city/region coverage
- `hasOfferCatalog` for nested service catalogs
- `numberOfEmployees` with `QuantitativeValue`
- `sameAs` linking to Wikidata entities
- A companion `Dataset` example showing how a service business can publish open pricing data with structured markup

### Proposed page content

The full page is ready to add to the wiki as `Examples:-CleaningService-and-LocalBusiness-Markup`. Here's the content:

---

# CleaningService and LocalBusiness Markup for Multi-Location Service Companies

## Question:
How do I use Schema.org to mark up a commercial cleaning company that operates from multiple locations, offers several service types (e.g., window cleaning, janitorial), and wants to include structured pricing data and service area coverage?

## Answer:
Use [schema.org/CleaningService](https://schema.org/CleaningService) as the `@type` — it inherits from [LocalBusiness](https://schema.org/LocalBusiness) and supports all the properties you need: `location`, `areaServed`, `hasOfferCatalog`, `priceRange`, and `employee` counts.

For multi-location businesses, nest multiple `location` entries. For structured service descriptions, use `hasOfferCatalog` with [OfferCatalog](https://schema.org/OfferCatalog) and individual [Offer](https://schema.org/Offer) items.

### Example 1: Multi-Location CleaningService with Service Catalog (JSON-LD)

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "CleaningService",
  "name": "Binx Professional Cleaning",
  "url": "https://www.binx.ca/",
  "description": "WSIB-covered commercial and residential cleaning company operating in Northern Ontario since 2013 with 70+ staff.",
  "foundingDate": "2013",
  "numberOfEmployees": {
    "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
    "minValue": 70
  },
  "priceRange": "$$",
  "currenciesAccepted": "CAD",
  "areaServed": [
    {
      "@type": "City",
      "name": "North Bay",
      "containedInPlace": {
        "@type": "AdministrativeArea",
        "name": "Northern Ontario, Canada"
      }
    },
    { "@type": "City", "name": "Sudbury" },
    { "@type": "City", "name": "Timmins" },
    { "@type": "City", "name": "Sault Ste. Marie" }
  ],
  "location": [
    {
      "@type": "Place",
      "name": "Binx Professional Cleaning — North Bay",
      "address": {
        "@type": "PostalAddress",
        "streetAddress": "1315 Hammond Street",
        "addressLocality": "North Bay",
        "addressRegion": "ON",
        "postalCode": "P1B 2J2",
        "addressCountry": "CA"
      },
      "telephone": "+1-705-845-0998"
    },
    {
      "@type": "Place",
      "name": "Binx Professional Cleaning — Sudbury",
      "address": {
        "@type": "PostalAddress",
        "streetAddress": "767 Barry Downe Road, Unit 203M",
        "addressLocality": "Sudbury",
        "addressRegion": "ON",
        "postalCode": "P3A 3T6",
        "addressCountry": "CA"
      },
      "telephone": "+1-249-239-1225"
    }
  ],
  "hasOfferCatalog": {
    "@type": "OfferCatalog",
    "name": "Commercial Cleaning Services",
    "itemListElement": [
      {
        "@type": "OfferCatalog",
        "name": "Window Cleaning",
        "itemListElement": [
          {
            "@type": "Offer",
            "itemOffered": {
              "@type": "Service",
              "name": "Exterior Window Cleaning",
              "description": "Exterior commercial window cleaning including ground-level, ladder, boom lift, rope access, and swing stage methods"
            }
          }
        ]
      }
    ]
  },
  "sameAs": [
    "https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q138850701",
    "https://github.com/DaveCookVectorLabs/window-cleaning-2026"
  ]
}
```

### Example 2: Dataset with Service Business as Creator

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "Dataset",
  "name": "Commercial Window Cleaning Costs — Northern Ontario",
  "description": "5,376 commercial window cleaning cost scenarios across 28 building profiles in 4 Northern Ontario cities.",
  "url": "https://huggingface.co/datasets/davecook1985/commercial-window-cleaning-costs-northern-ontario",
  "license": "https://opensource.org/licenses/MIT",
  "creator": {
    "@type": "CleaningService",
    "name": "Binx Professional Cleaning",
    "url": "https://www.binx.ca/"
  },
  "spatialCoverage": {
    "@type": "Place",
    "name": "Northern Ontario, Canada"
  },
  "identifier": "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19373427"
}
```

### Key Points
- **CleaningService** inherits from `LocalBusiness > HomeAndConstructionBusiness`
- Use multiple `location` entries to keep the entity unified across offices
- `areaServed` describes service coverage beyond physical office locations
- `numberOfEmployees` takes a `QuantitativeValue` — use `minValue` for seasonal fluctuation
- `sameAs` links to Wikidata and other authoritative references for entity resolution

---

Happy to adjust the format or content if needed. Would also be glad to submit this as a PR if there's a preferred workflow.
