issues.title: JSON-LD example: Healthcare facility cleaning service with VOC compliance data
issues.author: DaveCookVectorLabs
issues.body:
## Proposal: Healthcare CleaningService + VOC Compliance JSON-LD Examples

Following up on [issue #4790](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4790) which provided LocalBusiness + CleaningService examples for commercial cleaning, this issue proposes additional JSON-LD examples for healthcare facility cleaning services that include VOC (Volatile Organic Compound) compliance data.

### Use Case

Healthcare facilities need to evaluate cleaning service providers based on regulatory compliance — specifically whether the cleaning products used meet VOC limits set by EPA (40 CFR Part 59), CARB, and Canada SOR/2021-268. Structured data for this use case would help facility managers discover compliant service providers.

### Proposed JSON-LD Example

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "CleaningService",
  "name": "Binx Professional Cleaning",
  "url": "https://www.binx.ca/commercial.php",
  "areaServed": [
    {"@type": "City", "name": "North Bay", "containedInPlace": {"@type": "AdministrativeArea", "name": "Ontario"}},
    {"@type": "City", "name": "Sudbury", "containedInPlace": {"@type": "AdministrativeArea", "name": "Ontario"}}
  ],
  "serviceType": "Healthcare Facility Cleaning",
  "hasOfferCatalog": {
    "@type": "OfferCatalog",
    "name": "Healthcare Cleaning Services",
    "itemListElement": [
      {
        "@type": "Offer",
        "itemOffered": {
          "@type": "Service",
          "name": "VOC-Compliant Patient Room Cleaning",
          "description": "Daily cleaning using products compliant with Canada SOR/2021-268 and EPA 40 CFR Part 59 VOC limits"
        }
      }
    ]
  },
  "knowsAbout": [
    "VOC compliance",
    "IPAC Canada protocols",
    "Healthcare facility sanitation",
    "OSHA permissible exposure limits"
  ],
  "sameAs": [
    "https://github.com/DaveCookVectorLabs/healthcare-voc-compliance",
    "https://zenodo.org/records/19455155"
  ]
}
```

### Related Resources

- Open-source VOC compliance calculator: https://github.com/DaveCookVectorLabs/healthcare-voc-compliance
- VOC regulatory limits dataset (650 records, 26 jurisdictions): https://zenodo.org/records/19455155
- PDF guide: https://www.binx.ca/guides/healthcare-voc-compliance-guide.pdf

### Relevant Schema.org Types

- `CleaningService` (subtype of `LocalBusiness`)
- `Service` / `Offer`
- `HealthAndBeautyBusiness` (potential parent for healthcare cleaning)

This builds on the pattern established in #4790 for commercial cleaning services.

issues.author: DaveCookVectorLabs

## Context

This issue submits JSON-LD structured data examples for an open reference dataset and working paper that models Canadian home care service-mix decisions. The project publishes eight CSV datasets and a 17-page working paper covering all ten Canadian provinces and three territories.

The dataset is relevant to schema.org because it demonstrates useful patterns for:

- `schema:Dataset` markup with licensed open data (CC BY 4.0)
- `schema:Book` / `schema:ScholarlyArticle` markup with a DOI
- Cross-referencing related resources via `schema:isBasedOn`, `schema:isPartOf`, and `schema:citation`
- `schema:ClaimReview` style scope-of-practice warnings

## Resources

- Working paper: https://www.binx.ca/guides/home-care-cost-model-guide.pdf
- Zenodo DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19491364
- GitHub: https://github.com/DaveCookVectorLabs/home-care-cost-model
- Hugging Face datasets: https://huggingface.co/datasets/davecook1985/home-care-cost-model

## JSON-LD examples

### Dataset (CC BY 4.0, DOI, publisher)

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Dataset",
  "name": "Home Care Cost Model — Canadian Service Mix, Rate Bands, and Tax Relief Sensitivity",
  "description": "Open dataset companion to the Home Care Cost Model working paper. Eight CSVs totalling ~9,000 rows covering scope of practice, 2026 tax parameters, provincial subsidised programs, and engine-derived scenario grids.",
  "url": "https://github.com/DaveCookVectorLabs/home-care-cost-model",
  "sameAs": "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.19491364",
  "identifier": "10.5281/zenodo.19491364",
  "license": "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/",
  "creator": {
    "@type": "Person",
    "name": "Dave Cook",
    "email": "dave@binx.ca"
  },
  "variableMeasured": [
    "Katz ADL score",
    "Lawton IADL score",
    "PSW hourly rate",
    "subsidised hours per week",
    "out-of-pocket monthly CAD after credits"
  ],
  "temporalCoverage": "2026/2026",
  "spatialCoverage": {"@type": "Place", "name": "Canada"}
}
```

### ScholarlyArticle with DOI

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "ScholarlyArticle",
  "headline": "The Home Care Cost Model: Personal Support, Housekeeping, and Service Mix Decisions for Aging in Place in Canada",
  "author": {"@type": "Person", "name": "Dave Cook"},
  "datePublished": "2026-04-10",
  "identifier": {"@type": "PropertyValue", "propertyID": "DOI", "value": "10.5281/zenodo.19491364"},

  "isPartOf": {
    "@type": "CreativeWork",
    "name": "Binx open-source projects",

  }

```

Reference model only; not clinical or financial advice.

issues.title: Proposal: Add planInstructions property to ExercisePlan
issues.author: mnito
issues.body:
### Background

Currently the **ExercisePlan** schema lacks an unambiguous way for defining a routine like a HIIT workout or weightlifting sets and reps, limiting its utility for defining exercise routines. The description implies that describing exercise routines is a goal of this schema.

Some of the current options for defining exercise routines are nesting **ExercisePlan** schemas or **HowTo**-related schemas using `hasPart`, or defining the base schema with an MTE of **ExercisePlan** and **HowTo**. Both of these approaches feel indirect. Regardless, the core issue is that there is ambiguity here.

### Proposed Solution

Add a `planInstructions` property to **ExercisePlan**, with the **CreativeWork**, **ItemList**, or **Text** expected type

**Description**: "A routine or steps in the workout plan, in the form of a single item (document, video, etc.) or an ordered list with HowToStep and/or HowToSection items."

### Prior Work

This property serves a similar semantic purpose to the `recipeInstructions` property on **Recipe**.

### Alternatives

Alternatively, examples for ExercisePlan would be helpful in resolving the ambiguity. E.g. defining a HIIT or weightlifting workout routine

--

I think there is a strong case for a `planInstructions` field based on the described purpose of the **ExercisePlan** schema and how **Recipe** has a similar field.

issues.title: Proposal: Add Colorectal to MedicalSpecialty enumeration
issues.author: diegovfeder
issues.body:
## Background

The current `MedicalSpecialty` enumeration does not include a value that clearly represents colorectal surgery or coloproctology.

The closest existing values are:

- `Gastroenterologic`
- `Surgical`

But both are only partial matches:

- `Gastroenterologic` captures part of the organ system, not the specialty itself
- `Surgical` captures the procedural nature, but loses anatomical specificity

This stands out because the enumeration already includes anatomy-specific values such as `Urologic`, `Gynecologic`, `Cardiovascular`, and `Gastroenterologic`.

## Proposed solution

Add:

- `Colorectal`

## Why this fits

`Colorectal` matches the existing enum style well:

- concise
- anatomy-based
- internationally understandable
- parallel to values like `Urologic` and `Gynecologic`

It is also broader and more accurate than `Proctologic`, which may suggest only anorectal scope.

## Supporting context

Colorectal surgery is widely recognized as a distinct specialty or subspecialty focused on diseases of the:

- colon
- rectum
- anus
- anal canal
- perianal region

This includes conditions such as hemorrhoids, fissures, abscesses, fistulas, polyps, and colorectal cancer.

Recognition examples include:

- **ABMS** — Colon and Rectal Surgery
- **ASCRS** — American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons
- **UEMS** — Coloproctology section
- **SBCP** — Sociedade Brasileira de Coloproctologia

## Closing note

Adding `Colorectal` would be a small, low-risk improvement that makes healthcare structured data more precise for `Physician`, `MedicalClinic`, and `MedicalOrganization` markup.

issues.title: Proposal: Add organicPurityLevel to Product and Certification to distinguish between 100% and 95% Organic thresholds (etc)
issues.author: MLSpyShop
issues.body:
Currently, the Product and Certification types do not have a granular way to distinguish between different regulatory levels of organic purity. While many products carry an "Organic" label, the actual purity varies significantly between jurisdictions (e.g., USDA "100% Organic" vs. the 95% threshold allowed by Canada Organic/COR or the EU).

For high-integrity supply chain tracking and transparent consumer search engines, we need a standardized property to represent these specific regulatory tiers.

Proposed Property

• Property Name: organicPurityLevel
• Expected Type: Text or DefinedTerm
• Domain: Product, Certification
Suggested Enumeration (The GOPIS Scale)

1.	P-100: 100% Organic (Strictly 100% ingredients; no synthetic processing aids).

2.	P-95: Organic (The standard 95% threshold used by USDA, COR, EU, and JAS).

3.	P-70: Made with Organic (70%–94% organic content; no official seal permitted).

4.	P-I: Organic Ingredients (< 70% organic content; identification only in the ingredient list).

Example JSON-LD

{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "Product",
  "name": "High-Integrity Organic Hemp Oil",
  "brand": {
    "@type": "Brand",
    "name": "Landry Industries"
  },
  "certification": {
    "@type": "Certification",
    "name": "USDA 100% Organic",
    "certificationRating": "P-100"
  },
  "additionalProperty": {
    "@type": "PropertyValue",
    "name": "organicPurityLevel",
    "value": "100%"
  }
}

Use Case

Consumer search engines and supply chain audits need to differentiate between "Absolute Purity" and "Regulatory Standard Purity."

Standardizing this metadata prevents the obfuscation of the "5% buffer" (non-organic substances) allowed in standard P-95 and lower certifications.

This allows search engines and AI to understand the certified organic industry.

issues.title: ## Titre de la proposition Extension CaribbeanCulturalWork pour schema.org — Caribbean Metadata Standard
issues.author: heso73
issues.body:
Titre de la proposition
Extension CaribbeanCulturalWork pour schema.org — Caribbean Metadata Standard

 Résumé
Nous proposons l'ajout d'un type `CaribbeanCulturalWork` et de propriétés
associées à schema.org, basés sur le Caribbean Metadata Standard (CMS) v1.0.

 Problème documenté
Les types schema.org existants (CreativeWork, MusicRecording, Movie, Book) ne
permettent pas de décrire les spécificités culturelles caribéennes :
- Pas de champ pour les langues créoles
- Pas de vocabulaire pour les expressions culturelles caribéennes (zouk, gwo-ka…)
- Pas de notion de territoire caribéen comme distinct du pays de production
- Pas de score ou indicateur d'authenticité culturelle

 Proposition de type

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "CaribbeanCulturalWork",
  "@id": "https://schema.org/CaribbeanCulturalWork",
  "rdfs:subClassOf": "schema:CreativeWork",
  "rdfs:label": "CaribbeanCulturalWork",
  "rdfs:comment": "A creative work originating from or deeply rooted in Caribbean culture, language, and territory.",
  "schema:url": "https://caribbeanmetadata.org/schema/v1.0/cms-metadata.json"
}
```

 Nouvelles propriétés proposées

| Propriété | Type | Description |
|-----------|------|-------------|
| caribbeanTerritory | Text | Territoire caribéen d'origine (GP, MQ, HT, CU…) |
| creoleLanguage | Text | Variante créole utilisée (guadeloupean, haitian, martiniquais…) |
| caribbeanIdentityScore | Integer | Score d'ancrage culturel caribéen (0-100) |
| caribbeanTheme | Text | Thème culturel caribéen (creolization, oral_tradition…) |
| culturalExpression | Text | Expression culturelle spécifique (zouk, gwo_ka, carnival…) |
| cmsComplianceLevel | Text | Niveau de certification CMS (bronze/silver/gold/platinum) |
| diasporaPerspective | Boolean | Contenu créé depuis la diaspora caribéenne |

 Exemple JSON-LD

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": ["Movie", "CaribbeanCulturalWork"],
  "name": "Anba Dlo",
  "alternateName": ["Sous les eaux", "Beneath the Waters"],
  "director": { "@type": "Person", "name": "Marie-Cécile Bonhomme" },
  "inLanguage": "gcf",
  "dateCreated": "2025",
  "datePublished": "2026",
  "caribbeanTerritory": ["GP", "MQ"],
  "creoleLanguage": "guadeloupean",
  "caribbeanIdentityScore": 88,
  "caribbeanTheme": ["creolization", "maritime_culture", "oral_tradition"],
  "culturalExpression": ["gwo_ka", "carnival"],
  "cmsComplianceLevel": "platinum",
  "license": "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-nc-sa/4.0/",
  "sameAs": "https://caribbeanmetadata.org/examples/audiovisual/film.json"
}
```

 Alignement avec standards existants
- Dublin Core : mapping complet disponible
- EIDR : compatible via identity.isbn_issn_isan
- ISRC/ISAN : champ dédié isbn_issn_isan
- ISO 639 : langues caribéennes (ht, gcf, pap, srn)
- ISO 3166 : territoires caribéens

 Référence technique
Schéma JSON officiel : https://caribbeanmetadata.org/schema/v1.0/cms-metadata.json
Documentation : https://caribbeanmetadata.org/developers.html
Contact : caribbeanmetadata.org

issues.title: Proposal - Fix for Organizations with multiple locations.
issues.author: ghost
issues.body:
To quote Michael Scott: "There are four kinds of business: tourism, food service, railroads, and sales. And hospitals/manufacturing. And air travel." In truth, things get complicated and there are always other types of businesses or organizations that no one really considered, and often, it seems, things just kind of get shoved where they fit, which gets a bit confusing for humans and machines (and let's face it, most LLMs and consumers are addicted to context).

The problem I've seen for organizations with multiple locations is that there is simply not a good way to disambiguate multiple locations that are part of a single organization in schema.org. Period. Schema experts (as well as most advice on the internet) tell you "well, put them as subOrganizations or departments" — I would argue that on the majority of websites that's wrong, and that it's a problem.
subOrganization implies separate business entities that are related (think franchise/franchisee, or Google → YouTube, Meta → Facebook). It does not imply 4 restaurants owned by the same owner in the same city.

department seems to have been intended for department stores, pharmacies, and bakeries with cafes — but its range (Organization) implies ownership/separate-entity status for what should really be routing within one entity. Walgreens doesn't have a subsidiary Pharmacy organization; It has a Phone Number for the Pharmacy. 

The location property is promising, but if you just have a reference, the validator defaults the reference to Place. And if you add a specific LocalBusiness type, Google's Rich Results Test identifies it as an Organization AND a LocalBusiness — which, it isn't. I don't really care too much about rich results, especially when it comes to Organization or LocalBusiness, because your schema really doesn't impact what Google shows. However, the purpose of schema.org is to help machines understand the internet, and if one of the largest consumers of schema can't disambiguate, the problem is probably pretty widespread. It's also naive to believe that having what Google considers invalid schema on a post can't lead to consequences ranging from very minor to very severe and long-lasting.

**The problem is threefold:**

**#1 — References from an organization node to the sub-node**
On the organization node: in the location property, a single @id reference defaults to Place, creating a type mismatch against the actual node definition. Adding the specific LocalBusiness subtype makes Google's validator see separate Organizations.
**Proposed solution:** Explicitly allow the expected value of location to be a LocalBusiness (not just a LocalBusiness inherited via Place), and clarify that values in location are not standalone Organizations regardless of inherited type. subOrganization already handles the case where you want to list LocalBusinesses that are also separate Organizations (i.e., franchisees). 

**#2 — References from the sub-node back to the organization node**
branchOf (deprecated) sort of solved this; the fact that it was superseded by parentOrganization makes a lot of sense. But parentOrganization doesn't definitively give a machine the concrete answer to "is this a separate business entity?"
**Proposed solution:** If a LocalBusiness has a value for parentOrganization, this should signal that it is NOT a separate Organization. In the case of a franchisee (which IS a separate Organization with a parent), the publisher would multi-type the node with Organization explicitly to disambiguate.

**#3 — References from offerings (Service, MedicalProcedure, FoodService, etc.) pointing back to their actual provider node**

This is where things get most complicated. Schema.org is all over the place for services that are provided, and while services don't matter much for rich results, they absolutely matter for machine understanding. Currently, provider is the way to point from a service back up the chain. Its range is Organization, which makes sense. But there's no way to express which specific location of that Organization is providing the service.

**Proposed solution:** Introduce a new property — providerLocation — that points specifically to a LocalBusiness. The specific location providing a service often matters more than the umbrella Organization (e.g., "order it from the Home Depot on 39th, they're always on time compared to the one downtown"). Machines should have this context too.
Most importantly, this issue isn't new:

[#806](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/806) raised a similar hierarchy concern for MedicalOrganization (closed as not planned, though the decoupling for MedicalOrganization does appear to have occurred somehow).
[#3420](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/3420) continues that work for Physician.

Both are gestures at the same underlying problem: there isn't a clean way to disambiguate a LocalBusiness from an Organization.

issues.title: DefinedTermSet lacks vocabulary for temporal versioning and cross-system classification mappings
issues.author: jackmmaher
issues.body:
**Context**

We've implemented DefinedTermSet for the UK's Standard Industrial Classification (SIC) system at [siccodes.co.uk](https://siccodes.co.uk), covering SIC 2007 (731 codes), SIC 2026 (1,474 codes), GICS (273), and ICB (249).

This is related to #1276 (SIC/NAICS codes), #3384 (concept hierarchy), and #2192 (ISCO08 classification).

**Problem**

Two patterns have no clean Schema.org vocabulary:

### 1. Temporal versioning of classification systems

SIC 2007 is being replaced by SIC 2026 (effective April 2026). We use `supersededBy` on the DefinedTermSet to link the old system to the new one, and on individual DefinedTerm entries where the ONS correspondence table defines a successor.

- DefinedTermSet (SIC 2007): https://siccodes.co.uk/schema/sic-2007.jsonld
- Individual term with supersededBy: https://siccodes.co.uk/schema/sic-62020.jsonld

Is `supersededBy` the right predicate for classification-system succession? Other government systems facing the same issue: NAICS (US, revised every 5 years), NACE (EU), ISIC (UN).

### 2. Cross-system mappings with information loss

We map between SIC, GICS (MSCI/S&P), and ICB (FTSE Russell). Some mappings are exact equivalences, others are approximate. We use `sameAs` for exact and `related` for approximate, but `related` doesn't express directionality or confidence.

SKOS has `closeMatch` vs `exactMatch`, but we wanted to stay within Schema.org vocabulary. Is there a better predicate for "maps to with known information loss"?

## Live implementation

- SIC 2007 DefinedTermSet: https://siccodes.co.uk/sic-codes
- Cross-mapping page: https://siccodes.co.uk/convert/sic-2007-to-2026
- JSON-LD (full set): https://siccodes.co.uk/schema/sic-2007.jsonld
- JSON-LD (single term): https://siccodes.co.uk/schema/sic-62020.jsonld
```

issues.title: Introduce FAQSection as a WebPageElement subtype for FAQ content that's part of a page, not the whole page
issues.author: jdevalk
issues.body:
## Problem

`FAQPage` was designed for pages whose primary purpose is question-and-answer content. In practice, it has been widely (mis)used on pages where Q&A is one section among many — product pages, landing pages, articles with an FAQ at the bottom. There is no honest schema.org type for *"this page contains an FAQ section, but the FAQs are not the page's main entity."*

Publishers face a bad choice today:

1. Declare `FAQPage` and lie about what the page is.
2. Skip schema on the FAQ section entirely.

Most chose the first. Consumers (search engines, AI agents) then have no reliable way to tell whether a `FAQPage` declaration accurately scopes the page.

Issue #2349 asked this exact question ("how do I combine `FAQPage` with `ItemPage` on a product page?") and was closed with a stacked-JSON-LD workaround. Issue #2317 tried `isPartOf` to scope `Question`s to a parent `FAQPage` and reported that Google ignored the property.

As of May 2026, Google has [deprecated FAQ rich results entirely](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/appearance/structured-data/faqpage), driven in significant part by years of `FAQPage` misuse the spec never gave publishers a clean alternative for.

## Proposal

Introduce **`FAQSection`** as a subtype of [`WebPageElement`](https://schema.org/WebPageElement), alongside existing siblings (`SiteNavigationElement`, `WPHeader`, `WPFooter`, `WPSideBar`, `Table`, `WPAdBlock`).

`FAQSection` would:

- Be referenced via `hasPart` on the parent `WebPage`, `Article`, `Product`, or any `CreativeWork`.
- Contain its `Question` children via `hasPart` (each `Question` retains its `acceptedAnswer` as today).
- Have **no** `mainEntity` property in idiomatic use. That's the point: an FAQ section, by definition, is not the main entity of anything. If the FAQ *is* the main entity of the page, `FAQPage` is still the correct type.

### Example: a product page with an FAQ section

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "WebPage",
  "mainEntity": {
    "@type": "Product",
    "name": "Coffee Grinder X",
    "offers": { "@type": "Offer", "price": "199.00", "priceCurrency": "USD" }
  },
  "hasPart": {
    "@type": "FAQSection",
    "name": "Frequently Asked Questions",
    "hasPart": [
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "What grind size is best for espresso?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "A fine grind, similar to table salt."
        }
      },
      {
        "@type": "Question",
        "name": "Is the burr replaceable?",
        "acceptedAnswer": {
          "@type": "Answer",
          "text": "Yes, replacement burrs are available from the manufacturer."
        }
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

Every claim in this graph is true. The page is a `WebPage` whose main entity is a `Product`. The FAQ exists as a section within the page. Consumers can surface, ignore, or reason about the FAQ without parsing inferred relationships.

## Why `WebPageElement` is the right parent

`WebPageElement` already exists as schema.org's concept of "a part of a page." Its existing subtypes describe scoped sections (navigation, header, footer, sidebar, ad block, table). `FAQSection` slots in with no new structural precedent required. Crucially, it sits at the same conceptual level as those siblings: not a top-level page type, not an entity claim, just a typed section.

## Migration and coexistence

`FAQPage` remains valid for pages that genuinely *are* FAQ pages (support hubs, dedicated Q&A pages). `FAQSection` is the recommended type for embedded FAQ blocks on pages whose primary purpose is something else. This is purely additive — no deprecation of `FAQPage` proposed.

## Open question

Should `FAQSection.hasPart` be range-constrained to `Question`, or stay open like `CreativeWork.hasPart`? Constraining it makes consumers' jobs easier; leaving it open keeps it consistent with the rest of the spec.

## Related prior issues

- #1723 — original `FAQPage` proposal (implemented)
- #2349 — "How To Combine FaqPage With Other Page" (closed; workaround only)
- #2317 — "FAQPage and Question on different webpages" (closed; `isPartOf` not honored)

issues.title: Add answer property to Question for publisher-authored single answers
issues.author: jdevalk
issues.body:
## Problem

`Question` currently has two properties for connecting it to an `Answer`:

- **`acceptedAnswer`** — *"The answer that has been accepted as best, typically on a Question/Answer site."* Designed for community Q&A flows where multiple users post answers and one gets accepted or upvoted.
- **`suggestedAnswer`** — implies the answer is one of several possibilities and may not be correct.

Both fit `QAPage`-style community Q&A. Neither cleanly fits publisher-authored Q&A on `FAQPage` (or the proposed [`FAQSection`](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4816)), where:

- There is no community.
- Nobody "accepted" anything.
- The answer is the answer, not a suggestion.

When `FAQPage` was introduced in 2019, `acceptedAnswer` was retrofitted as the property to use despite the awkward semantics. Every FAQ markup tutorial, every CMS plugin, every Google docs example uses `acceptedAnswer` for what is functionally just *"this is the answer."*

This is a small but accumulating semantic debt. It also prevents downstream consumers from distinguishing between *"a community accepted this answer as best"* (a meaningful claim) and *"the publisher wrote this Q&A pair"* (a different meaningful claim).

## Proposal

Add a property **`answer`** to `Question`:

- **Domain:** `Question`
- **Range:** `Answer`, `Text`
- **Description:** *"The answer to a question authored by the page's publisher (as in an FAQ). For community Q&A pages where multiple answers exist and one has been accepted as best, use `acceptedAnswer` instead. For tentative or alternative answers, use `suggestedAnswer`."*

This is purely additive. `acceptedAnswer` and `suggestedAnswer` retain their meaning and use. `answer` becomes the recommended property for publisher-authored FAQ markup.

### Example

Current pattern, using the retrofitted property:

```json
{
  "@type": "Question",
  "name": "What grind size is best for espresso?",
  "acceptedAnswer": {
    "@type": "Answer",
    "text": "A fine grind, similar to table salt."
  }
}
```

Proposed pattern, using a property whose name matches the relationship:

```json
{
  "@type": "Question",
  "name": "What grind size is best for espresso?",
  "answer": {
    "@type": "Answer",
    "text": "A fine grind, similar to table salt."
  }
}
```

## Migration

No deprecation. No breaking change. `acceptedAnswer` continues to work everywhere it is currently used, including in Google's existing `FAQPage` parsing. New publisher-authored FAQ markup can adopt `answer` immediately or stay on `acceptedAnswer` indefinitely. Tooling that consumes `Question` should handle either property.

## Related

- #4816 — proposes `FAQSection` as a `WebPageElement` subtype for FAQ content that is part of a page rather than the whole page. The two proposals are independent but complementary: `FAQSection` fixes the page-vs-section structural problem, and this `answer` property fixes the Q&A relationship at the property level. Either can ship without the other.

issues.title: [Community Proposal] Direct booking channel vocabulary for LodgingBusiness
issues.author: CohenNathan
issues.body:
### 1. Background

Trippchain operates a meta-search and price-comparison tool for
accommodation. We do not hold inventory and we do not earn commission
on bookings. We maintain the Direct Booking Protocol, an open
specification (CC-BY-4.0) that lets any property publish a
machine-readable description of how a guest can book directly. We
also maintain a live production reference implementation at
`trippchain.com`, including canonical specification and schema URLs.
Package-registry reference libraries for Python and JavaScript, plus
a WordPress reference plugin, are planned follow-on implementation
artifacts rather than prerequisites for this vocabulary discussion.

We are bringing this proposal to the schema.org community because we
believe accommodation booking signals are a recurring gap in the
existing `LodgingBusiness` vocabulary, and that solving it inside
schema.org would benefit consumers, properties, search engines, AI
agents, and meta-search operators alike -- without requiring any
party to adopt the Direct Booking Protocol specifically.

### 2. Motivation

`LodgingBusiness` (and its subtypes `Hotel`, `BedAndBreakfast`,
`Hostel`, `Motel`, `Resort`, `VacationRental`, `Campground`) currently
supports `url`, `telephone`, `email`, `address`, `geo`, and a
`potentialAction` of `ReserveAction` pointing to a single booking
URL.

What is missing:

1. There is no way for a property to declare WHICH of multiple booking
   channels is "direct" (operated by the property) vs "intermediated"
   (operated by an OTA or third party). A `ReserveAction` to
   `booking.com/...` and a `ReserveAction` to the property's own
   widget are structurally indistinguishable in current schema.org.
2. There is no native way to declare non-web direct channels
   (WhatsApp, Telegram, SMS, voice, Messenger, Instagram DM, etc.)
   that are increasingly the primary booking surface for small
   properties -- particularly in markets where Booking.com, Airbnb,
   and Expedia have limited penetration.
3. There is no native way to declare that one channel charges
   commission (and to whom) while another does not, which is
   relevant data for travellers and for tools that surface
   commission-free options.
4. There is no native way to express channel availability
   (always-available widget vs business-hours-only phone vs
   seasonally-staffed inbox).

This proposal addresses (1), (2), and (4) -- leaving (3) for a
separate discussion as it touches commercial-relationship modelling.

### 3. Proposed vocabulary additions

We propose two additions, scoped narrowly and shaped to fit
schema.org's existing patterns.

#### 3.1 New property: `directBookingChannel`

Defined on: `LodgingBusiness` and subtypes.
Expected type: `BookingChannel` (new -- see 3.2) OR
`ReserveAction` OR `CommunicateAction`.
Cardinality: zero-to-many.
Definition: "A direct booking channel operated by the property
itself, as opposed to a third-party intermediary. May be specified
as a `BookingChannel` (preferred), or as an existing
`ReserveAction` / `CommunicateAction` annotated with
`actionStatus = ActiveActionStatus` and an explicit
`provider` reference to the property's own `LodgingBusiness` node."

#### 3.2 New type: `BookingChannel`

Parent: `Intangible`.
Properties:
- `channelType` -- Text, allowlist of suggested values:
  `website`, `widget`, `whatsapp`, `telegram`, `sms`, `voice`,
  `email`, `messenger`, `instagram`, `facebook-page`, `other`.
  Open vocabulary; consumers should treat unknown values as `other`.
- `url` -- URL -- the public address consumers use to reach the
  channel. May be `https://`, `tel:`, `sms:`, `mailto:`, `https://wa.me/`,
  `https://t.me/`, etc. URL scheme is the primary mechanical signal.
- `availableLanguage` -- Language / Text, zero-to-many -- languages
  the channel handles (matches `Language` usage elsewhere in
  schema.org).
- `availabilityStarts` / `availabilityEnds` -- DateTime or Time --
  when the channel is staffed.
- `provider` -- Organization / Person / LocalBusiness -- who operates
  the channel. For direct channels, this is the property itself.
- `additionalType` -- URL -- optional pointer to a more specific type
  (e.g. a Direct Booking Protocol `path_type` value URI).

### 4. Use cases (worked examples)

#### 4.1 A small B&B with three direct channels

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "BedAndBreakfast",
  "@id": "https://example-bnb.com/#property",
  "name": "Example B&B",
  "url": "https://example-bnb.com/",
  "directBookingChannel": [
    {
      "@type": "BookingChannel",
      "channelType": "website",
      "url": "https://example-bnb.com/book",
      "availableLanguage": ["en", "it"],
      "provider": { "@id": "https://example-bnb.com/#property" }
    },
    {
      "@type": "BookingChannel",
      "channelType": "whatsapp",
      "url": "https://wa.me/15555550123",
      "availableLanguage": ["en", "it"],
      "provider": { "@id": "https://example-bnb.com/#property" }
    },
    {
      "@type": "BookingChannel",
      "channelType": "email",
      "url": "mailto:book@example-bnb.com",
      "availableLanguage": ["en"],
      "provider": { "@id": "https://example-bnb.com/#property" }
    }
  ]
}
```

A consumer (browser, AI agent, meta-search, voice assistant) can
present any of these to the traveller depending on context, knowing
all three are property-operated and commission-free.

#### 4.2 A hotel that publishes both direct and OTA channels

The hotel declares its direct channels via `directBookingChannel`
and its OTA channels via existing `potentialAction` /
`ReserveAction` with a different `provider`:

```json
{
  "@type": "Hotel",
  "@id": "https://example-hotel.com/#property",
  "name": "Example Hotel",
  "directBookingChannel": [
    {
      "@type": "BookingChannel",
      "channelType": "widget",
      "url": "https://example-hotel.com/book-widget",
      "provider": { "@id": "https://example-hotel.com/#property" }
    }
  ],
  "potentialAction": [
    {
      "@type": "ReserveAction",
      "target": "https://www.booking.com/hotel/.../example-hotel.html",
      "provider": {
        "@type": "Organization",
        "name": "Booking.com",
        "url": "https://www.booking.com/"
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

A consumer reading this can present the direct channel as such, and
the OTA channel as such, with the commercial relationship made
explicit through `provider`.

### 5. Why structured data in schema.org (not a separate standard)

We considered keeping this entirely inside the Direct Booking Protocol
namespace. We are bringing it to schema.org instead for these
reasons:

1. **Consumer adoption is wider when the vocabulary is part of
   schema.org core or its standard extension surface.** Most search
   engines, AI agents, and CMS plugins already consume schema.org.
   A direct-booking vocabulary inside schema.org reaches consumers
   that do not parse `.well-known/direct-booking.json`.
2. **Accommodation is a recurring schema.org topic.** Issues on the
   schema.org tracker discussing `LodgingBusiness` gaps go back
   years. A community-vetted addition here addresses one of the
   highest-impact gaps without introducing a competing top-level
   vocabulary.
3. **The Direct Booking Protocol can coexist.** Properties wanting the
   richer machine-readable contract continue to publish
   `.well-known/direct-booking.json`. The schema.org additions are a
   simpler, more discoverable surface that interoperates cleanly
   with the protocol via the `additionalType` URL pointer.
4. **Search engines have stated, repeatedly, that no special
   structured data is required to appear in AI Overviews or generated
   search experiences.** This proposal is NOT motivated by a claim
   that properties "need" this vocabulary to surface in AI search.
   Properties benefit from a clearer, more accurate signal -- and
   consumers benefit from being able to tell a direct channel from an
   intermediated one -- but the proposal stands on its own merits as
   vocabulary hygiene, independent of any specific search-engine
   behaviour.

### 6. Prior art and related work

- `schema:LodgingBusiness` and subtypes (existing).
- `schema:potentialAction` with `ReserveAction` and
  `CommunicateAction` (existing).
- The Open Travel Alliance (OTA) message specifications (industry
  XML schemas; widely used in OTA-to-PMS messaging; not consumer-
  facing).
- The HTRIO industry initiative for hospitality data interchange
  (peer effort; complementary, not overlapping).
- The Direct Booking Protocol v1, CC-BY-4.0, maintained by Trippchain
  (open spec at https://trippchain.com/spec/direct-booking/v1;
  JSON Schema at https://trippchain.com/schemas/direct-booking/v1.json).

### 7. Impact analysis

- **Backwards compatibility:** additive. Consumers ignoring the new
  property or type are unaffected.
- **Existing usage:** `potentialAction` / `ReserveAction` is the
  current pattern; the proposal complements rather than replaces it.
- **Search-engine consumption:** unaffected unless a search engine
  chooses to use the new signal. We do not request any specific
  search-engine behaviour.
- **CMS and plugin ecosystem:** existing schema.org plugins continue
  to work. Hospitality plugins can adopt the new vocabulary at their
  own pace. The Trippchain WordPress reference plugin will adopt it
  in v1.0 if this proposal is accepted (or in a v1.1 patch if the
  proposal lands later).
- **Performance:** negligible. The new properties are small
  additions to existing nodes.

### 8. Maintainer commitment

If the schema.org community is willing to consider this proposal,
Trippchain commits to:

- Maintain a publicly-fetchable production reference implementation
  and publish open-source reference libraries for Python, JavaScript,
  and WordPress as follow-on implementation artifacts.
- Maintain a worked-examples gallery for community review.
- Respond to issues on the schema.org tracker tagged with
  `direct-booking` within 5 business days.
- Provide a stable contact: protocols@trippchain.com.

We do NOT request any commercial relationship with schema.org, and
we do NOT seek named placement or attribution beyond the standard
contributor credit. This is a contribution to a vocabulary we want
to use, and to a community we want to participate in.

### 9. Next steps

We propose:

1. Open this letter as an issue on the schema.org GitHub repository
   tagged with `LodgingBusiness` and `direct-booking`.
2. Invite community discussion for at least 30 days before any
   schema change is requested.
3. After discussion, refine the proposal based on community input
   and re-submit as a formal pull request following the schema.org
   contribution guide.

We are happy to participate in any teleconference or working-group
meeting the community prefers.

Sincerely,

The Trippchain Direct Booking Protocol maintainers
protocols@trippchain.com
https://trippchain.com/trust-methodology

issues.title: Proposal: Add CompetitionBusiness and Competition types for prize competition / raffle websites
issues.author: RyanZap95
issues.body:
Hey Schema.org team,

I would like to propose two new schema types to better represent online prize competition / raffle platforms and the individual competitions they publish.

**Background**

There is currently no dedicated Schema.org type that accurately models online competition or raffle websites where users purchase entries/tickets for a chance to win a prize.

At present, many sites use Product schema to represent competitions because it is the closest available option. However, this creates semantic inaccuracies because:

- The item being offered is not the prize itself, it is simply the chance to win the item. Therefore the user is not purchasing ownership of a product, so product schema is incredibly misleading for this industry.
- The transaction represents entry into a competition/chance-based event. This is different to event schema in the sense that the event is continuously on-going. The deadline isn't the day of the event itself. 
- inventory, shipping, GTINs, brand ownership, and other Product concepts are often irrelevant or misleading for competitions/raffles.
- Search engines may incorrectly interpret the page as ecommerce product inventory.

This creates structured data ambiguity for both publishers and consumers of Schema.org data.


**Proposed Types**

- CompetitionBusiness (A subtype intended for businesses whose primary activity is operating online competitions, raffles, sweepstakes, or prize draws.)
- Competition or Raffle (A type representing an individual prize competition, raffle, sweepstake, or prize draw listing.)


**Suggested properties for Competition**

name
description
image
url
entryPrice
entryMethod
maximumEntries
closingDate
drawDate
winner
numberOfWinners
competitionStatus
eligibilityRequirement
minimumAge
organizer
oddsOfWinning
jurisdiction
termsAndConditions
hasPart
isAccessibleForFree


**Potential Benefits**
Competition businesses are growing rapidly in the UK, the EU and soon in the US. I believe there is a huge missed opportunity here and as someone who works in SEO within this industry, there are so many challenges when it comes to schema. 

Some of the potential benefits I can see these schema types benefitting. 

- More accurate semantic representation
- Reduced misuse of Product
- Improved search engine understanding
- Better structured data consistency across competition websites
- Clearer distinction between ecommerce and competition entry models
- Extensible support for regulated jurisdictions and compliance metadata


Thank you for considering the proposal!

issues.title: Missing context entry for fibo registration
issues.author: OmarJAH
issues.body:
Hi there,

In the JSON-LD file for version 30.0 ([link](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/420231f6bfac8372fc564abb121fae57ccb36a0c/data/releases/30.0/schemaorg-all-https.jsonld)) following node exists:

```
 {
    "@id": "https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Arrangements/Registration/hasRegistrationIdentifier",
    "@type": "rdf:Property"
  }
```

**Issue**:

This @id is in absolute form. Interestingly, @context does not declare a prefix that covers https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Arrangements/Registration/ — the FIBO prefixes in the context use the namespace pattern https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Arrangements/Documents/ (fibo-fnd-arr-doc) and …/LifecyclesAndOccurrences/ (fibo-fnd-arr-lif), but no  …/Registration/ namespace is present. So it cannot be compacted with the current @context — it likely needs either a new prefix added (e.g. fibo-fnd-arr-reg) or fixing whichever upstream  mapping produced this node.

Here the analysis results including the previous 5 versions:

  | Version | Total nodes | All compact with known prefix? | Offenders |
  |---------|-------------|--------------------------------|-----------|
  | 30.0 (reference) | 3235 | No — 1 absolute | `https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Arrangements/Registration/hasRegistrationIdentifier` |
  | 29.4 | 3203 | No — 1 absolute | same `…/Registration/hasRegistrationIdentifier` |
  | 29.3 | 2965 | Yes | — |
  | 29.2 | 2962 | Yes | — |
  | 29.1 | 2958 | Yes | — |
  | 29.0 | 2955 | Yes | — |

**Proposal**:
Please add the missing context entry for https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/FND/Arrangements/Registration/ 

Sinc. Omar

issues.title: Proposal for new term: Audiology as a MedicalSpecialty
issues.author: raidengatedesign
issues.body:
**Background**: While developing a website for a client in the audiology/hearing health space, I noticed that Audiology is missing as a dedicated MedicalSpecialty in the Schema.org vocabulary. This prompted me to research the gap more formally and submit this proposal.

**Definition/Description:** Audiology is the branch of science concerned with the sense of hearing, balance, and related disorders. It focuses on the diagnosis, management, and treatment of hearing-related conditions, including, but not limited to, tinnitus, hyperacusis, and misophonia.

**Motivation:** Currently, `Otolaryngologic` (ear, nose, and throat) is often used as a catch-all category. However, this is insufficient for modern digital health information architecture for the following reasons:

1. **Scope mismatch:** Otolaryngology is primarily surgical and medically focused on the physical anatomy. Audiology focuses on the perception of sound, auditory processing, and non-surgical management.
2. **Clinical accuracy:** Conditions like Tinnitus and Hyperacusis are frequently non-anatomical/non-surgical in origin; they involve complex neuro-auditory processing that requires specialized audiologic diagnostic frameworks (e.g., UCL - Uncomfortable Loudness Levels).
3. **SEO and Information Retrieval:** Search engines (like Google) rely on precise taxonomy to connect patients with appropriate care providers. Using `Otolaryngologic` for a tinnitus-related auditory therapy content is too broad and often inaccurate. Adding `Audiology` would allow for more precise mapping between medical conditions, expert specialists (Audiologists), and specialized therapeutic services.

**Supporting References:**

* World Health Organization (WHO) - Tinnitus: [https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/deafness-and-hearing-loss--tinnitus](https://www.who.int/news-room/questions-and-answers/item/deafness-and-hearing-loss--tinnitus)
* American Tinnitus Association: [https://www.ata.org/about-tinnitus/why-are-my-ears-ringing/](https://www.ata.org/about-tinnitus/why-are-my-ears-ringing/)
* British Society of Audiology: [https://thebsa.org.uk/](https://thebsa.org.uk/)
* American Academy of Audiology: [https://www.audiology.org/about-the-aaa/](https://www.audiology.org/about-the-aaa/)
* Wikidata entries:
  * Tinnitus: [https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q192309](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q192309)
  * Misophonia: [https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2054837](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q2054837)
  * Hyperacusis: [https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421356](https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q1421356)

**Proposed Hierarchy:** `Thing > MedicalEntity > MedicalSpecialty > Audiology`

I believe that formally defining `Audiology` within the Schema.org vocabulary would significantly improve the semantic quality of medical data and search results for patients suffering from auditory processing disorders.

issues.title: [Open Source 2.0] Pending Proposal: Create property `sourceFile` for `CreativeWork` to describe the ability to modify across the knowledge infrastructure
issues.author: AbcSxyZ
issues.body:
*Proposal for the [pending section](https://schema.org/docs/pending.home.html).*

## Context

**[Related to my citizen research on the definition of "open source" and the preprint « [Open Source 2.0: From Open Source
Software to Open Source Resources](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20237079) »]**

Similarly to software and its source code, many typologies of digital resources are composed of a distributed/final format and an editable format. These editable formats are commonly designated as source files.

> **Examples:** ODT, DOCX, Markdown or LaTeX files for a PDF document, SVG or PSD files for a PNG/JPEG image, H5P files for interactive HTML content, FLP or ALS project files for an MP3 audio file, .FCStd or .scad design files exported to .stl for 3D printing, etc.

**This `sourceFile` property would create an explicit (!) link between a resource and its source file(s) — its editable components.**

## Problem

Today schema.org provides the ability to describe the right to modify via `license` property without describing the ability to do so through the access to source files.

## Use Case for the Open Knowledge Infrastructure (and beyond)

With the paradigm shift towards « open source resources », this property could become a key component of the modern knowledge infrastructure — though the pattern extends beyond open practices to any digital resource published alongside its source files.

Archives and journal platforms are the most immediate potential consumers of this property. arXiv provides both PDF and source files, a large demonstration of the source/final practice in academic publishing. Despite imperfect source file handling in current workflows, `sourceFile` could be progressively integrated into platforms such as OJS or Zenodo, among others. This property could find application across millions of resources in the academic publishing ecosystem alone — providing a standard vocabulary for existing practices and a reference point for future infrastructure development.

In open education, the notion of « [Open Source Educational Resources](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14330) » was recently proposed in extension to OER signaling an increasing consideration of source files. In the [UNESCO recommendation on Open Educational Resources](https://www.unesco.org/en/legal-affairs/recommendation-open-educational-resources-oer), they suggest to « develop mechanisms to support and incentivize all stakeholders to publish source files ». OER repositories will probably implement more and more systems for source files management, with again millions of resources potentially concerned by this property.

While these openness movements have historically focused on licences — leading to situations where one has the right to modify without the ability to do so — we will likely witness increasing efforts to handle source files across these infrastructures. With the democratisation of open science and open education adoption of this property may grow exponentially. By making source file availability machine-readable, this property could contribute to fostering collaboration at the heart of the knowledge infrastructure.

## Proposed Property

> **sourceFile:** _Source file(s) from which this creative work is produced._

- **Domain:** CreativeWork
- **Cardinality:** 0..n
- **Expected Values:** MediaObject, URL, SoftwareSourceCode(, SourceCollection ?)

## Examples

For a research article with its zipped LaTeX source:

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "ScholarlyArticle",
  "name": "Developing Open Source Educational Resources for Machine Learning and Data Science",
  "url": "https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.14330",
  "license": "https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/",
  "encodingFormat": "application/pdf",
  "sourceFile": {
    "@type": "MediaObject",
    "contentUrl": "https://arxiv.org/src/2107.14330",
    "encodingFormat": "application/x-tar"
  }
}
```

With my preprint which use markdown, bibtex, latex components archived in Zenodo & produced from Codeberg
```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org/",
  "@type": "ScholarlyArticle",
  "name": "Open Source 2.0: From Open Source Software to Open Source Resources?",
  "url": "https://opensource2.cc/article.pdf",
  "license": "https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/zero/1.0/",
  "encodingFormat": "application/pdf",
  "sourceFile": [
    {
      "@type": "SourceCollection",
      "url": "https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20237079"
    },
    {
      "@type": "SoftwareSourceCode",
      "codeRepository": "https://codeberg.org/Open-Models/Open-Source-2/src/branch/main/articles"
    }
  ]
}
```

## About SourceCollection

When source files consist of multiple files — a Git repository, a Zenodo record, an OER folder — no existing Schema.org type seems to model this precisely. A dedicated `SourceCollection`(/`sourceRepository`) or similar type may be worth considering to complement sourceFile for these cases, wondering how to handle it.

This would act as `codeRepository` for non-code artefacts.

## Limits of Existing Properties

Source files may be (or are already) provided by `isBasedOn` or `associatedMedia`, however neither property captures the specific semantic of the upstream editable file(s) from which the distributed form is produced.

- `isBasedOn`: covers creative derivation or inspiration between distinct works, a broader scope than the technical source/final relationship.
- `associatedMedia`: no role distinction. A source file, a thumbnail, or the distributed resource itself are semantically equivalent, indistinguishable for data consumers.

`sourceFile` would enable data consumers to specifically identify and filter resources that provide upstream editable files — a query currently impossible with existing properties.

This property could become an important component in the description of digital resources and contribute to a more collaborative semantic web.

issues.body:
Remove the term definition `@type` keywords from the `jsonldcontext.jsonld` generation script, delegating all value object type mapping to the data consumer. In summary, this has the following effects.

* Closes [#4384](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/pull/4384) which incorrectly tried to support multiple types via JSON-LD.
* Closes [#4852](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4852) which documents valid `Integer` values of `merchantReturnDays` being incorrectly typed as `Date`.
* Reduce scope of JSON-LD context to IRI term expansion (without the incomplete, incorrect JSON-LD type mapping).
* Avoid downstream consumers needing to patch the context file locally.

Removing the `@type` keywords via local patch is currently required for non-trivial data consumption. Based on @rrlevering's [related comment](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/pull/4384#issuecomment-4007511294), this is Google's internal approach, and it also matches my own investigations about validation methods. As a reminder, JSON-LD can only map value objects to a single datatype (see [spec](https://www.w3.org/TR/json-ld/#value-objects)) which isn't compatible with Schema.org's value ranges.

The primary risk is if consumers were relying on specific properties being a resolved IRI via JSON-LD's `@id` processing. Of course, many properties support `Text` in addition to `URL`, and those have always remained an `xsd:string` requiring consumers to resolve them anyway. That URL-like properties may or may not end up as an IRI is another reason for this change, in my opinion. Similarly, not all `Date` properties end up as `Date`, and, of those, not all correctly as seen in [#4852](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/issues/4852).

I tried to find the original requirements for the `@type` implementation, but the closest I found was in the original [code comment](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/commit/01957026c58c65c20a7eb19f25b234b62afac01b#diff-1ed02c3495a2cbdfb7310b80b4a533d180f77b750ebf1e23a86d0d93e5872178R274) saying `this needs improving; we only started with real types that are subtyped, not Text literals`. To me, that sounds more like it was a prototype that stuck around, but maybe others have more background.

Happy to discuss further, and hopefully others can help provide feedback on this change.

/cc @madbob, @rrlevering, @LuisCCFigueira, @danbri, @wiesmann from linked issues and related commits

<details><summary>JSON-LD Context Commit Notes</summary>

From looking into the history to find more context about the `@type` functionality...

* [2014-06-14](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/commit/01957026c58c65c20a7eb19f25b234b62afac01b) (for v2.2) - JSON-LD context introduced supporting `Date` + `DateTime` datatypes; code comment of `this needs improving; we only started with real types that are subtyped, not Text literals.`; notably this uses a scalar `@type`.
* [2014-06-17](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/commit/d234d261324c33b54be9f55c225079dfee589faf) (for v2.2) - `@id` for `URL` was added to the list.
* [2020-09-10](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/commit/53ac3933b608734c1161caea3b7172f4f42464f4) (for v11.0) - new Python implementation for generating the context, mirroring the existing `@type` conventions. This is where the `Datetime` case typo appears to have been introduced. It also switched to using a local array instead of scalar (although it always outputs a JSON scalar).
* [2024-10-11](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/commit/018f5073af574daf6c3c077ab03affb698941225) (for v28.1) - seems like a proactive refactor and adding tests for the non-valid (and as-of-yet unused) case of outputting an array for `@type`.

</details>

From investigating the definitions and enumerating collisions...
  
```
PREFIX rdf: <http://www.w3.org/1999/02/22-rdf-syntax-ns#>
PREFIX rdfs: <http://www.w3.org/2000/01/rdf-schema#>
PREFIX schema: <http://schema.org/>

SELECT
  ?property 
  (GROUP_CONCAT(STR(?rangeIncludes); separator=", ") AS ?ranges)
WHERE {
  ?property rdf:type rdf:Property .
  ?property schema:rangeIncludes ?rangeIncludes .
  FILTER EXISTS {
    ?property schema:rangeIncludes schema:URL .
  }
  {
    SELECT ?property WHERE {
      ?property rdf:type rdf:Property .
      ?property schema:rangeIncludes ?otherRange .
      ?otherRange rdfs:subClassOf*/rdf:type schema:DataType .
      FILTER NOT EXISTS {
        ?property schema:rangeIncludes schema:Text .
      }
    }
    GROUP BY ?property
    HAVING (COUNT(DISTINCT ?otherRange) > 0)
  }
}
GROUP BY ?property
ORDER BY ?property
```

</details>

issues.title: "asin" on Product seems inconsistent with other schema.org decisions
issues.author: bkimmel
issues.body: Recently "baptismDate" was rejected as an addition to "Person" on the grounds that it is relevant to only one religion (Christianity) and should therefore be referenced in a more generic "lifeEvent". I broadly agree with that as an ontological decision, but it is also deeply inconsistent with allowing a single merchant (Amazon) to have a normalized property like "asin" on a broad category like "Product". Christianity (and the practice/sacrament) of Baptism has existed for millenia and Amazon has been around for a few decades: for the same reason "baptismDate" should go in a "lifeEvent", "asin" should go in a subcategory of Product like "merchantID" or something like that.

issues.title: Correct and expand Italian nonprofit type definitions
issues.author: endelwar
issues.body:
Related issue: #3629

Corrects outdated and inaccurate legal references in the Italian nonprofit type enumeration (`ITNonprofitType`) and adds missing Italian Third Sector categories. All changes are confined to `data/ext/pending/issue-3629.ttl`; only `rdfs:comment` values were changed for existing terms — no identifiers were renamed or removed.

## Corrections

- **ITVolunteerAssociationCharity** (ODV) and **ITSocialPromotionCharity** (APS): now anchored to the Third Sector Code (Legislative Decree 117/2017, Articles 32 ff. and 35 ff.); the superseded Laws 266/1991 and 383/2000 are mentioned as historical sources.
- **ITMutualAidCharity**: Law 3818/1886 kept, coordinated with Articles 42 ff. of Legislative Decree 117/2017.
- **ITSocialCompanyCharity**: fixed "Italian Law 112 of 2017" (it is a Legislative Decree); clarified that the *impresa sociale* status may be acquired by different types of private entities, not only companies.
- **ITCooperativeCharity**: correctly anchored to Law 381/1991 (social cooperatives), with the ex lege social enterprise status under Article 1(4) of Legislative Decree 112/2017.
- **ITSportCompanyCharity** (SSD): updated to Legislative Decrees 36/2021 and 39/2021; distinguished from ASD and from the Third Sector.
- **ITNonprofitType**: comment now frames the Third Sector Code as the main framework, noting exceptions such as amateur sports entities.

## New values (pending)

From Article 4 of Legislative Decree 117/2017: **ITPhilanthropicEntityCharity** (ente filantropico, Articles 37 ff.), **ITAssociativeNetworkCharity** (rete associativa, Article 41), and **ITOtherThirdSectorEntityCharity** (residual value for other RUNTS-registered Third Sector entities).

## Note on misnamed identifiers

Three identifiers are semantically imprecise: `ITSocialCompanyCharity` (an *impresa sociale* is a status open to many private entity types, not a "company" — a better name would be `ITSocialEnterpriseCharity`), `ITCooperativeCharity` (it covers only social cooperatives under Law 381/1991, not Italian cooperatives in general — better: `ITSocialCooperativeCharity`), and `ITSportCompanyCharity` (it omits the qualifying "amateur" element — better: `ITAmateurSportsClubCharity` or similar). This PR deliberately does not rename them, since they were published in v30.0: the corrected semantics live in the comments. However, as these terms are still in the pending section and presumably have little or no adoption yet, this may be the right window for the maintainers to either rename them outright or introduce the corrected names with `supersededBy` on the old ones. Happy to update this PR either way.

## Testing

Turtle syntax validated, full unit test suite and SHACL validation of examples pass. Legal references verified against Normattiva and the Ministry of Labour and Social Policies.

issues.title: Support Recognition of a Link to a Digital Product Passport and High Level Semantic Concepts
issues.author: MichaelLinck
issues.body:
# Motivation
With the upcoming EU Ecodesign for Sustainable Products Regulation (ESPR), manufacturers will be legally required to provide a Digital Product Passport (DPP). This passport contains critical lifecycle, sustainability, and compliance data.

Currently, there is no standardized way for search engines, web crawlers, or semantic consumers to discover a product's DPP link or to parse its high-level regulatory claims (such as EPDs or Substances of Concern) using standard web markup.

# Proposal
We propose a lightweight extension to the :Product and :Certification classes to act as a discovery mechanism for these passports.

In accordance with Schema.org's guiding philosophy (as noted in the global README), this proposal intentionally avoids modeling the massive complexity of the full DPP regulation. Instead, it provides the high-level semantic concepts necessary for discovery, with the explicit expectation that more detailed, domain-specific ontologies (such as the open-source DPP Keystone ontology) will "gap-fill" the granular data structure once the DPP link is followed.

## Proposed Additions

### 1. Core DPP Discovery:
 - **`DigitalProductPassport` (Class):** Represents the passport record itself.
 - **`hasDigitalProductPassport` (Property on `Product`):** Accepts either a `:URL` (e.g., a GS1 Digital Link resolver) or a nested `:DigitalProductPassport` object.

### 2. Key Supply Chain Roles:
 - **`importer` (Property on `Product`):** The organization importing the product into a specific market.
 - **`authorizedRepresentative` (Property on `Product`, `Organization`):** Essential for EU compliance tracking.

### 3. Compliance & Sustainability Certifications:
 - **`EnvironmentalProductDeclaration` (Subclass of `Certification`):** Allows EPDs to be parsed as verifiable claims.
 - **`DeclarationOfConformity` (Subclass of `Certification`):** Represents the formal regulatory compliance document (DoC).

### 4. High-Level Product Metrics:
 - **`recycledContentPercentage` (Property on `Product`)**
 - **`substanceOfConcern` (Property on `Product`):** Accepts `:Text`, `:URL`, or `:ChemicalSubstance` to allow transparent declaration of restricted materials (e.g., REACH/RoHS compliance).
 
## Next Steps
Draft the `.ttl` definitions and a JSON-LD example, to demonstrate how these properties fit together on a single product using a GS1 Digital Link so we can get feedback on the proposed changes.

### Changes Included:
1. **Vocabulary Definitions (`issue-4870.ttl`):**
   * Adds the `DigitalProductPassport` class and `hasDigitalProductPassport` property.
   * Adds the most fundamental supply chain roles in the EU to `Product`: `importer` and `authorizedRepresentative`.
   * Subclasses `Certification` to create `EnvironmentalProductDeclaration` and `DeclarationOfConformity`.

2. **JSON-LD Examples (`issue-4870-examples.txt`):**
   * **Example 1:** Demonstrates a standard e-commerce merchant site linking out to a DPP via a GS1 Digital Link resolver.
   * **Example 2:** Demonstrates the actual Digital Product Passport page itself, fully populated with the new regulatory properties and attached compliance certifications. 

Please see the linked issue for the full motivation and context regarding the upcoming ESPR regulations and our strategy for gap-filling with external ontologies.

issues.title: Proposal: Add common product data properties for retail and marketplaces
issues.author: MichaelLinck
issues.body:
### Motivation
E-commerce ecosystems have evolved significantly over the years, and many advanced product data capabilities have become standard across modern brands, sellers, and marketplaces. However, when trying to represent this rich product data using Schema.org, we often encounter gaps. 

Currently, modeling commonplace concepts—such as grouping technical specifications, flagging mandatory safety warnings, setting minimum order constraints for shipping, or describing increasingly common popularity rankings—often requires workarounds like unstructured text or overusing generic `additionalProperty` key-values.

This proposal seeks to close these gaps, allowing merchants to map their existing structured product data to Schema.org in a way that is standard, explicit, and easily parseable by search engines and e-commerce platforms.

### Proposal
To satisfy these needs without overcomplicating the ontology, we are proposing the smallest possible set of novel concepts. Rather than creating entirely new structures, we have leaned heavily into extending existing types (like `Product`, `Offer`, and `OfferShippingDetails`) and reusing established classes.

The new concepts included in this proposal address:
*   **Structured Specifications:** A cleaner way to group technical product specifications (e.g., grouping "Resolution" and "Sensor Type" under "Camera Specs").
*   **Pricing & Shipping Constraints:** Support for Maximum Retail Price (MRP), as well as minimum order thresholds required to unlock specific shipping rates.
*   **Consumer Safety & Notices:** A structured way to pass mandatory warnings (like Choking Hazards or Prop 65).
*   **Item Relationships & Popularity:** Standardizing the "often bought with" relationship and exposing product popularity/sales rank.

### Proposed Additions

**1. Product Specifications**
*   **`specification`** (Property): Adds to `Product` with range `PropertyValue`. A cleaner alternative to `additionalProperty` for strict retail product specifications.
*   **`valueGroup`** (Property): Adds to `PropertyValue` with range `Text`. Provides a header or section name for grouping related specifications.

**2. Consumer Notices**
*   **`ConsumerNotice`** (Class): A new subclass of `Intangible` representing a consumer notice, such as a safety warning or mandatory information.
*   **`consumerNotice`** (Property): Adds to `Product` with range `ConsumerNotice`, `Text`, `URL`, or `WebContent`. Used to attach the notice to the product.

**3. Product Relationships & Ranking**
*   **`isOftenBoughtWith`** (Property): Adds to `Product` with range `Product`. A sub-property of `isRelatedTo` indicating items frequently purchased together.
*   **`itemPopularity`** (Property): Adds to `Offer` with range `Number` or `QuantitativeValue`. A measure of popularity or sales rank.

**4. Pricing & Shipping**
*   **`MaximumRetailPrice`** (Enumeration Value): A new value for `PriceTypeEnumeration` representing the maximum retail price (MRP) of a product.
*   **`minimumOrderValue`** (Property): Adds to `ShippingRateSettings` with range `PriceSpecification` or `Number`. Represents the minimum order value required for a specific shipping rate to apply.
*   **`provider`** (Property Update): Extends the domain of the existing `provider` property to include `OfferShippingDetails`, allowing explicit definition of the shipping carrier/provider.

issues.title: Broaden the applicability and definition of :dateIssued beyond :Ticket
issues.author: leskneebone
issues.body:
Broaden the applicability and definition of `dateIssued` beyond `Ticket`

The [dateIssued](https://schema.org/dateIssued) property currently has:

> **Definition:** The date the ticket was issued.
> **Used on:** `Ticket`

The property name itself, however, expresses a considerably more general concept: the date on which something was formally issued.

There appear to be useful Schema.org use cases beyond tickets. For example:

* certificates and certifications;
* permits, licences and other formally issued documents;
* datasets, reports and other information resources that have an issuance date distinct from their creation or publication date.

This broader meaning is already familiar from other widely-used metadata vocabularies. For example, Dublin Core Terms defines `dcterms:issued` as the “Date of formal issuance of the resource”.

There is also some evidence of this broader interpretation already arising within Schema.org discussions. For example, #4290 proposes using `dateIssued` for an `OrganicCertification`, even though `Certification`/`CreativeWork`/`Thing` are not currently included in the property's documented applicability.

I appreciate that `schema:domainIncludes` is intentionally advisory rather than an RDFS domain constraint, so data using `dateIssued` outside `Ticket` is not necessarily invalid. However, the current definition and `domainIncludes` make such usage appear unintended, and can discourage reuse of what is otherwise a very naturally named property.

Would it make sense to generalise the definition, perhaps along the lines of:

> **The date on which the item was issued.**

and broaden `domainIncludes` accordingly?

One possibility would be to include a relatively general type such as `CreativeWork`, together with more specific issued-object types where appropriate. Another would be to consider whether `Thing` is justified given the range of things that can formally be issued.

I would be interested in views on the intended distinction between `dateIssued`, `datePublished`, and `dateCreated`. In information-resource metadata these commonly represent distinct lifecycle events, and retaining that distinction seems useful.
