issues.title: Proposal: ExchangeTradedFund subtype of InvestmentFund
issues.author: samwant
issues.body:
Follow-up to discussion [#3416](https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/discussions/3416) (Dec 2023), reframed as a concrete, additive proposal now that `InvestmentFund` exists in Pending.

## Summary

Exchange Traded Funds are one of the fastest-growing investment products globally, and fund issuers, exchanges, and data providers already publish rich, structured ETF data on the open web. Since [`InvestmentFund`](https://schema.org/InvestmentFund) was added to Pending, the general fund concept is covered — but the characteristics that define an ETF specifically have no schema.org representation.

This proposal is deliberately split into two parts so the uncontroversial half can proceed independently:

- **Part 1 (primary ask)** — one new type and five descriptive properties. All are stable characteristics that do not change over time.
- **Part 2 (secondary ask)** — three periodically-updated figures, proposed with explicit dating requirements. Raised separately because schema.org has reasonably been cautious about market-adjacent data.

Everything proposed is purely additive. No existing term definitions or supertypes are modified, so this is compatible with the Pending staging mechanism.

## Why structured markup improves accuracy here

It's worth addressing the obvious objection up front, because it motivates the design of Part 2.

Fund figures are already being extracted from the web at scale — by search engines, finance aggregators, and AI assistants — today, without this vocabulary. That extraction currently happens by scraping rendered issuer pages or third-party aggregators, typically stripped of any "as at" qualification and with no indication of whether the issuer is the source.

Structured markup does not make these figures staler. Markup is generated server-side from the same data source that renders the visible figure, so it is exactly as fresh as the page carrying it, and any crawl-to-display lag is identical to the lag on a scraped value. What markup adds is issuer authority and an explicit, machine-readable date. The proposal below therefore treats dating not as a nicety but as part of the term definitions.

---

## Part 1 — Type and stable properties (primary ask)

### Proposed type

**`ExchangeTradedFund`** — *An investment fund whose units are traded on a securities exchange throughout the trading day, much like shares. Most ETFs track an index. Subtype of `InvestmentFund`.*

The definition aligns with the Financial Industry Business Ontology, which schema.org's existing financial vocabulary drew on: [`fibo-sec-fund:ExchangeTradedFund`](https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/SEC/Funds/Funds/ExchangeTradedFund) — "investment fund whose fund units are traded on an exchange, much like stocks."

### Proposed properties

| Property | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `underlyingIndex` | `Text`, `URL` | The index the fund seeks to track (e.g. "S&P/ASX 200", "Solactive Australia 200 Index"). |
| `assetClass` | `Text` | The asset class of the underlying holdings (e.g. equities, fixed income, commodities, diversified). |
| `investmentObjective` | `Text` | The stated objective of the fund from the investor's perspective (e.g. "income", "capital growth", "income and capital growth"). Fixed income and equity funds generally serve materially different investor purposes, and this is disclosed in every product disclosure document. |
| `dividendFrequency` | `Text` | The schedule of income distributions to unitholders (e.g. monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual). |
| `fundDomicile` | `Country` | The country in which the fund is legally established and regulated. Distinct from the exchange(s) on which its units trade — see below. |

These five are fixed characteristics of a fund. They are set at launch, change rarely if ever, and carry no staleness or currency concerns.

Management fees are deliberately **not** proposed as a new property: the existing [`feesAndCommissionsSpecification`](https://schema.org/feesAndCommissionsSpecification), inherited from `FinancialProduct`, already covers fee disclosure. This keeps the proposal minimal.

### Domain extension

Add `ExchangeTradedFund` to `domainIncludes` of the existing [`tickerSymbol`](https://schema.org/tickerSymbol) property, which is currently scoped to `Corporation`. This is the only change to an existing term and it is additive.

### Why `fundDomicile` matters

An ETF's domicile and its listing venue are independent facts, and the difference is material to investors. On the Australian Securities Exchange, Vanguard's VAS (Australian-domiciled) and VTS (US-domiciled, cross-listed) sit side by side; the US-domiciled fund carries different tax treatment and different regulatory disclosures. The same pattern occurs across Europe, where UCITS funds domiciled in Ireland or Luxembourg are listed in London, Frankfurt, and Milan.

Publishers already disclose domicile prominently for exactly this reason, yet no existing schema.org property expresses it. [`areaServed`](https://schema.org/areaServed) describes where a service is offered, not where a fund is established; conflating the two would mislead.

Listing venue itself is expressible today by pairing the extended `tickerSymbol` with the exchange's identifier or MIC in publisher markup, so no new "exchange" property is requested.

---

## Part 2 — Periodically-updated figures (secondary ask)

These three properties carry figures that issuers republish on a regular cycle, dated "as at" a stated period end. They are raised separately so that Part 1 can proceed on its own if reviewers prefer to take these more slowly.

| Property | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `netAssets` | `MonetaryAmount` | The net assets of the fund, as published by the issuer. |
| `distributionYield` | `QuantitativeValue` | The fund's distribution yield — annual income distributions as a percentage of unit price, as published by the issuer. |
| `annualisedReturn` | `QuantitativeValue` | The fund's annualised total return over a stated period. Repeatable: one value per period, with the period named in the value (e.g. `name`: "5 years", "since inception"). |

### These are not live market data

To be explicit, since this is the likely concern: none of these are real-time or price-like. Issuers publish them on a monthly cycle on fund pages and factsheets, dated to a stated month-end. The proposal mirrors that existing publication practice rather than introducing a live-data expectation into the vocabulary.

### Precedent for moving figures in schema.org

Schema.org already carries figures that change, and handles them by pairing the value with explicit validity:

- [`Offer.price`](https://schema.org/price) changes constantly and is paired with [`priceValidUntil`](https://schema.org/priceValidUntil) — "the date after which the price is no longer available."
- [`ExchangeRateSpecification`](https://schema.org/ExchangeRateSpecification) and its `currentExchangeRate` property cover FX rates, which move far faster than any figure proposed here, and sit in the same "new" area as `InvestmentFund`.

The proposal follows that established pattern.

### Dating should be part of the definition

Given the above, these three properties should not be usable undated. Suggested approach, modeled directly on `priceValidUntil`:

- Add a dedicated date property on `ExchangeTradedFund` — working name **`figuresAsAt`** (range `Date`) — giving the effective date of the fund's published figures, with the term definitions for the three properties above stating that it should accompany them.

**Open modeling question for reviewers.** An alternative would be to reuse existing dating properties on the values themselves. That works for `netAssets`: [`validFrom`](https://schema.org/validFrom) and `validThrough` already include `MonetaryAmount` in `domainIncludes`. It does **not** currently work for the other two, because neither property includes `QuantitativeValue` in its domain. So the alternative would require adding `QuantitativeValue` to the domain of `validFrom`/`validThrough` — also additive, but a change to existing terms rather than a purely new one. I'm happy to go whichever way reviewers prefer; flagging it because it affects which mechanism is cleanest.

### Regulatory context motivating mandatory dating

In several jurisdictions, published fund performance and yield figures are treated as regulated promotional material rather than neutral data, which is a further argument for dating being structural rather than advisory.

In Australia, ASIC conducted surveillance of managed fund marketing in 2022 ([22-249MR](https://www.asic.gov.au/about-asic/news-centre/find-a-media-release/2022-releases/22-249mr-managed-funds-amend-their-marketing-following-asic-surveillance/), [22-330MR](https://www.asic.gov.au/about-asic/news-centre/find-a-media-release/2022-releases/22-330mr-managed-funds-to-improve-marketing-oversight-following-asic-surveillance/)) and the resulting remediation included requiring digital advertising to be tested before release and digital displays to match approved versions. Structured data is part of that digital surface — it is what gets lifted into a search result or an assistant's answer. Equivalent regimes govern performance advertising elsewhere, including past-performance warning requirements.

The practical consequence for this vocabulary: an undated performance or yield value in markup is a worse outcome for issuers and consumers than no markup at all, whereas a dated, issuer-authoritative value is better than the scraped status quo. Building the date into the definitions is what makes adoption safe for publishers who are subject to these regimes — and publisher-safe terms are terms that actually get adopted.

---

## Evidence of real-world publication

This data is already published, consistently and at scale, by issuers and exchanges worldwide — the proposal maps vocabulary onto existing web content rather than inventing it:

- **Betashares** (AU): every fund page lists index tracked, management cost, distribution frequency, fund size — e.g. https://www.betashares.com.au/fund/australia-200-etf/
- **Vanguard Australia**: e.g. https://www.vanguard.com.au/personal/invest-with-us/etf?portId=8205 (VAS)
- **ASX**: ETP directory with issuer, benchmark, and listing data — https://www.asx.com.au/markets/trade-our-cash-market/asx-investment-products-directory/etps
- **iShares / BlackRock** (global): e.g. https://www.ishares.com/us/products/239726/
- **justETF** (EU): comparison pages exposing domicile, replication, TER, and distribution policy — https://www.justetf.com/

## Example markup

### Part 1 only — stable characteristics

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "ExchangeTradedFund",
  "name": "Betashares Australia 200 ETF",
  "tickerSymbol": "A200",
  "url": "https://www.betashares.com.au/fund/australia-200-etf/",
  "provider": {
    "@type": "Organization",
    "name": "Betashares Capital Ltd"
  },
  "underlyingIndex": "Solactive Australia 200 Index",
  "assetClass": "Australian equities",
  "investmentObjective": "Income and capital growth",
  "dividendFrequency": "Quarterly",
  "fundDomicile": {
    "@type": "Country",
    "name": "Australia"
  },
  "feesAndCommissionsSpecification": "Management fee 0.04% p.a."
}
```

### With Part 2 — dated figures

Figures below are illustrative, to show structure. The point of the example is the dating mechanism, not the values.

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "ExchangeTradedFund",
  "name": "Betashares Australia 200 ETF",
  "tickerSymbol": "A200",
  "figuresAsAt": "2026-07-31",
  "netAssets": {
    "@type": "MonetaryAmount",
    "currency": "AUD",
    "value": "5000000000",
    "validFrom": "2026-07-31"
  },
  "distributionYield": {
    "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
    "value": "3.2",
    "unitText": "% p.a."
  },
  "annualisedReturn": [
    {
      "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
      "name": "1 year",
      "value": "10.0",
      "unitText": "% p.a."
    },
    {
      "@type": "QuantitativeValue",
      "name": "5 years",
      "value": "8.0",
      "unitText": "% p.a."
    }
  ]
}
```

### Cross-listed fund — why domicile and listing are separate facts

```json
{
  "@context": "https://schema.org",
  "@type": "ExchangeTradedFund",
  "name": "Vanguard US Total Market Shares Index ETF",
  "tickerSymbol": "VTS",
  "underlyingIndex": "CRSP US Total Market Index",
  "assetClass": "US equities",
  "fundDomicile": {
    "@type": "Country",
    "name": "United States"
  }
}
```

## Consumers and adoption path

Search engines and assistants already surface fund data in finance experiences; structured markup gives them issuer-authoritative, dated figures rather than scraped ones. Issuer marketing and product teams have direct incentive to adopt, since it improves the accuracy of how their funds are represented, and the properties map one-to-one onto data their pages already render.

On implementation feedback specifically: Pending exists to gather exactly that, and I'm well placed to help source it. In my own capacity I can pressure-test these terms against how an issuer actually publishes and approves this data — including the compliance review that performance and yield figures attract — and feed that back here. I'm not in a position to commit any organisation to deployment, but I'd expect real adoption interest from issuers if these terms reach Pending in a form that carries dating properly, and I'm happy to help make that case.

I'm also happy to prepare a pull request adding these terms to the Pending area if there's support for the direction, and to adjust naming or scoping per feedback — including taking Part 1 alone if that's the preference, renaming `ExchangeTradedFund` to `ETF`, or folding properties up to `InvestmentFund` where reviewers think they generalise.

## References

- FIBO `ExchangeTradedFund`: https://spec.edmcouncil.org/fibo/ontology/SEC/Funds/Funds/ExchangeTradedFund
- Existing pending type: https://schema.org/InvestmentFund
- Precedent for dated moving figures: https://schema.org/priceValidUntil, https://schema.org/ExchangeRateSpecification
- Original discussion: https://github.com/schemaorg/schemaorg/discussions/3416

issues.title: providerMobility: is it a live status or a standing characteristic of the service?
issues.author: Notts90
issues.body:
Follows on from #817.

## Ambiguity

It is unclear whether `providerMobility` describes:

- a live status, such as whether a taxi is currently moving vs stationary; or
- a characteristic of the service, such as whether the provider travels to the customer.

The only example suggests the first interpretation:

> "Car for hire driver 123 is within 50 meters of a given location, but is moving."

This describes a moment in time and uses a `GeoCircle` with a 50 metre radius. Under this interpretation, `dynamic` means the provider is currently moving and could change to `static` when the car stops.

However, #817 introduced the property in the context of increasingly mobile and virtual businesses, suggesting a more permanent characteristic of how the service is delivered.

## Missing case

Neither interpretation clearly covers services delivered at the customer's location by a provider who travels there, but is not providing the service while in transit. Examples include mobile hairdressers, plumbers, electricians and mobile mechanics. In my case, this includes on-site inspection and engineering services.

Some SEO sites already suggest using `dynamic` for these services, for example: https://onlineownership.com/local-business-schema-markup-tips-examples/

## Adoption

`providerMobility` is listed as `1K–10K` usage vs `Service` at `1M – 10M` in the 2026_05, 2026_06 and 2026_07 Schema.org public statistics.

## Proposal

Clarify that `providerMobility` describes a characteristic of how the service is delivered, and add a third value:

| Value | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `static` | Service delivered at the provider's premises. |
| `mobile` | Provider travels to the customer's location to deliver the service. |
| `dynamic` | Service delivered while the provider is in transit or its location changes in real time. |

If adding `mobile` as a value is undesirable, the minimum improvement would be to clarify which existing value covers the travelling-provider case and whether `providerMobility` is intended as a live status or a standing characteristic.

Existing uses of `dynamic` may already include the travelling-provider interpretation, so documenting the distinction would help prevent further ambiguity.

issues.title: Proposal: Add MedicalFood type (distinct from DietarySupplement and Drug)
issues.author: aplustrading24-png
issues.body:
### Summary

schema.org currently has no type representing "medical food," a legally distinct US and international regulatory category. Products in this category are being forced into `DietarySupplement` or `Product`-only markup, both of which under- or mis-represent their regulatory status. This proposal requests a new `MedicalFood` type as a subtype of `Product` and `MedicalEntity`.

### Why this is needed

"Medical food" is a defined legal term under US law — [21 U.S.C. §360ee(b)(3)](https://www.law.cornell.edu/uscode/text/21/360ee) (Orphan Drug Act §5(b)) and 21 CFR 101.9(j)(8) — describing a food formulated for enteral consumption under physician supervision for the specific dietary management of a disease or condition with distinctive nutritional requirements. FDA maintains dedicated guidance on this category ([FDA Medical Foods guidance](https://www.fda.gov/food/guidance-documents-regulatory-information-topic-food-and-dietary-supplements/medical-foods-guidance-documents-regulatory-information); [FDA FAQs About Medical Foods, 3rd ed.](https://www.fda.gov/media/97726/download)).

Internationally, the equivalent category is recognized as "Foods for Special Medical Purposes" (FSMP) under [Codex CXS 180-1991](https://www.fao.org/fao-who-codexalimentarius/sh-proxy/ar/?lnk=1&url=https%253A%252F%252Fworkspace.fao.org%252Fsites%252Fcodex%252FStandards%252FCXS+180-1991%252FCXS_180e.pdf).

Currently, publishers of medical foods have no correct schema.org type:
- `Drug` is incorrect — medical foods are not drugs and are not subject to premarket drug approval.
- `DietarySupplement` is incorrect — schema.org defines it as "a product taken by mouth that contains a dietary ingredient intended to supplement the diet" ([schema.org/DietarySupplement](https://schema.org/DietarySupplement)), which is a different legal and regulatory category from medical food and creates a factually inaccurate classification.
- Bare `Product` carries no medical/regulatory semantics at all.

This gap has real commercial consequences: without a distinguishing type, medical foods are commonly bucketed with "Vitamins & Supplements" in downstream commerce systems, which can subject a lawfully marketed medical food to enforcement policies intended for unapproved supplements/drugs (see [Google Merchant Center Healthcare & medicines policy](https://support.google.com/merchants/answer/6150151?hl=en)).

### Proposed type definition

```
MedicalFood
  - Subtype of: Product, MedicalEntity
  - Description: A food formulated to be consumed or administered enterally under
    the supervision of a physician, intended for the specific dietary management
    of a disease or condition for which distinctive nutritional requirements,
    based on recognized scientific principles, are established by medical evaluation.
```

**Proposed properties:**

| Property | Expected type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `intendedDiseaseOrCondition` | `MedicalCondition` | The disease or condition for which the product is intended for dietary management |
| `requiresMedicalSupervision` | `Boolean` | Whether use of the product requires ongoing supervision by a physician (true by regulatory definition for this type) |
| `regulatoryClassification` | `Text` or `URL` | Citation to the governing regulatory definition (e.g. "21 U.S.C. §360ee(b)(3)" or a link to Codex CXS 180-1991) |
| `nutritionalRequirementBasis` | `Text` | Brief statement of the distinctive nutritional requirement basis for the classification |

### Prior art / related types

- `DietarySupplement` (https://schema.org/DietarySupplement) — closest existing sibling type; this proposal is modeled on its structure but corrects the legal-category mismatch.
- `Drug` (https://schema.org/Drug) — sibling type for pharmaceutical products.
- `MedicalCondition`, `MedicalWebPage`, `MedicalEntity` — existing medical vocabulary this type would integrate with.

### Requesting party

Quantum LifeSciences Inc. (Pomona, CA, USA) — manufacturer/distributor of medical foods for the dietary management of chronic kidney disease (nephlong.com).

### Note on process

We understand schema.org proposals are strongest when supported by multiple implementers and real-world usage evidence, not a single company's request. We are seeking co-signers/supporting comments from other medical-food manufacturers and relevant trade associations before or alongside this filing.

issues.title: [Open source 2.0] Add property sourceFile to CreativeWork (pending)
issues.author: AbcSxyZ
issues.body:
*Following issue #4851*

## Proposal

| Property | Domain | Range | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `sourceFile` | [`CreativeWork`](https://schema.org/CreativeWork) | [`URL`](https://schema.org/URL) | Source file(s) from which this work is produced. |

## Description

Source files enable access to the editable components of various types of resources, such as [`ScholarlyArticle`](https://schema.org/ScholarlyArticle),  [`LearningResource`](https://schema.org/LearningResource),  [`ImageObject`](https://schema.org/ImageObject),  [`AudioObject`](https://schema.org/AudioObject),  [`VideoObject`](https://schema.org/VideoObject),  [`3DModel`](https://schema.org/3DModel),  [`SoftwareApplication`](https://schema.org/SoftwareApplication), etc.

`sourceFile` may point to a repository, an archive, or individual file(s) depending on the resource.

## Motivation

Similar to software and source code, different kinds of digital resources have an editable/distribution pattern, and source files are a commonly used terminology to refer to these editable elements.

To complement the [`license`](https://schema.org/license) property — which indicates the right to modify — `sourceFile` enables access to the most appropriate form for modification.

#### Source/distribution files examples

| Domain | Source file | Distribution format |
|--------|-------------|---------------------|
| Documents | .md, .tex, .odt | .pdf |
| Images | .svg, .psd | .png, .jpg |
| Fonts | .glyphs, .ufo | .ttf, .otf, .woff |
| Hardware | .fcstd, .kicad | .stl, .gerber |
| Software | .c, .go, .py | executable |
| Music | .mid, .aup | .mp3 |

This property could play an important role with open practices (open science, open education, open hardware...) where source file availability is increasingly considered alongside open licensing. This proposal is part of a broader citizen research « [Open Source 2.0: From Open Source Software to Open Source Resources?](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.20237079) », arguing around the availability of these source files.

A deliberately simple basis to be discussed, experimented and improved.
